units.testAssessment: Four strong database cases cover multiple binding layers, metadata-only listing, plaintext non-leak assertions, success audit, fail-closed redaction, concurrency deduplication and three restricted caller classes. units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Secret delivery that is tenant-, Work-, Connector-, purpose- and data-policy-bound, keeps values out of the control-plane domain where possible and leaves a complete custody/access record.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT binding resolution, metadata/value separation, no-store, redaction-before-delivery, failure closure, run snapshot manifest and low-trust denial. Prefer execution-node injection or short-lived broker leases over plaintext control-plane API responses; bind every access to WorkExecution, ResponsibilityContract, purpose and export policy, use provider/version references, expiry and least-use scope, and audit allowed plus denied attempts without revealing Secret existence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A successful fetch is linked to Agent/run but not to an accountable human, exact permission/data contract or approval. Plaintext crosses the HTTP/control-plane boundary. units.function: Embedded-Postgres AgentService tests for transactional SecretRef binding synchronization across create/update/pending activation, plaintext Adapter-key conversion and allowlisted static-lease metadata.

Invalid references roll back create/update and failed activation stays pending.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Secret custody and projection contracts that cannot diverge from approved Agent/Connector configuration and that roll back atomically on invalid or unavailable authority.

units.function: HTTP integration tests for the custom API JSON compression middleware, including content negotiation, cache validators, streamed/download responses and Better Auth's writeHead plus Uint8Array response bridge.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes emit responses through an API-scoped middleware that temporarily wraps ServerResponse write/end/flushHeaders, buffers eligible JSON and asynchronously applies node:zlib gzip or deflate before restoring the original methods.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP Accept-Encoding quality preferences, Content-Type/Encoding/Disposition/Range/Cache-Control, ETag and Content-MD5 validators, status/body eligibility, Buffer and Uint8Array chunks, write/end callbacks.

The middleware buffers JSON writes unless headers, streaming semantics or response metadata require passthrough; bodies below 1 KiB remain unchanged, eligible large bodies are compressed and validators adjusted, while compression failure falls back to the original bytes.
units.testAssessment: Ten real-socket tests strongly cover hot-list compression, both encodings, small/already-encoded/streamed/attachment responses, ETag weakening and the Better Auth Uint8Array regression. Missing are malformed and duplicate q-values, q=0 versus wildcard precedence, HEAD/204/304/errors, Cache-Control no-transform, flushHeaders, callback/backpressure ordering, client aborts, compression failure, Content-MD5 removal and a maximum buffered-body or concurrency memory bound.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will return large task, evidence and office projections and needs transport efficiency that preserves identity cookies, evidence bytes, streaming and cache correctness under self-hosted and managed profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the regression corpus and protocol guards, but prefer a maintained platform/proxy compression facility or a bounded implementation. Add Brotli where supported, hard buffer/concurrency limits, abort handling and metrics; never transform evidence downloads or signed/digested payloads unless the stored and transported representations are explicit.
units.responsibilityConflict: Compression is not a responsibility model, but silent byte transformation can invalidate evidence digests or obscure which representation was approved. The middleware buffers eligible JSON without an upper bound, creating a control-plane availability risk that is not exercised by the tests.

units.function: HTTP route tests for approval decision idempotency, tenant non-disclosure, authenticated-human attribution, Agent-created issue-linked board requests and low-trust recovery-run containment.
units.dependencyDirection: Session or API-key actor middleware supplies trusted human/Agent identity; approval routes scope records to the actor's Company, call Approval/IssueApproval/Heartbeat/Secret/Access services, then emit activity and wakeup side effects only when a decision was newly applied.
units.keyDataModels: Board or Agent actor, Company scope, Approval type/status/payload/decision note/requester/decider, linked Issue ids, heartbeat run contextSnapshot and status-only recovery capability flags.
units.lifecycle: Approve/reject retries return the resolved record without repeating logs, issue lookup or wakeups. Cross-Company decision and revision attempts return indistinguishable 404. Human identity comes from the authenticated actor rather than request fields. Normal Agents may open generic board requests linked to Issues, while cheap status-only recovery runs cannot create, resubmit or comment on approvals.
units.testAssessment: Eleven route-level cases cover duplicate side-effect suppression, cross-tenant non-disclosure, forged decider rejection, generic Agent requests and three recovery-run mutation paths. Missing are requester/approver separation, role/risk policy, exact action and payload digest binding, evidence/result/permission/data-contract references, concurrent requests, Idempotency-Key, revision versioning, comment/list/read containment, expired/cancelled approvals, structured error codes and real database/service integration rather than permissive mocks.
units.designRationale: Keep retries safe, derive attribution from trusted authentication context, avoid tenant existence oracles, let Agents escalate decisions to humans and prevent degraded watchdog runs from changing governance state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Agent-initiated escalation and human decisions that are tenant-safe and retryable while proving the exact proposed action, authority, data, evidence and accountable human through revision and execution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT actor-derived attribution, 404 non-disclosure, explicit low-trust capability denial and issue/work linkage. Replace generic title payloads with a versioned ApprovalRequest binding canonical action digest, Work, ResponsibilityContract, Agent, permission/data grants, evidence and expiry; require policy-selected accountable human and structured stable errors.
units.responsibilityConflict: An Agent can create a generic board approval whose fixture binds only a title and optional Issue ids, not an executable action or responsibility contract. Human decision tests prove identity attribution but not authority, independence, what the reviewer saw, or whether later side effects match the approved bytes.

units.function: ApprovalService unit tests for compare-and-set decision idempotency, hire-Agent activation/creation side effects and lookup of an Agent's open hire approval.
units.dependencyDirection: ApprovalService reads and conditionally updates Approval rows, then invokes AgentService activation/create/terminate and an external hire-approved notification hook; a SQL-filtered query finds open hire approvals by Company, type, status and payload Agent id.
units.keyDataModels: Hire Approval company/type/status/payload/requesting Agent, decision user/note/time, optional pending Agent id, Adapter config SecretRef, applied boolean and post-decision Agent/notification side effects.
units.lifecycle: A pending approval is conditionally resolved. If another worker wins, the service rereads the final row and returns applied=false without repeating Agent or notification effects. A winning approval activates the pending Agent or creates one from payload and notifies the requester; rejection terminates the pending Agent. Open-hire lookup delegates all predicates to SQL.
units.testAssessment: Six focused service tests demonstrate the compare-and-set winner/loser contract, winning side effects, Agent creation from SecretRef payload and filtered lookup. The database and downstream services are stubs, so they do not cover transaction isolation, crashes between status update and side effects, side-effect failure/retry, outbox durability, duplicate external notification, concurrent payload mutation, approval digest, create/activate rollback, requester/approver policy or JSON predicate/index behavior.
units.designRationale: Prevent concurrent or retried decisions from activating, terminating or notifying twice while supporting both pre-created pending Agents and deferred creation from an approved payload.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must resolve approvals exactly once at the decision ledger while guaranteeing eventual, idempotent execution of every approved side effect and preserving proof that execution used the approved revision.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the boundary around an immutable decision plus transactional outbox/work command. Keep conditional state transition and explicit applied result, but persist a canonical action digest and durable side-effect intents in the same transaction; consumers use idempotency keys, retry independently, record execution receipts and compensate or escalate permanent failure.
units.responsibilityConflict: The current no-op retry rule creates a crash gap: if the database becomes approved and Agent activation or notification fails, later retries see applied=false and deliberately skip those side effects. Approval payload JSON is mutable authority without an immutable digest, and the tests do not prove that the exact reviewed configuration is what an external runtime receives.

units.function: HTTP upload tests for general Company assets and Company logos, including storage metadata, attachment limits, image-type rejection and SVG sanitization before persistence.
units.dependencyDirection: Multipart board requests enter asset routes; route validation/sanitization writes bytes through StorageService, persists metadata through AssetService and returns an opaque content endpoint path, with activity logging mocked at the boundary.
units.keyDataModels: Company id, namespace, original filename, content type, byte body/size, SHA-256, storage provider/object key, Asset creator/time metadata, content path and sanitized SVG DOM.

General assets admit configured non-image attachments; logos require supported images, use the general size ceiling and sanitize SVG scripts, event handlers and external links before storage. units.companyOsFit: ADAPT opaque asset ids/content paths, content hash metadata, pre-storage SVG sanitization and size tests. units.responsibilityConflict: The tests prove byte filtering but not who had authority to attach the artifact, whether the stored hash matches original or sanitized representation, or which Work/evidence contract owns it. units.function: Pure tests for configurable attachment MIME allowlists, wildcard matching, content-type normalization, Office-type inference from filenames and the set of content types eligible for inline browser rendering.
units.dependencyDirection: Operator configuration and upload metadata enter normalization/matching helpers; routes use their result to admit uploads and choose inline versus download behavior, independent of storage or domain services.
units.keyDataModels: MIME type/pattern, wildcard, default allowlist, original filename/extension, octet-stream fallback, inferred Office MIME type and inline-safe content-type set.
units.lifecycle: Missing allowlist configuration falls back to images plus common Office types. Matching is case-insensitive and supports type or suffix wildcards and a global *. Generic binary uploads may be relabeled as Office documents from filename extension when the inferred type is allowed. PNG/SVG/PDF/plain text/MP4 are classified inline; HTML and ZIP are not.
units.testAssessment: Twenty-one concise cases cover parsing, normalization, wildcard behavior, legacy/current Office extensions, generic binary inference and inline classification. Missing are MIME parameters, malformed patterns, Unicode/double extensions, magic-byte or archive inspection, macro-enabled Office types, polyglots, decompression bombs, executable content, SVG/PDF active-content behavior, browser nosniff/CSP/sandbox/Content-Disposition and the danger of the global allow-all wildcard.
units.designRationale: Accept useful office and media attachments across inconsistent clients while retaining configurable admission and preventing obviously active or binary types from inline rendering.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS evidence and enterprise-data uploads are untrusted inputs whose admission, rendering, model ingestion and export must be governed separately and preserve the original bytes and declared/detected representations.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT normalization and table-driven parsing only. Do not treat client MIME or filename inference as trust; record declared, detected and normalized types, hash original bytes, quarantine and scan asynchronously, validate archives, enforce per-purpose policy and serve active formats from an isolated origin with nosniff, sandbox and attachment disposition. Disallow unrestricted * in managed production profiles.
units.responsibilityConflict: A filename can cause generic bytes to be relabeled as an Office document and several active-capable formats are called inline-safe without proving delivery controls. That weakens evidence integrity and can expose accountable reviewers when opening Agent-supplied artifacts.

units.function: Extensive embedded-Postgres and HTTP suite for a human-only decision-attention projection that merges approvals, interactions, join requests, recovery actions, productivity reviews, blockers, reviews, exhausted runs, budget incidents, Agent errors and first-class decisions into ranked, deduplicated, queueable and dismissible work.
units.dependencyDirection: AttentionService reads many operational/domain tables and user-specific dismissal/triage/queue state, constructs a common projection with source details and decision actions, ranks/filters/pages it, and exposes it through board-only routes; it does not own the underlying approval, run, Issue or Agent lifecycle.
units.keyDataModels: Attention source kind/id/dedup/dismissal key, subject/project/workspace/detail, whyNow/entryRule/exitRule/decisionVerbs/rank, approval/interaction/review/blocker/run/budget/Agent status, unblock owner/transition, queue membership/retention, user dismissal/snooze, decideBy/attribution, cursor/snapshot/counts/shelf and decision origin/expiry.
units.lifecycle: Only active human-action sources enter; internal harness, Agent-addressed active work, transient/recovered failures and revision-requested approvals are suppressed. Paused/terminated Agent addressees return work to the board. Newer successful runs remove old failure alerts. Pending interactions are enriched with project, plan, images and action-specific detail; only the newest same-Issue/same-kind confirmation shows. Dismissals are invalidated by newer source activity, snoozes reappear after expiry, blockers collapse into cycle-safe weighted terminal causes, and queues/triage/retention/ranking produce paged or complete snapshots.
units.testAssessment: Twenty-four high-value scenarios exercise ten source families, real joins and ranking, human/Agent routing, recovery suppression, enrichment, dedup, graph cycles, snooze/dismissal invalidation, queue snapshots over 100 rows, paging/filter validation, UTC-week ordering, board-only HTTP access and uniform aging. This is a strong behavioral reference. Missing are query plans/load tests across large tenants, snapshot consistency under concurrent updates, authorization by responsible human/department/project, risk/non-dismissible escalation policy, stable cursor mutation semantics, timezone/locale choices, per-source exhaustive state matrices, information redaction, immutable decision evidence and E2E proof that projected verbs execute the exact displayed revision.
units.designRationale: Reduce board overload by presenting only decisions that currently require a human, explain why each item entered and how it exits, collapse duplicate operational signals, rank by urgency/impact and retain user-controlled queues and triage without changing source-of-truth workflows.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss is a Company OS differentiator: one accountable human needs a trustworthy action queue across several Agents, approvals, data risks, evidence, failures and organizational dependencies, with no important responsibility silently hidden.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT this as the leading reference for an AttentionProjection read model: common source envelope, explicit entry/exit/why-now/action verbs, cycle-safe blocker impact, recovered-failure suppression, source-version-aware dismissal and paged snapshots. Rebuild from Company OS events/projections, partition by accountable human/position/data contract, attach risk/SLA/evidence/action digest, make high-risk items non-dismissible or escalation-bound, and verify every verb against the displayed source revision.
units.responsibilityConflict: The feed is Company-wide for any admitted board user rather than routed by accountable role. Agent-attributed triage can snooze human decisions; complete snapshots deliberately bypass safety limits; same-Issue/same-kind logic hides older still-pending confirmations; and generic dismiss/snooze can suppress approvals without a risk policy. Projection details do not bind the responsible human, exact permission/data grants or immutable evidence revision.

units.function: Actor-middleware integration tests for authenticated sessions and a Paperclip Cloud tenant-header bootstrap path that provisions users, Companies, memberships and defaults, repairs legacy Company names and removes stale instance-admin elevation.
units.dependencyDirection: Either the configured session resolver or a shared Cloud tenant server token plus identity headers enters actorMiddleware; middleware reads/writes auth users, Companies, memberships, permission defaults, instance settings/roles and activity log before publishing a board actor consumed by route authorization.
units.keyDataModels: Session/user profile, cloud tenant token, global user id/email/name, stack id/role, external Paperclip Company id/name, generated internal Company id, active membership, principal permission grants, instance role, Company rename activity and actor source.
units.lifecycle: Normal sessions preserve persisted human profile and load memberships/admin state. A matching tenant token causes header claims to be trusted, marks email verified, idempotently seeds identity/Company/membership/default grants/settings and emits a non-admin cloud_tenant actor. Real membership rows extend access to imported Companies. Trusted human names repair known machine-generated Company names with an audit event. A tenant-header request deletes a legacy instance_admin row so later session requests stop elevating that user.
units.testAssessment: Six substantial route/integration scenarios cover session projection, JIT tenant bootstrap, imported-Company membership access, legacy-name migration with activity evidence, stale-admin cleanup and naming heuristics. Database behavior is still heavily stubbed. Missing are invalid/missing/rotated token cases, constant-time comparison, signed issuer/audience/expiry/nonce and replay, header stripping by proxies, role allowlist validation, cross-stack identity collisions, concurrent bootstrap, transaction rollback, deprovisioning/suspension, membership downgrade, email ownership, failure before stale-admin purge and proof that a session cannot elevate during the migration window.
units.designRationale: Let a managed Cloud front door inject tenant/user context into a self-contained Paperclip instance, bootstrap resources without a separate onboarding flow, preserve access to imported Companies and clean up authorization artifacts from older deployments.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS managed-cloud and self-hosted profiles need replaceable enterprise identity federation, JIT provisioning and migration without equating an upstream account with all Company permissions or letting migration order temporarily expand authority.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind IdentityPort and OrganizationPrincipalPort using OIDC/SAML or short-lived signed workload assertions with issuer, audience, tenant, subject, expiry, nonce and key rotation. Map external identity to opaque internal Principal, validate roles against policy, transact JIT provisioning and audit receipts, process deprovisioning, and run privilege-revocation migrations before serving sessions rather than lazily after a privileged request.
units.responsibilityConflict: A single long-lived server token authenticates arbitrary identity/role headers and directly marks email verified; compromise permits impersonation and organization provisioning. Legacy cloud users can receive instance-admin authority through the ordinary session path until they first make a trusted-header request, so the cleanup sequence temporarily violates least privilege and accountable-human guarantees.

units.function: Large embedded-Postgres authorization decision suite covering user/Agent grants, Company boundaries, responsible-human ceilings, Agent/skill changes, task assignment, issue visibility and mutation, low-trust review boundaries, protected/private Agents, mention-derived access, instance administration, scoped runtime tokens, inbox delegation and Secret proposals.
units.dependencyDirection: Authenticated actor, action, typed resource and optional scope enter AuthorizationService; it reads Company memberships, explicit Principal grants, Agent permission-policy JSON, hierarchy, Issues/comments, instance roles and inbox policy, then emits a structured allow/deny decision with reason, code, explanation and optional matching grant. Routes and services consume that decision before mutation.
units.keyDataModels: Human/Agent Principal, Company membership and role, PermissionKey grant with JSON scope, responsible-user delegation, action/resource/scope tuple, Agent trustPreset/authorizationPolicy/visibility/assignment policy/hierarchy, Issue/project/assignee/origin/comment mention, task_bridge and skill_test key scopes, instance admin, inbox Agent policy and structured decision reason/code.
units.lifecycle: Cross-Company Agent access is denied first. Low-trust boundaries precede explicit change grants and constrain projects, root/child Issues and allowed Agents. Direct grants or consented suggest grants authorize configuration changes; protected/private targets add hard blocks or scoped grants. Standard-trust same-Company Agents receive default-open visible Issue writes and assignment, while active board members receive several null-mapped actions without explicit grants. Mention comments can dynamically grant Issue read/comment. Scoped JWTs constrain task bridges and skill tests. Responsible-human membership/grants cap delegated Agent actions, and per-user inbox policy controls self or cross-user inbox management.
units.testAssessment: More than fifty database-backed cases exercise a broad decision matrix, real SQL filtering, boundary precedence, structured reasons, low-trust containment, cross-Company denial and scope variants; this is one of Paperclip's strongest test assets. Major gaps remain: grant expiry/revocation/version and concurrent runs, deny grants and policy conflict ordering, immutable consent/approval evidence, purpose/data/tool/export conditions, organization position and accountable role, time/network/environment attributes, exhaustive action-resource coverage, property-level mutation, decision audit receipts, performance/query plans and generated completeness checks. Some tests codify fail-open compatibility rather than safe policy.
units.designRationale: Evolve from a simple same-Company collaborative board toward granular governance without breaking existing Agent workflows: keep default-open collaboration and legacy CEO/member behavior, layer explicit grants and scoped tokens, then introduce low-trust presets and responsible-user ceilings as hard constraints.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a single explainable policy decision point for mixed humans and Agents, but authority must derive from organization responsibility, explicit grants, approved actions and data contracts rather than product-era compatibility defaults.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the policy core while ADAPTing the typed action/resource decision envelope, structured reason/code, explicit scope tests, low-trust precedence, responsible-human ceiling and capability-limited token concepts. Use versioned deny-by-default policy with validated scope schemas, explicit action/resource registry, Principal/Position/ResponsibilityContract, Work/action digest, permission and data grants, risk/approval/evidence context, expiry/revocation and immutable decision receipt. Generate matrix completeness tests and tenant-scope queries.
units.responsibilityConflict: Several intentional defaults violate Company OS invariants: standard-trust Agents may comment on and mutate peer-owned visible Issues without grants; an active non-viewer board member can receive runtime:manage and secrets:read through simple membership; unknown grant-scope metadata is treated as unconstrained; legacy CEO Agents can create Agents without explicit authority; and mutable comment mentions mint access. Responsible-human checks often prove only membership/non-viewer status, not responsibility for the exact action, data or outcome.

units.function: Pure route-authorization tests for Company read/write access across board users, viewers, instance admins, local implicit operators, Agent actors and Agents acting on behalf of a responsible human.
units.dependencyDirection: Actor middleware supplies user/Agent identity, Company ids, membership snapshots and deployment-source flags; route helpers derive boolean visibility or throw HTTP errors before services execute, while organization-level board access uses a broader membership-or-instance-admin predicate.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent/none actor, source, Company id, active membership and viewer/operator role, instance-admin flag, onBehalfOfUserId and responsible-user membership snapshot, HTTP read/write method and structured denial code.
units.lifecycle: Active viewers may read but not write; detailed membership snapshots override legacy Company-id lists. Session instance admins cannot enter a Company without membership, while local_implicit board identity can. Agents are confined to their Company and delegated writes are capped by an active non-viewer responsible human; absent/read-only snapshots fail closed unless a global shadow-mode environment switch converts denial into logging only.
units.testAssessment: Nineteen focused cases cover read/write role behavior, legacy compatibility, local mode, responsible-human ceiling, boolean/assert parity and organization-level access. Missing are suspended/expired/duplicate memberships, membership version or revocation during a run, method override/WebSocket/background jobs, route-level policy composition, shadow-mode audit verification, deployment-profile misconfiguration, accountable purpose and property/action-level permissions. Tests also codify two broad bypasses: legacy companyIds-only writes and local_implicit all-Company access.
units.designRationale: Centralize coarse tenant isolation, preserve older actor shapes, support frictionless local operation and progressively roll out responsible-user authorization without immediately breaking existing Agent flows.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires identity-provider-neutral tenant isolation and a mandatory accountable-human authority ceiling that remains valid through long-running Agent work in managed and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a versioned authorization decision port with explicit Principal, MembershipGrant, ResponsibilityContract, action/resource/purpose and policy revision. Preserve fail-closed responsible-human checks and read-only viewers. Restrict local bootstrap to a named instance owner and explicit organizations; remove production legacy actor fallback and never permit a global shadow switch to bypass high-risk enforcement.
units.responsibilityConflict: The accountable-human ceiling is optional under PAPERCLIP_RESPONSIBLE_USER_AUTHZ_SHADOW, legacy board actors can write from companyIds without role detail, and local_implicit identity receives unrestricted Company access. Membership snapshots carry no policy version, expiry or proof that authority remained valid when an Agent later executes.

units.function: Repository-static regression test intended to require a tenant-visibility 404 gate before write authorization on resources looked up by id, preventing 403-versus-404 cross-tenant existence disclosure.
units.dependencyDirection: The test scans first-party route source text at test time, matches direct assertCompanyAccess(req, variable.companyId) calls, searches the previous twelve lines for a corresponding hasCompanyAccess call and exempts two request-input sites through a manually maintained allowlist.
units.keyDataModels: Route filename/source line, resource variable and companyId expression, twelve-line lookback window, request-input allowlist entry and 404 visibility-before-403 mutation pattern.
units.lifecycle: Every test run enumerates TypeScript route files and reports recognized assertion sites without a nearby visibility gate. A companion test rejects allowlist entries whose exact assertion expression disappeared.
units.testAssessment: The two tests provide useful cheap regression coverage and stale-allowlist hygiene, but the regex recognizes only one-line direct calls with a word variable and literal .companyId. Aliases, destructuring, multiline calls, wrappers, optional chaining, renamed helpers, non-route transports and gates more than twelve lines away can evade or falsely trigger it; it proves source shape, not runtime 404 behavior or query-level tenant filtering.
units.designRationale: Institutionalize a subtle tenant-enumeration fix across many route handlers without requiring each contributor to remember the pattern manually.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must prevent cross-tenant existence, timing and count oracles consistently across REST, events, search, export, Connector and realtime boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the invariant structurally: tenant-scope repository queries by construction, expose findVisibleById rather than global getById, use typed authorization middleware, add runtime black-box cross-tenant suites and optionally an AST rule. Retain a narrowly documented exception ledger with owners and expiry, not regex source scanning as the primary control.
units.responsibilityConflict: A source-shape guard can be green while an alias, alternate helper or non-HTTP path leaks another Company's resource. Responsibility evidence itself is sensitive, so existence protection must apply to every projection and event subscription rather than only recognized route assertions.

units.function: Unit tests for projecting the authenticated actor and intended technical consumer into SecretService access-event context without injecting binding or configuration-path authority.
units.dependencyDirection: Route code supplies the trusted Express actor plus consumer type/id; buildActorSecretContext maps board users or delegated Agents to actor and responsible-user attribution, then SecretService performs any later resolution and binding checks.
units.keyDataModels: Actor type/id/source, userId, onBehalfOfUserId, responsibleUserId, consumerType agent/environment/system, consumerId, deliberately absent configPath and allowedBindingIds.
units.lifecycle: Board user identity becomes both actor and responsible human. Agent identity remains the actor while its on-behalf-of human becomes responsible; direct userId wins if both fields exist. Missing human responsibility remains null. Caller-selected consumer attribution passes through, but no binding allowlist or path is minted by this helper.
units.testAssessment: Five compact cases cover attribution precedence, absent human responsibility, all consumer classes and absence of accidental binding fields. Missing are actor type/source validation, spoof-resistant construction, consumer ownership/tenant matching, required responsible human by purpose, grants, Work/action/purpose, Secret version, expiry, decision/evidence linkage and integration proving access is denied rather than merely logged when context is incomplete.
units.designRationale: Separate honest audit attribution from Secret binding authorization and avoid fabricating configuration scope at the HTTP edge.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs every Secret projection to identify the actual requester, accountable human and execution consumer while proving a purpose-bound grant to a specific Work action and data policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the separation of actor, responsible human and consumer, plus the rule that route helpers cannot invent binding authority. Replace free consumer parameters with a validated Connector/ExecutionPrincipal reference and require SecretGrant id/version, Work/action digest, purpose, expiry, data contract and accountable human before issuance; null responsibility must fail for governed use.
units.responsibilityConflict: The context is attribution metadata, not authorization. Callers choose consumerType/id, responsibility may be null and no grant/binding/action scope is carried, so an access event can truthfully describe a technically successful use that was never organizationally authorized.

units.function: Comprehensive AWS Secrets Manager provider tests for managed and externally linked Secrets, SigV4 requests, namespace isolation, rotation, metadata-only discovery, error redaction, version resolution, health, deletion/recovery and rollback of write-through changes.
units.dependencyDirection: SecretService-facing provider methods receive provider-vault config, Secret value/context and stored provider material; a gateway or built-in signed HTTP client calls AWS APIs. Only opaque ARN/version/hash/material returns to persistence, while plaintext crosses the provider boundary transiently for create, update or resolve.
units.keyDataModels: AWS region/endpoint/credentials/KMS key, deployment/prefix/Company namespace and tags, managed versus external-reference material, ARN, AWS VersionId/VersionStage, PAPERCLIP_PENDING/AWSCURRENT, previous and last-written versions, provider vault candidate, metadata pagination, health warning and redacted client error.
units.lifecycle: Managed creation derives an exact deployment/Company name and optional KMS key, with later versions staged pending and out-of-scope refs rejected. External references store metadata only; optional write-through captures current version, publishes a new AWSCURRENT and records rollback ids. Listing/discovery never calls GetSecretValue and filters foreign managed samples. Resolution may pin a version and revalidates managed namespace. Managed deletion uses a recovery window; archive removes pending stage, while external rollback moves AWSCURRENT back to the prior version.
units.testAssessment: Eighteen unusually strong provider tests cover plaintext non-persistence, selected-vault isolation from env fallback, request signing/timeout signal, namespace drift, managed/external ownership separation, metadata-only discovery, redacted public errors, version-pinned resolution, configuration health, deletion safety and rollback semantics. Missing are real AWS/LocalStack contract tests, binary Secrets, credential refresh/IMDS failure, retries/throttling/idempotency tokens, endpoint/account/partition validation, KMS policy/grants, tag spoofing, pagination limits, concurrent rotations/CAS, partial network outcomes, deletion restoration, zeroization and proof that rawMessage is never logged or serialized.
units.designRationale: Support both Company-owned managed Secret lifecycle and existing enterprise vault references without copying values into the control database, while defending provider ownership boundaries and offering reversible operations and safe discovery UX.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a provider-neutral Secret custody port spanning managed cloud and customer-local vaults, with explicit ownership, immutable grant/audit evidence, purpose-bound delivery and safe coexistence with enterprise rotation systems.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the provider contract, managed/external ownership split, namespace revalidation on every operation, metadata-only discovery, recovery window, structured redaction and version material. Use the official AWS SDK/credential chain rather than owning SigV4 transport unless proven necessary. Require KMS/profile policy, account/partition allowlists, idempotency/CAS, transactional operation journal and execution-node leases tied to Work, Connector, purpose, expiry and accountable human.
units.responsibilityConflict: External write-through immediately changes AWSCURRENT for every external consumer without an approval/action digest in the provider contract. Rollback records two version ids but does not prove AWSCURRENT still equals the version Company OS wrote; a concurrent enterprise rotation could be overwritten. The error object retains raw provider text containing account/ARN metadata, and selected vault config permits no KMS key despite the default health path treating KMS as required.

units.function: Pure configuration tests for Better Auth cookie namespace isolation, secure-cookie selection, authentication rate limiting and trusted-origin derivation across deployment modes, exposure profiles, URLs, hostnames and resolved ports.
units.dependencyDirection: Deployment/bootstrap configuration and environment variables enter helper functions that build Better Auth advanced, rate-limit and trusted-origin options; the external Better Auth library derives concrete cookie names and enforces the resulting settings.
units.keyDataModels: Instance id and cookie prefix, deployment mode/exposure, auth base-URL mode, explicit/resolved public URL, secure-cookie boolean, rate-limit override, allowed hostname, configured/listen port and HTTP/HTTPS trusted origin.
units.lifecycle: Startup scopes cookies per instance, disables Secure for local HTTP/private auto-origin cases, retains it for HTTPS/public cases, enables auth rate limiting by default but accepts an explicit off override, and expands allowed hostnames into HTTP/HTTPS origin variants including the resolved non-default port.
units.testAssessment: Seventeen focused cases cover cookie naming, local/public/private URL combinations, default and overridden rate limiting, case-normalized hostnames and port resolution. Missing are SameSite/HttpOnly/domain/path/max-age, prefix sanitization/collision and cookie tossing, malformed/credentialed/IDNA/IPv6 origins, wildcard or proxy headers, CSRF flows, session rotation/revocation, distributed rate-limit storage/keying/bypass and a guard prohibiting rate-limit disablement on public profiles.
units.designRationale: Allow multiple local/worktree instances and mixed HTTP/HTTPS deployments without cookie collisions or broken sign-in, while supplying safe-ish auth defaults and host-derived origin trust.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs replaceable OIDC/SSO/local Identity adapters whose browser session policy is explicit per managed-cloud and self-hosted profile and cannot silently weaken due to URL autodetection.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the instance namespace, canonical-origin and resolved-listen-port test matrix at the Web adapter boundary. Enforce profile invariants: public production requires HTTPS Secure cookies and non-disableable distributed rate limiting; trusted origins must use explicitly configured schemes rather than automatically trusting both HTTP and HTTPS for every hostname. Keep Better Auth optional behind IdentityPort.
units.responsibilityConflict: Cookie/session configuration authenticates a browser but does not prove Company role or accountable authority. Explicitly disabling rate limiting is allowed even for public exposure, and auto-derived origins trust both schemes; operator configuration can therefore weaken identity assurance without a governed change record.

units.function: Route tests for an experimental local-only Conference Room board chat that persists conversation through an Issue, spawns a local assistant subprocess, streams output, terminates it on client disconnect and classifies only concierge-authored comments as assistant history.
units.dependencyDirection: Experimental instance setting and deployment mode gate the route; board request and Issue/comment history feed a node child_process, whose output streams to the client and whose replies persist as a synthetic board-concierge user. Client connection lifecycle controls subprocess termination.
units.keyDataModels: Feature flag, local_trusted/authenticated mode, Company/message request, standing Issue/comments, synthetic board-concierge author, human/Agent history role, subprocess stdin/stdout/stderr/exit and SSE disconnect.
units.lifecycle: Disabled or non-local deployments fail before persistence. Enabled local requests validate Company/message, load/create board Issue history and spawn a process. Client abort sends SIGTERM and close releases the slot. Only comments with no Agent author and exact concierge user id become assistant turns, preventing Agent comments from impersonating prior assistant output.
units.testAssessment: Five focused cases cover flag/mode ordering, structured disabled codes, missing-body admission, disconnect cleanup and history-role spoof resistance. Authorization is mocked to unconditional success. Missing are real actor/Company isolation, exact command/argument safety, environment/Secret exposure, input length/content, concurrency/queue bounds, child-process tree and forced-kill timeout, crash/restart, stderr/redaction, output framing/backpressure, persistence consistency, model identity/version, prompt injection and evidence that synthetic concierge output is never represented as a real Agent or human.
units.designRationale: Experiment with a conversational board entry point using existing Issue history while containing an immature local subprocess feature behind both a flag and deployment-mode gate.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS may need an Agent Boss conversational entry, but every assistant must be a declared Connector/Agent runtime with capability, identity, evidence, cancellation and responsibility—not an implicit local child process hidden behind a UI route.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT this runtime pattern for Company OS production. REFERENCE ONLY the early feature/mode gate, disconnect cancellation and non-impersonating history classification. Implement future chat through Connector SDK and AgentExecutionPort with explicit Demo versus real labeling, bounded streaming, durable Run/evidence, accountable requester and policy checks.
units.responsibilityConflict: Replies persist under a synthetic user id and a locally spawned process is not modeled as an Agent/Connector principal with permissions, model/provider identity, execution attestation or accountable human. Route-level process spawning also bypasses the planned customer-local execution boundary.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres ownership-transfer test for a token-and-code board claim challenge that replaces the local implicit administrator with a signed-in user and grants that user owner membership.
units.dependencyDirection: Deployment initialization creates an inspectable challenge/warning URL; a signed-in user presents token plus code to claimBoardOwnership, which updates instance roles and Company membership in the database and updates challenge inspection state.
units.keyDataModels: Claim token/code/status, requires-sign-in flag, claimed user, local-board and human instance-admin roles, Company owner membership, authenticated/local deployment mode and warning URL.
units.lifecycle: Switching to authenticated mode produces a warning URL with two challenge components. Inspection reports available and sign-in-required. A valid signed-in claimant atomically removes local-board admin, creates its instance-admin role and owner membership, after which inspection reports claimed.
units.testAssessment: One high-value real-database happy path proves privilege transfer and Company membership effects. Missing are token entropy/storage/hash and log exposure, expiry/rotation/single-use, wrong token/code/user, replay, parallel claims, transaction failure, multiple Companies and existing owners, challenge persistence across restart, audit event, session freshness/MFA and recovery from a lost challenge.
units.designRationale: Make the security-sensitive transition from implicit local control to authenticated human ownership explicit and observable rather than silently retaining a shared local administrator.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs an auditable installation/ownership-transfer ceremony for self-hosted deployments and later IdP changes that does not collapse instance administration and every Company's accountable ownership.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the two-part one-time challenge, sign-in requirement, atomic removal/grant and inspectable state. Separate InstanceOperator from CompanyOwner, hash and expire server-side capabilities, require target organization and verified identity/MFA, emit immutable before/after receipt, test restart/concurrency/recovery and never place both secret components in the same URL or log channel.
units.responsibilityConflict: The test grants the claimant instance admin and owner membership together and does not show which Companies are affected. A technically valid setup token is not by itself proof that the claimant is the organization's accountable human, and no durable decision/audit receipt is asserted.

units.function: Middleware tests for browser-origin protection on state-changing board requests, with exemptions for non-cookie local, API-key, Cloud-tenant and Agent actors.
units.dependencyDirection: Authenticated actor source plus HTTP method and Host/Origin/Referer/X-Forwarded-Host headers enter boardMutationGuard before mutation routes; cookie-session board requests require a matching browser origin, while non-browser credentials bypass this CSRF-specific gate and proceed to authorization.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor source, safe versus mutating HTTP method, Host and forwarded host, Origin/Referer URL and 403 browser-origin error.
units.lifecycle: Reads pass. Session-backed board mutations without a trusted Origin/Referer fail; matching direct or forwarded host passes. local_implicit, board_key and cloud_tenant board sources and all Agent actors bypass the origin requirement because their credentials are treated as non-cookie or trusted channels.
units.testAssessment: Ten focused middleware cases cover safe methods, missing/matching/mismatched origins, Referer fallback, forwarded hosts and credential-source exemptions. Missing are OPTIONS/HEAD semantics, malformed/multiple/comma-separated forwarded hosts, trusted-proxy enforcement, scheme/downgrade/default-port normalization, IPv6/IDNA, Origin null, forwarded proto, Sec-Fetch-Site, SameSite cookie behavior, websocket/SSE mutation paths and structured error codes. The permissive forwarded-host case is not paired with a direct-client spoof denial.
units.designRationale: Prevent cookie-authenticated cross-site request forgery without breaking local CLI, Agent API keys or a trusted Cloud gateway whose requests do not carry browser Origin headers.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs profile-aware CSRF/origin enforcement that remains correct behind enterprise proxies and distinguishes browser sessions from Connector/workload credentials without treating actor type alone as transport proof.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT source-aware CSRF separation, but bind credential class during authentication and use an explicit canonical-origin allowlist. Honor Forwarded/X-Forwarded-* only through verified proxy hops, require HTTPS in managed profiles, add SameSite and anti-CSRF token defense in depth, cover websocket/realtime commands and return stable codes.
units.responsibilityConflict: Origin validation protects request provenance, not organizational authority. board_key, cloud_tenant and Agent actors bypass it entirely, so their credential issuance and scope must carry the responsibility contract. Trusting client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host without a proven proxy boundary can turn the guard into a bypass.

units.function: Configuration tests for global JSON, portable JSON and compressed Company-import upload ceilings, including operator override parsing and arithmetic-safe clamping.
units.dependencyDirection: Environment configuration initializes HTTP parser/import constants; global and import-specific routes consume the limits before archive parsing, with no domain or tenant context in this unit.
units.keyDataModels: 10 MiB JSON ceiling, 64 MiB portable JSON ceiling, 1 GiB default ZIP upload, operator byte override and 64 GiB maximum clamp chosen so four-times derived guard math remains a safe integer.
units.lifecycle: Startup uses fixed JSON limits and a one-GiB compressed import default. A positive integer environment override replaces it up to 64 GiB; invalid, fractional or nonpositive values fall back to default.
units.testAssessment: Six deterministic cases cover defaults, real-world larger portable payloads, override acceptance/fallback and numeric-overflow protection. Missing are route-level streaming enforcement, Content-Length absent/lying/chunked requests, compressed/uncompressed ratio and entry-count limits, disk/memory quota, concurrent uploads, tenant/operator quotas, slowloris/timeouts, multipart overhead, cleanup on abort and validation that very large configured values are operationally safe.
units.designRationale: Accommodate large real Company export packages and operator-specific deployments while preventing invalid configuration and JavaScript numeric overflow in derived archive guards.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS imports may contain sensitive organization, evidence and configuration data; availability and storage budgets must be enforced by profile, tenant and import plan rather than a single process-wide byte constant.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as streaming staged import with small compressed ingress quota, independent uncompressed bytes/entry/depth/path/ratio limits, tenant reservation, rate/concurrency/time ceilings, quarantine storage and cleanup. Retain strict override parsing and safe arithmetic, but require explicit deployment policy for multi-gigabyte imports and emit capacity/audit events.
units.responsibilityConflict: A one-GiB default and configurable 64-GiB compressed upload can exhaust shared control-plane resources before Company-level authorization or accountability is considered. Byte ceilings alone do not constrain ZIP bombs or ensure imported responsibility records and assets are validated atomically.

units.function: Route tests for first-instance-admin claim through an authenticated private browser session or a bootstrap human invite, including deployment-profile gating, actor restrictions, CSRF guard composition and concurrent-winner conflict.
units.dependencyDirection: Deployment mode/exposure, board actor and optional invite token enter access routes; both browser and invite paths call one claimFirstInstanceAdmin compare-and-set helper, while boardMutationGuard and invite validation sit outside the helper.
units.keyDataModels: Authenticated/private deployment profile, board session actor, instance-admin claim status, bootstrap_ceo invite token hash/type/expiry/revocation/acceptance, claimed user and 200/202/401/404/409 outcomes.
units.lifecycle: Only a session user on authenticated-private deployment can call the direct browser claim; anonymous, Agent, board-key and local-implicit actors are rejected and public/local modes hide the route. The origin guard can block the mutation. A valid human bootstrap invite runs its acceptance inside the shared claim callback. Whichever claimant wins becomes first admin; later direct or invite attempts receive conflict.
units.testAssessment: Seven route scenarios cover profile/actor gating, origin composition, shared atomic helper and race conflict. Service/database behavior is mocked. Missing are proof that signup itself is restricted, out-of-band deployment ownership, brute-force/rate limit, invite expiry/revocation/hash timing, simultaneous real transactions, rollback of invite acceptance, session freshness/MFA, audit alert, existing data/Companies, recovery/reset and stable machine-readable errors.
units.designRationale: Offer a browser-friendly zero-admin bootstrap for private instances while avoiding exposure on public deployments and sharing atomic ownership transfer with the explicit invite path.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS self-hosted setup must securely bind the first accountable human and enterprise identity provider without allowing the first reachable authenticated account to seize every Company and credential.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as an installation ceremony: one-time short-lived setup capability emitted to console/file or signed installer assertion, canonical local origin, fresh IdP authentication/MFA, explicit target organization, atomic claim and immutable audit. Disable open signup or first-admin mutation until ownership proof; keep invitation and disaster recovery as separate governed flows.
units.responsibilityConflict: Private network exposure is treated as evidence of deployment ownership. Any user able to establish a session before the legitimate operator can claim instance-admin authority, and the fixture does not bind the claim to a named organization, legal administrator or setup capability.

units.function: BudgetService tests for Company, project and Agent spend policies, soft/hard incidents, approval creation, pause/cancellation, invocation release gates, budget raise/resume, ledger reconciliation, overview projection and telemetry redaction.
units.dependencyDirection: Immutable-ish cost events and active policies enter BudgetService; it aggregates observed spend, writes incidents and budget-override approvals, pauses Company/project/Agent records, calls a runtime cancellation boundary and logs sanitized activity. Invocation paths query the same service before starting work, while board incident resolution updates policy/budget and resumes only budget-owned pauses.
units.keyDataModels: Budget policy scope/metric/window/amount/warn percent/hard-stop flags, CostEvent provider/model/tokens/cents/time, soft/hard incident and observed/limit/window, budget_override_required Approval, Company/project/Agent pause reason/time, invocation block, overview utilization and decision note/user.
units.lifecycle: Each cost event reevaluates applicable policies against live ledger totals. Crossing warning creates one soft incident per window; crossing hard resolves soft state, creates one hard incident plus pending override Approval, marks the scope budget-paused and cancels work. New invocations are blocked by either pause state or still-exceeded live policy. Resolution rejects a limit not above current spend, approves the incident, raises the policy/Company monthly budget and clears only budget-owned pause; overview reconciles live ledger values.
units.testAssessment: Seven focused unit/integration cases cover reactive enforcement, release-gate checks independent of pause lag, manual-versus-budget pause reason, live spend at resolution, Company budget sync, one-incident idempotency, Agent/project cancellation, ledger-derived overview and telemetry redaction. Gaps include cost-event dedup/idempotency key, transaction/outbox around incident/approval/pause/cancel, cancellation failure/retry, concurrent spend/raises, reservations before expensive actions, delayed/estimated/negative/refund costs, currency/FX, hierarchical policy precedence, window boundaries/timezones, authorization/separation of duties, maximum override and evidence tying the Approval to exact policy/action digest.
units.designRationale: Make spend governance an enforceable backend release gate rather than a dashboard warning, preserve a human override path, stop already-running work and reconcile decisions against the authoritative cost ledger instead of stale incident snapshots.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs cost and resource governance across heterogeneous models/Agents where an accountable human approves exceptional spend and the system can prove which work was stopped, resumed and charged.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the ledger-derived live check, scope hierarchy, soft/hard incident split, budget-owned pause reason, pre-invocation block, sanitized telemetry and raise-above-observed rule. Add budget reservations/estimated upper bounds before execution, currency and provider billing normalization, immutable policy/action digest, risk-based approver separation, transaction + outbox for cancel/resume, Connector cancellation receipts and reconciliation for late/refunded costs.
units.responsibilityConflict: Enforcement is primarily reactive after a CostEvent, so spend can exceed the limit before cancellation. The service API accepts a board-user id to approve and raise without proving role, separation of duties or maximum authority. Repeated hard evaluation avoids duplicate incidents but calls cancellation twice, and no durable side-effect receipt proves every affected Run stopped before later spend.

units.function: Pure tests for parsing and resolving the full source commit embedded into a deployment when Git metadata is unavailable.
units.dependencyDirection: Build environment or a stamped marker file enters a server helper; a valid full hexadecimal SHA is normalized and exposed as deployment metadata, with environment taking precedence over file.
units.keyDataModels: Forty-character Git commit SHA, environment override, build marker path/file and null invalid state.
units.lifecycle: Startup first parses an explicit environment value and otherwise reads the image marker. Full mixed-case SHA is lowercased; truncated/malformed values return null.
units.testAssessment: Four concise cases cover normalization, malformed/truncated denial, precedence and marker fallback. Missing are file read errors, invalid environment followed by valid file behavior, SHA-256 repositories, dirty state, repository identity, signature/SBOM/provenance validation and proof the environment value matches the executable image.
units.designRationale: Preserve exact source traceability in packaged images and installations where .git is intentionally absent.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs every control-plane and customer-local execution node to report verifiable software provenance so responsibility evidence can identify the code that made or executed a decision.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT full immutable source revision stamping and environment/file fallback as informational metadata. Add product/repository identity, build digest, SBOM, dependency lock digest, deployment profile, database schema revision and signed supply-chain attestation; never treat a caller-controlled environment SHA as proof.
units.responsibilityConflict: A syntactically valid SHA can be injected through the environment and is not cryptographically bound to the running artifact. It is useful observability but insufficient runtime attestation for an approval or evidence chain.
evidence: 16b95eece54ef95d9eb5ebfdac952f2bba51f269 fix(server): preserve source SHA without Git metadata (#9638)

units.function: Pure tests for resolving a human-readable stamped build version from environment or image marker with null fallback.
units.dependencyDirection: Build environment/file marker flows into a server metadata helper; nonempty single-token text is returned, with explicit environment taking precedence and missing files producing null.
units.keyDataModels: Git-describe or release/canary version string, environment override, build-version marker and null unknown version.
units.lifecycle: Startup trims a stamped version, rejects empty or whitespace-bearing values, prefers environment and otherwise reads the marker; absent or unreadable source yields null.
units.testAssessment: Six cases cover git-describe/release strings, malformed whitespace, precedence, marker and absence. The parser accepts any non-whitespace token and does not enforce SemVer/calendar-version grammar, maximum length, allowed characters, consistency with commit or signed release metadata.
units.designRationale: Show the actual image/release version rather than a placeholder package version and remain functional in source or incomplete build environments.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS managed and self-hosted operators need a stable support/upgrade identity and compatibility matrix independent of source checkout details.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY for fallback mechanics. Define a structured BuildIdentity with validated product version, protocol/schema compatibility ranges, source revision and artifact digest; keep display labels separate from machine upgrade contracts.
units.responsibilityConflict: An arbitrary environment token can become the displayed version and null is tolerated, so this cannot prove which policy or Connector implementation executed accountable work.

units.function: HTTP route tests for listing, provisioning and resetting registry-defined built-in Agents and controlling their scheduled/manual routines behind an experimental feature gate.
units.dependencyDirection: Company-scoped board or Agent actor enters feature/access checks; routes validate strict payloads and call BuiltInAgentService for state/provision/reset/routine operations, then emit activity. Generic AuthorizationService gates provision/reset with agents:create, while routine controls use board-only tasks:assign.
units.keyDataModels: Built-in definition key/display/purpose/instructions/role/allowed Adapter types, materialized Agent/state/pause, optional Adapter override and monthly budget, hire Approval, routine key/schedule/run, actor/requester and activity event.
units.lifecycle: Feature-disabled routes hide with 404. Authorized Company actors may list redacted state. Provision validates exact fields and can materialize immediately or return pending hire approval under Company policy. Reset uses the same create grant. Only board users with tasks:assign may enable/disable/trigger routines; Agent actors are categorically denied. Every accepted mutation logs actor and entity context.
units.testAssessment: Fourteen route cases cover Company isolation, feature gate ordering, explicit create denial, strict body schema, Adapter/budget forwarding, board-only routine controls, pending approval response, reset auditing and cross-Company Agent denial. Services and auth are mocked. Missing are idempotency/concurrency, exact definition/version/digest, Adapter Secret redaction beyond response config, risk-specific reset/reconfigure approval, requester/approver separation, routine input/goal/budget/data grants, cancellation/timeouts, feature-toggle audit, stable errors and E2E proof that the approved registry revision is materialized.
units.designRationale: Ship opinionated first-party Agent capabilities with a simple setup experience while preserving Company isolation, existing Agent-creation policy, strict configuration and human control over recurring autonomous work.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs FDE-driven industry templates and installable capability packs that can create organization roles, Agent/Connector bindings, workflows, policies and views without embedding one vendor's runtime or silently bypassing responsibility.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the definition registry, allowed Adapter constraints, redacted state, strict payloads, approval-aware provisioning and disabled-by-default routines into a signed TemplatePackage contract. Separate template installation from Agent creation/reset permissions, pin package/version/digest, preview a change plan, require risk-based human approval, and instantiate vendor-neutral Connector/Position/Responsibility/DataGrant objects transactionally with rollback.
units.responsibilityConflict: A generic agents:create grant also authorizes resetting built-in defaults, including for Agent actors, without proving which instructions/resources changed or requiring a human. Routine runs are gated only by tasks:assign and do not bind a Work goal, data/Secret grants, budget reservation or accountable result owner in the route contract.

units.function: Large embedded-Postgres suite for registry-defined built-in Agent bundles, including asset fallback, lazy/automatic provisioning, hire approval, Adapter validation, typed readiness, managed instructions/skills/routines, drift/reset, immutable markers, uniqueness/concurrency repair, default permissions and proposal-confirmation workflows.
units.dependencyDirection: Static first-party definitions/assets flow into BuiltInAgentService and startup reconciliation; the service composes generic Agent, Approval, Instruction, Skill, Routine, Permission and Interaction services plus database uniqueness/managed-resource bindings. Operators may configure/reset while reconciliation maintains identity/default resources without overwriting detected content drift.
units.keyDataModels: Built-in definition/key/features/defaults/allowed Adapters/models, Agent marker/status/config/budget/reportsTo/permissions, hire Approval payload, managed resource kind/key/current/stock hash and drift status, Skill version, Routine/trigger/schedule, config revision, proposal Interaction/target revision, partial unique index and reconciliation counters.
units.lifecycle: Registry validation rejects duplicate/invalid/default-disallowed definitions. Ensure lazily creates one marked Agent, validates Adapter/model and derives not_provisioned/needs_setup/ready/paused states. Policy-gated creation freezes a pending Agent and approval payload; approval restores the snapshot and materializes resources. Startup can auto-provision paused zero-budget bundles, grant suggestion capabilities, repair display metadata and missing bindings, preserve operator-modified content, reconcile duplicates and continue other Companies. Explicit reset restores selected stock resources. Routines remain disabled until a board enables them; accepted coaching proposals are applied only in a later step.
units.testAssessment: Thirty-plus rich tests cover real schema constraints, concurrent provisioning, legacy duplicate repair, pending approval tamper resistance, Adapter/model allowlists, typed errors, resource drift/hash/reset, startup fault containment, default-disabled automation, least-privilege suggestion grants and accept/reject proposal flow. Major gaps: signed package provenance/version/dependencies/migrations/rollback/uninstall, transactionality across Agent/Skill/Routine/grants, crash injection and outbox, explicit responsible human/data grants, package upgrade compatibility, malicious assets, resource ownership conflicts, approval digest for setup/reset/apply, multi-node reconciliation locks and proof that later execution uses the displayed proposal bytes.
units.designRationale: Deliver opinionated product capabilities as idempotent managed bundles while preserving operator customization, existing governance gates and safe disabled defaults; recover automatically from legacy duplicates or partial materialization without making startup brittle.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a trustworthy FDE/industry-template mechanism that packages organization structure, Agent/Connector roles, instructions, workflows, data policies and Agent Boss views, supports local customization and can upgrade or exit cleanly.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT uniqueness, idempotent materialization, managed-resource bindings, stock/current hash drift, selective reset, disabled automation, strict Adapter capabilities and approval-aware plans as the primary reference for TemplatePackage. Replace hardcoded vendor models/Agents with capability requirements and Connector bindings; add signed manifest/license/SBOM, semantic versions, dependency/migration/rollback/uninstall, atomic plan/apply receipts, organization/data/responsibility objects and explicit owner consent for grants or reset.
units.responsibilityConflict: First setup can apply previously unknown Adapter config and budget without a new approval merely because an empty Agent row already exists. Startup reconciliation auto-adds permissions and undeletable Agents. Missing asset files silently fall back to embedded text. Most critically, the follow-up apply helper checks only that an Interaction was accepted, then writes caller-supplied nextInstructions without verifying it matches the displayed diff/target revision; approval A can authorize execution B. Duplicate repair also keeps the oldest row and cancels the newer approval without evaluating which revision humans approved.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for refreshing execution isolation after plan acceptance, realizing approved child workspaces from a current base reference, and preventing an accepted-plan continuation or session from crossing Issue ownership boundaries.
units.dependencyDirection: The suite drives heartbeatService and issueService through real Company, Project, Issue, interaction, plan-decomposition, task-session and execution-workspace tables; it invokes local Git/worktree side effects through the Heartbeat path while mocking only the execution adapter.
units.keyDataModels: Issue workMode and responsibleUserId, accepted issue-document revision and thread interaction, IssuePlanDecomposition claim/owner/status, ExecutionWorkspace strategy and sourceIssueId, AgentTaskSession taskKey/session parameters, wake payload/context routing flags, and adapter runtime/context.
units.lifecycle: An accepted confirmation wake can discard a shared planning workspace and stale task session, realize an isolated worktree, and execute in a fresh session; decomposed child Issues retain only workspace strategy until their first run so they resolve the then-current remote base; an in-flight decomposition claim owned by another Issue suppresses continuation and forces a fresh session, while the same Issue may resume its existing accepted-plan session.
units.testAssessment: Five substantial integration cases cover shared-to-isolated refresh, delayed child realization after base movement, cross-Issue claim suppression for planning and standard work, and same-Issue continuation. They exercise a real database and Git repositories, but do not prove transactional behavior across interaction, decomposition, workspace, session and run writes; approval authorization, expiry, revocation or exact action/digest binding; concurrent claim acquisition; crash recovery during worktree creation; remote-base trust and authorization; cleanup/compensation; or rejection/cancellation. Several wake cases use unpersisted interaction IDs or trusted accepted flags in payload/context, so the suite does not establish that execution derives from an authoritative approval record.
units.designRationale: Separate planning from implementation by refreshing execution isolation and session state at the acceptance boundary, delay child workspace realization to avoid freezing an obsolete base commit, and use Issue-scoped decomposition ownership to prevent stale approvals or sessions from contaminating unrelated work.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must turn a human-approved plan into bounded execution without carrying stale Agent memory, code/data workspace state or approval authority into another Work item, while preserving a precise responsibility chain and reproducible execution base.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the approval-boundary workspace refresh, lazy child realization, Work-scoped session identity and cross-Work continuation guard. Company OS should drive them from an immutable ApprovalDecision bound to action, plan revision/digest, Work, responsibility contract, accountable human, Agent, permissions/data contract and expiry; reserve the claim atomically, materialize through WorkspacePort, record a base/workspace attestation, and publish state changes through a transaction/outbox with compensating cleanup. Wake payload fields are hints, never authority.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip stores a resolvedByUserId on a persisted acceptance fixture, but execution routing can be activated by caller-supplied interactionStatus/workspaceRefreshReason flags and some tests never persist the referenced interaction. The plan claim binds an owner Agent and revision but not the accountable human, exact approved action/digest, permission/data snapshot, runtime attestation or revocation state. Mutable multi-table state and local Git effects can therefore diverge from the approval and evidence chain.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres end-to-end specification for detecting active Heartbeat runs with stale output, creating deduplicated evaluation work, redacting log evidence, recording reviewer decisions, folding source-resolved runs and preventing recursive recovery.
units.dependencyDirection: The suite drives heartbeatService and recoveryService against real Run, Issue, WatchdogDecision, RecoveryAction, comment, relation and activity tables; it mocks execution adapters/telemetry but uses the real run-log store and redaction path.
units.keyDataModels: HeartbeatRun output timestamps/sequence/log reference, source Issue and executionRunId, stale_active_run_evaluation Issue, WatchdogDecision with continue/snooze/dismissed_false_positive, IssueRecoveryAction, same-run activity/comment evidence and source-resolved fold receipt in resultJson.
units.lifecycle: Seed an apparently running silent execution; scan suspicion/critical thresholds; create one manager-Agent evaluation without blocking the source; redact evidence; accept authorized decisions and re-arm windows; suppress false positives/board-closed repeats; when exact same-run terminal evidence proves source resolution, terminalize/fold the run, clear execution linkage, resolve recovery work and record event/decision; otherwise escalate.
units.testAssessment: Eighteen substantial cases cover priority thresholds, dedupe, source-comment idempotency, blocked-source exemption, secret/JWT/GitHub token redaction, decision authorization and run binding, re-arm/snooze, recursive recovery, same-run evidence versus other-actor completion, idempotent fold and board-close behavior. Gaps include Connector heartbeats that legitimately emit no text, structured progress versus log silence, distributed scanner races, clock skew, log-store outage, redaction property/fuzz tests, crash points across fold writes, human reviewer authorization, remote process attestation and immutable responsibility/data/approval digests.
units.designRationale: Treat silence as a suspicion requiring review rather than immediate cancellation, avoid self-amplifying blocker/recovery loops, and demand run-bound durable evidence before interpreting a terminal source Issue as proof that an apparently active execution actually finished.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs runtime health policies that distinguish no output from no progress, generate one intervention case, preserve secret-free evidence and require a responsible human or policy-approved actor to continue, stop or dismiss a run.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the graduated suspicion/critical states, observability-only incident, evidence redaction, run-bound decision authorization, finite continue re-arm, recursive-recovery guard and exact same-run fold requirement. Build on structured Connector progress/health/attestation events, immutable InterventionDecision receipts, human-first authority and an atomic event/outbox projection rather than Paperclip log silence and Issue rows.
units.responsibilityConflict: Although the fixture sets a company default responsible user, evaluation work is assigned to a manager Agent and an Agent recovery owner records decisions. Board-closing an Issue is automatically interpreted as dismissed_false_positive without an explicit human receipt. The fold spans multiple mutable tables and stores proof in resultJson, so authority/evidence can diverge if a write fails.
