units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration tests preventing new Heartbeat activity for archived Companies and Agents whose reporting chain contains a terminated manager.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat timer, wake, queue-resume and scheduled-retry entry points consult Company status and Agent organization-chain invokability before creating or starting Runs; invalid queued work is terminalized in Run and wake-request projections.
units.keyDataModels: Company active/archived status, Agent status/reportsTo hierarchy and heartbeat settings, Issue monitor timestamps, queued/scheduled-retry Run, wake request and structured agent_not_invokable/company.inactive reasons.
units.lifecycle: Archived Companies are excluded from timer iteration and monitor advancement; background wakes are persisted as skipped, explicit user invokes fail with 409, and existing queued Runs are left unstarted. A child of a terminated manager rejects explicit invocation, cancels queued Run/wake pairs at resume, and cancels due scheduled retries with a stable error code.
units.testAssessment: Eight integration cases cover timers, background and explicit wakes, monitors, queued resume, terminated-manager chain and scheduled retries. Missing are archive/reactivation authorization, archive while a Run is already executing, Connector/token/tool revocation, cancellation acknowledgment, queued-work pause versus cancel semantics, evidence retention, multi-level/cyclic/cross-Company chains, other manager/Agent statuses, reassignment to a valid accountable owner, concurrent status changes and transaction/outbox atomicity. Archived queued Runs remain queued without a durable pause reason or tested reactivation policy.
units.designRationale: Treat organization validity and Company lifecycle as hard execution admission invariants across every scheduler entry point, not just UI visibility, and prevent deferred work from bypassing them.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must stop or safely suspend all Agent authority when a Company, employment relationship or reporting/responsibility chain becomes invalid, while preserving evidence and an explicit recovery path.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the centralized invokability policy and revalidation across timer/wake/dequeue/retry paths. Model CompanyLifecycleDecision and Principal/ResponsibilityContract validity separately; on archive, atomically stop admission, revoke runtime/data capabilities, request cancellation of active attempts, classify queued work as suspended or cancelled by policy, and retain immutable receipts. A terminated manager should invalidate affected responsibility contracts and route reassignment to an accountable human, not merely make descendant Agents unusable indefinitely.
units.responsibilityConflict: The organization chain contains only Agents; no accountable-human role or formal responsibility contract determines who may restore or reassign work. Archival does not address active external execution, and mutable status/error rows do not prove capability revocation. Queued Runs for archived Companies are silently retained, leaving future execution semantics ambiguous.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres and controlled-WebSocket integration specification for serializing Issue-bound Agent execution, batching comment/approval/recovery wakes, promoting deferred work after terminal runs, and preserving the distinction between assignee execution ownership and mentioned-Agent participation.
units.dependencyDirection: The suite drives heartbeatService against real Company, Agent, Issue, comment, wake-request and run tables, process liveness state and an OpenClaw-compatible WebSocket adapter; the adapter boundary receives a rendered wake message while database projections control execution ownership and follow-up scheduling.
units.keyDataModels: HeartbeatRun execution/comment status and retryOfRunId, AgentWakeupRequest deferred status and embedded wake context, Issue assignee/execution/checkout/completion fields, IssueComment authorUserId/authorAgentId/createdByRunId/presentation/metadata, wake actor provenance, approval/recovery/comment/mention reasons, and ordered comment ID batches.
units.lifecycle: Wakes that arrive while an Issue has an active execution are persisted and coalesced rather than started concurrently; approval and recovery hand-backs wait for the current run; ordered comments are forwarded after success or cancellation; a finished Issue reopens only when a deferred batch contains an external human comment, not another Agent or the closing run's own comment; mentioned Agents may inspect without stealing assignment/execution ownership; a run that emits no Issue comment receives exactly one cheaper retry, while a real run-authored comment satisfies the communication requirement and automatic summary remains fallback-only.
units.testAssessment: Twelve broad integration cases cover approval/recovery deferral, ordered coalescing, cancellation and completion promotion, human-versus-Agent reopen behavior, mixed batches, bounded missing-comment retry, concurrent mention deferral, non-owning direct mentions and summary fallback. Tests exercise database and adapter concurrency but omit simultaneous claim/promotion races across service instances, transaction/outbox crash points, queue expiry/cancellation/revocation, deleted or edited comments, authorization and tenant-spoof resistance, oversized/adversarial batches, delivery acknowledgment and replay, Connector failure partitions, data-access effects of non-owner runs, and proof that approval/recovery payloads reference authoritative records. Human-versus-Agent semantics partly depend on authorUserId plus createdByRunId conventions rather than a typed principal.
units.designRationale: Prevent multiple Agents or reentrant events from executing the same Issue concurrently, preserve every follow-up while compressing wake noise, avoid self-generated completion comments reopening finished work, and require an Agent to leave a visible handoff rather than treating an adapter summary as sufficient collaboration evidence.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs durable human/Agent collaboration queues that do not lose input during execution, distinguish discussion from authority, prevent ownership theft, and preserve who requested, executed, reviewed and resumed each Work item.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the durable per-Work mailbox, ordered idempotent batching, single-executor lease, terminal promotion, non-owner participation role and bounded handoff retry. Model typed HumanPrincipal/AgentPrincipal/ConnectorPrincipal and explicit message purpose; a comment is collaboration input, not execution authorization. Reopen, resume or high-risk continuation must consume a capability or ApprovalDecision bound to Work/action/digest/responsibility/data contract. Non-owner mentions receive an inspection capability with least-privilege data/tool access. Publish queue and Work projections transactionally and retain delivery/acknowledgment evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: The fixtures set responsibleUserId but do not require that accountable human to authorize comment-triggered execution or reopen. An approval wake is accepted from payload/context without a persisted, action-bound approval receipt. Local CLI Agent comments can appear under authorUserId and are distinguished by createdByRunId, while any external human comment in a mixed batch reopens Work regardless of intent or role. A mentioned Agent avoids owning the Issue row but can still be dispatched, so row ownership alone does not enforce data/tool authority. Mandatory comments and system notices are communication artifacts, not verified evidence of result quality or responsibility discharge.

units.designRationale: Keep Agent instructions aligned with Work mode, avoid replaying stale approval state after a newer comment, reduce repeated prompt context on resumed sessions and protect list APIs from large nested Run payloads.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for blocker-aware wake admission, deferred dependency-resolution events, per-Agent concurrency queues, stale queued-run cancellation, and Issue-subtree pause handling.
units.dependencyDirection: The suite drives heartbeatService over Issue relations, tree holds, wake requests, run/execution-lock projections and Agent runtime configuration; dependency and hold policy are evaluated inside the scheduling service before a mocked adapter is invoked.
units.keyDataModels: Issue blocks relation and parent tree, IssueTreeHold mode/status/release policy, Agent heartbeat maxConcurrentRuns, AgentWakeupRequest queued/skipped/deferred states and idempotency key, HeartbeatRun queued/running/cancelled/result/error fields, Issue execution lock, and interaction context annotations.
units.lifecycle: A normal assignment to blocked Work is skipped without creating a Run, while a comment interaction may execute with unresolved-blocker context; completing a blocker permits a resolution wake, or defers it if the same Work already runs; excess Agent work remains queued; queued runs are revalidated and cancelled with their stale execution lock cleared when blockers persist; an active ancestor pause suppresses ordinary wakes at least 17 levels deep but permits a persisted human comment interaction, including under a legacy full_pause note.
units.testAssessment: Six integration cases cover blocker admission, interaction bypass, same-Work resolution deferral with idempotency, maxConcurrentRuns=1, dequeue-time dependency revalidation, execution-lock cleanup, deep tree-hold propagation and rejection of an Agent-forged comment wake. Missing are multiple/partially resolved blockers, cycles and cross-Company relations, dependency deletion/rewrite races, distributed scheduler concurrency and fairness, priority/starvation, queue expiry/cancellation, crash atomicity, lease fencing, hold release/revocation, authorization to create relations or holds, comment edits/deletion, and proof that an allowed interaction is technically restricted from tools/data mutations. The tests manually create a relation table, weakening migration/schema fidelity.
units.designRationale: Treat dependency and pause state as admission policy rather than prompt advice, re-check mutable blockers immediately before queued execution, preserve liveness when resolution occurs during a run, and keep human communication reachable even while automated work is paused.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a durable Work dependency graph, resource-aware scheduling and emergency pause controls that prevent unsafe execution without cutting off accountable-human communication or losing resumable intent.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the admission/dequeue double-check, idempotent deferred resolution, fenced per-principal concurrency limit, stale-run terminal receipt, lock cleanup and ancestor-hold projection. Separate CommunicationCapability from ExecutionCapability: a human message during a hold may update the mailbox or request review, but must not start a mutation-capable Agent runtime unless a distinct policy authorizes it. Define typed hold modes, dependency graph invariants, accountable owner, expiry/release authority, permission/data snapshots and event/outbox transitions; use a scheduler lease rather than process-local liveness.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId is present in most fixtures but never participates in blocker, hold, resume or cancellation authority. Caller-supplied wake context helps route work, while an allowed user comment starts the same adapter execution path even under pause/full_pause without a demonstrated read-only sandbox or tool/data restriction. Relations and holds lack tested creator authorization and responsibility-contract binding, and clearing mutable Issue locks is not an immutable cancellation/decision receipt.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for detecting stalled Issue dependency/review paths, repairing missed dependency wakes, and creating bounded, deduplicated liveness recovery Issues with ownership, budget, workspace and cooldown policy.
units.dependencyDirection: The Heartbeat reconciler reads Issue/relation/review, run, hold, workspace-operation, Agent hierarchy, budget/cost and settings state; it writes wake requests, recovery Issues, blocker relations, comments and activity projections, while attentionService exposes unresolved review decisions to a user feed.
units.keyDataModels: Liveness finding/reason and lookback, dependency readiness and idempotent wake key, workspace finalize operation, review-path recovery attempt, attention decision verb, harness_liveness_escalation Issue with originId/originFingerprint, Agent reportsTo hierarchy, budget policy/cost events, pause hold, recovery blocker relation and re-escalation cooldown.
units.lifecycle: Detection can remain advisory while a separate dependency-wake backstop still repairs resolved blockers; review-path loss gets one bounded automated retry before surfacing a stalled human decision; resolved dependencies wait for assignee and required workspace finalization, retry stale skipped wakes and avoid active duplicates; stalled leaf blockers inside lookback and outside holds/live paths create or reuse one recovery Issue assigned to a direct Agent or manager fallback, excluding budget-blocked candidates and execution workspace inheritance; closed recoveries detach from blocker relations, completed incidents cool down before re-escalation, while cancellation permits immediate retry.
units.testAssessment: Twenty-three substantial cases cover advisory mode, bounded review recovery and attention surfacing, dependency-wake compensation, assignee timing, stale retry, workspace-finalize gating, multi-blocker dedupe, disabled wake-on-demand classification, lookback/hold/live-path suppression, backlog and review failure classes, recovery reuse, Agent owner selection, budget fallback, workspace isolation, cooldown/cancellation and closed-relation cleanup. Missing are graph cycles and cross-Company corruption, simultaneous reconcilers and transactional/outbox crash points, database lease/fencing, falsified or zombie executionRunId, remote runtime attestation, cost-event trust, human authorization for recovery ownership, incident severity/SLA, notification delivery, recovery failure limits, permission/data-contract inheritance, large-graph query performance, and evidence that an existing recovery is actually progressing. Treating any active executionRunId or open recovery Issue as a live path can mask a stalled runtime.
units.designRationale: Use periodic reconciliation as a backstop for event-loss and state races, separate safe mechanical healing from optional auto-recovery, deduplicate incidents by stable leaf fingerprints, avoid recovery storms through bounded attempts and cooldowns, and keep recovery work isolated from production execution workspaces.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs an Agent Boss exception plane that detects stalled responsibility chains, repairs provably mechanical omissions, escalates ambiguous decisions to the right accountable human, and preserves incident evidence without creating recursive Agent work or hidden spend.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the independent reconciliation backstop, explicit advisory/automatic modes, workspace-finalize readiness, stable incident fingerprint, bounded attempt/cooldown, shared-root dedupe, budget-aware candidate filtering, stale relation cleanup and user attention projection. Split MechanicallyRepairableInvariant from ResponsibilityIncident: only deterministic, evidence-backed repairs may run automatically; other findings create an immutable incident assigned to the accountable human with severity, SLA, exact Work/runtime/permission/data evidence and explicit decision capabilities. Runtime liveness requires Connector attestation/lease, not a row ID. Keep incidents out of the business dependency graph or project them through a typed relation, and never choose a cheap model as authority for responsibility decisions.
units.responsibilityConflict: Most escalation fixtures have no responsibleUserId or human membership involved in the decision; recovery ownership is assigned to a direct or manager Agent, and a low-cost model override is treated as the response path. A recovery Issue is inserted as another blocker, so operational incident state mutates business dependency semantics. Lookback can silently leave old findings advisory, open recovery rows or mutable executionRunId can suppress escalation without progress proof, and activity/comments do not constitute an immutable human decision or evidence receipt.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for suppressing repeated Issue-bound wakes after consecutive successful runs with no Issue-visible progress, while reopening admission for new human input, failures or scoped progress.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat admission queries recent terminal Runs and activity-log events for the target Issue, then either persists a skipped AgentWakeupRequest with throttle metadata or proceeds to the normal adapter execution path.
units.keyDataModels: Issue-scoped terminal Run history and finish time, no-progress streak, nextAllowedAt cooldown, Wake reason/request actor, ActivityLog actor/run/action/entity provenance, resume intent and Issue-visible progress.
units.lifecycle: Two recent successful no-progress Runs suppress another event-free assignment and record the streak/cooldown; a later user comment activity admits work without first breaking the streak through execution; system comment wakes bypass the throttle, Agent-authored comments and explicit resume remain suppressed unless new human input exists; a failed latest Run or same-Issue run-linked comment admits retry, cross-Issue activity does not; long Runs count by terminal time within the lookback.
units.testAssessment: Eight focused integration cases cover streak threshold, cooldown receipt, new user input, system and Agent comment distinctions, explicit Agent resume, failure recovery, same-versus-cross-Issue progress and long-run lookback semantics. Missing are concurrent admission races, database uniqueness/lease fencing, clock skew, exact window boundaries, queued/running Runs, cancellation/timeouts, repeated failures, high-risk approval events, user/Agent impersonation, edited/deleted comments, authoritative comment existence, progress types beyond comments, Connector evidence, configurable policy and starvation/notification behavior. One test admits a system comment wake with a random commentId and no persisted comment, so it does not prove source authenticity.
units.designRationale: Reduce cost and noise from Agents repeatedly waking on unchanged Work, while treating genuinely new external input, failure recovery and Work-scoped visible output as evidence that another attempt may be useful.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs loop and spend containment that does not suppress accountable-human intervention, approval resolution or new evidence, and must explain why a Work item was throttled and how it can resume.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the Work-scoped no-progress streak, explicit cooldown receipt, finish-time window, cross-Work isolation and priority for verified external input. Compute admission from immutable Message/Approval/Evidence cursors and Connector attempt receipts, with typed outcome classes and per-risk policy. A comment is communication, not necessarily progress; require a semantic ProgressReceipt or changed evidence/result projection. Human bypass must reference an authenticated principal and persisted message/decision, while failure retries use separate bounded backoff/circuit-breaker policy. Use atomic compare-and-set or a scheduler lease for distributed admission.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId is recorded but not consulted. User versus Agent significance is inferred from mutable activity-log actor labels, a system comment wake can bypass without an authoritative comment, and any Issue-visible comment can count as progress without proving result or responsibility discharge. The skipped wake carries operational metadata but no accountable owner, notification/override decision, permission/data snapshot or evidence digest.

units.lifecycle: List can return a lightweight row with usage, result, session, log, external-run and process fields nulled while retaining core status/error/context; getRun preserves small arbitrary result JSON but replaces oversized legacy payloads with a bounded summary/stdout and truncation receipt; event payloads retain bounded prompt/context metadata; an undefined linked-schema field maps processGroupId to null.

units.designRationale: Keep run lists fast and bounded, retain detail fidelity for normal payloads, prevent legacy rows or adapter events from creating unbounded API/storage amplification, and tolerate staged application/schema rollout.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs separate operational summaries and permission-scoped evidence details across cloud and local deployments without leaking prompts, private sessions, credentials, raw external identifiers or large provider payloads.

units.responsibilityConflict: The projection has no accountable-human or responsibility-contract fields. getRun accepts only a Run ID at this service boundary and tests do not establish Company/role authorization. Small arbitrary result JSON, error text, context snapshots and truncated prompts may still contain secrets or private reasoning; truncation limits volume but does not create authorized evidence or provenance.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres end-to-end tests for automatically provisioning the default Local execution environment, leasing it to a Heartbeat Run, releasing the lease, and injecting Paperclip control-plane identity variables into a process adapter.
units.dependencyDirection: heartbeatService selects/creates an Environment, records an EnvironmentLease, launches the process adapter on the server host, injects run-scoped environment variables and a generated API credential, then updates Run context and releases the lease.
units.keyDataModels: Instance-scoped Local Environment, Run-bound EnvironmentLease status/provider/releasedAt, Run context environment projection, process command/arguments, Agent/Company/Run identifiers, API URL and PAPERCLIP_API_KEY generated from a server JWT secret.
units.lifecycle: An on-demand process Run creates or reuses one default Local environment, acquires a lease, executes an arbitrary configured host process, records environment/lease identifiers in context, releases the lease at terminal success, and exposes Agent, Company, Run, API URL and an API key in the child process environment.
units.testAssessment: Two end-to-end cases prove happy-path Local environment creation, lease release and expected process environment injection. Missing are concurrent/exclusive lease behavior, crash/kill/timeout/cancellation, orphan detection and expiry, server restart, failed acquisition/release, host filesystem/network/process isolation, command authorization, environment inheritance and secret leakage, token claims/audience/scope/TTL/revocation/rotation, per-Work permission and data contracts, remote execution attestation, cleanup of the created temp directory, and non-local drivers. Credential presence is asserted, but its least privilege is not.
units.designRationale: Give every Run an explicit execution-environment lifecycle even for simple local development, expose enough identity for the Agent to call back into the control plane, and retain a lease record for cleanup and observability.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs interchangeable local/customer/cloud execution nodes with fenced leases, short-lived runtime identity and auditable capability/data boundaries, without assuming the control plane may execute arbitrary commands on its own host.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit EnvironmentPort, acquire/renew/release lease lifecycle and Run-bound environment attestation. Treat host-local process execution as an opt-in development adapter, never the production default. Issue a one-time, short-TTL, audience-bound RuntimeCapability token containing exact Work/attempt/Connector/tool/data scopes and proof key; keep the signing secret outside child environments, support revocation and renewal, redact all process output, and require sandbox/network/filesystem policy plus crash-safe lease fencing. units.responsibilityConflict: The fixture has responsibleUserId but no human authorization or responsibility contract controls the host command or credential issuance. A generic API key is injected into an arbitrary process and the test does not prove least privilege, while a successful process exit is treated as sufficient lifecycle success without result/evidence validation. Local lease state provides observability, not runtime isolation or legal/business accountability.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres regression tests for cross-Agent reassignment while another Agent owns an Issue execution lock, including deferral behind a running holder and optimistic cancellation protection when a queued holder is concurrently claimed.
units.dependencyDirection: heartbeatService reads mutable Issue execution ownership and Run status to defer the new assignee; the race regression directly exercises the conditional database UPDATE shape used to cancel a stale queued holder.
units.keyDataModels: Issue assigneeAgentId versus executionRunId/executionAgentNameKey/executionLockedAt, holder HeartbeatRun queued/running/cancelled state and error code, original/new AgentWakeupRequest status, and requested actor metadata.
units.lifecycle: If Work is already running under the previous Agent after reassignment, the new Agent wake is persisted as deferred and the current Run/lock is left untouched; for a holder observed queued, cancellation is conditional on that exact status, so a concurrent queued-to-running claim prevents cancellation and retains the holder and Issue lock.
units.testAssessment: Two focused database tests cover running-holder deferral and a compare-on-status race guard. They do not cover the actual queued-holder cancellation through heartbeatService, promotion of the deferred new assignee, terminal handoff, process/Connector cancellation acknowledgment, session/tool/token revocation, workspace ownership, evidence preservation, reassignment authorization, repeated/ABA state transitions, distributed fencing, transaction/outbox crash points, timeout or old Agent completion after reassignment. The race is simulated by issuing the production-shaped UPDATE manually rather than interleaving service transactions.
units.designRationale: Avoid concurrent Agents executing the same Issue and prevent a reassignment cleanup path from clobbering a Run that another worker has just claimed.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must transfer responsibility and execution authority between Agents or humans without double execution, stale credentials, lost evidence or ambiguity over whether the previous attempt may finish.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the compare-and-set guard and deferred successor queue, but model reassignment as a versioned HandoffDecision. Use a fenced ExecutionLease generation bound to Work, responsibility contract, Agent, permissions/data contract and runtime attestation; select an explicit policy to let-finish, cancel-and-wait or force-revoke, require Connector acknowledgment/timeout, revoke runtime capabilities, freeze evidence, and only then activate the successor. Persist immutable requested/approved/effective handoff receipts through a transaction/outbox.
units.responsibilityConflict: The Issue assignee already points to Reviewer while Coder continues executing, with no accountable-human handoff decision or indication whether old authority remains valid. The requestedBy user is not authorization-tested, the running holder's capabilities are not revoked, and mutable row/status predicates provide concurrency safety but not responsibility-chain continuity or external-runtime fencing.

units.function: Unit/integration tests for authenticated managed Git checkout materialization, concurrent clone serialization, atomic installation, failure cleanup and credential-environment preservation.
units.dependencyDirection: ensureManagedProjectWorkspace derives a Company/Project checkout path, optionally calls a Git auth provider, invokes Git with a sanitized environment and scoped credential helper, atomically renames a temporary clone and returns a workspace; git-credentials owns host gating, secret-to-invocation conversion and error scrubbing.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Project/repository checkout identity, optional GitRemoteAuthProvider result, company-secret token source/name, URL-scoped credential-helper config, token environment variable, in-process materialization promise map, temporary/target checkout paths and operator warning.
units.lifecycle: No provider or null credentials preserves ordinary cloning; a supported credential is passed only through a child environment to a GitHub-HTTPS-scoped helper, never URL/argv/disk; same-process concurrent materializations share one promise, while temp-sibling clone plus atomic rename tolerates a cross-process winner; failures remove temp/target remnants and classify auth-shaped errors without exposing credential text; pre-existing Git or non-empty non-Git paths are adopted without cloning.
units.testAssessment: Eight cases cover no/null auth, non-auth error attribution, same-process concurrency, unauthenticated errors, failure cleanup, preserving an existing non-Git directory and sanitizer spread order. Related implementation adds two host/protocol gates, clears ambient helpers, disables prompts, sets a clone timeout and scrubs URL credentials. Missing are real authenticated Git server tests, token leakage assertions over process lists/logs/core dumps, secret TTL/rotation/revocation, multi-instance locks, crash between clone/rename, disk permissions/symlink attacks, remote identity verification for existing checkouts, malicious pre-existing directories, repository URL mutation, Git LFS/submodules, GHES/GitLab/Gitee and audit receipts. Tests do not prove that the selected company secret is authorized for this Work or repository.
units.designRationale: Provide private-repository access without embedding tokens in persistent Git state, serialize common clone races, install only complete workspaces and give actionable but correctly attributed failures.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs brokered, least-privilege source-data access for local and cloud execution nodes while preventing credential exfiltration, stale workspace adoption and cross-tenant repository confusion.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT—and consider source-level reuse after license/provenance review—the URL/argv/disk avoidance, ambient-helper clearing, double host/protocol validation, noninteractive timeout, error scrubbing, temp clone and atomic rename. Generalize behind CredentialBrokerPort and WorkspacePort for GitHub/GHES/GitLab/Gitee/enterprise Git; issue short-lived repository/action-scoped credentials on the execution node, bind them to Work/data authorization and record a secret-free access receipt. Replace the process-local promise map with a fenced filesystem/database lease, reject or quarantine non-Git paths, and verify existing checkout remote URL, commit trust and ownership before adoption.
units.responsibilityConflict: The secret source is Company-scoped but not bound to accountable human, Work, data contract or exact repository action. A pre-existing path may silently override the requested repository, and successful clone establishes filesystem state rather than authorized evidence. Secret name in diagnostic text is operationally useful but should itself be policy-controlled metadata.

units.function: Pure tests for requesting the single built-in cheap model profile, resolving adapter and Agent runtime patches, merging Issue-level adapter overrides, normalizing wake context and classifying model-not-found as non-retryable configuration failure.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat reads the shared global profile-key enum, asks the adapter registry for profile definitions, merges adapter-private configuration bags with Agent runtime and Issue overrides, and records request/application/fallback metadata in Run context/result.
units.keyDataModels: Global ModelProfileKey=cheap, adapter profile definition/label/source/config bag, Agent runtime profile enabled/configured state, Issue or wake-context request source, applied/fallback metadata, merged adapter config and configuration error code.
units.lifecycle: Issue override wins over wake context; an advertised adapter profile is enabled by default unless Agent runtime disables it, and Agent profile fields shallow-override adapter defaults; final Issue adapter config shallow-overrides both; unsupported profiles silently use primary config with a fallback reason; wake payload is copied to context; model_not_found avoids generic retry.
units.testAssessment: Six concise cases cover Codex preserving its primary model when cheap has no model patch, merge precedence, Agent customization, unsupported fallback, wake normalization and non-retryable model-not-found. Missing are authorization to choose/override models, typed capability and safety constraints, provider/model availability drift, data residency/export, regional endpoint, price/version/budget, context/tool limits, fallback consent, risk-class restrictions, approval-policy protection, secret/provider isolation, immutable selection evidence, dynamic profiles, concurrent config changes and end-to-end provider execution. The global domain currently permits only cheap and uses arbitrary adapter-private config objects.
units.designRationale: Offer a small cost-oriented execution hint without hardcoding a replacement model for adapters that cannot safely provide one, preserve explicit Work overrides and avoid retry loops for missing configuration.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral, policy-governed model selection across Chinese, global and enterprise-hosted providers, with explainable fallback, cost control and data/security constraints independent of adapter-specific configuration.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Preserve the useful ideas of explicit request source, applied-versus-requested receipt and non-retryable configuration errors, but replace cheap and shallow config merging with ModelRequirement, ProviderCapability, ModelDeployment, SelectionPolicy and SelectionDecision contracts. Resolve through ModelProviderPort using Company/Work/risk/data-residency/budget/tool/context requirements; protect safety and approval policy from Work-level overrides; require explicit fallback policy and record provider/model/version/pricing/policy digests. Adapter-private fields remain inside the adapter translation layer.
units.responsibilityConflict: Neither responsible human nor authorization policy participates in model selection. A wake payload or Issue can request a profile, Issue adapter config has highest precedence over fields such as approvalPolicy, and unsupported requests silently fall back to primary. The Run receipt lacks data authorization, risk, cost contract, policy version and accountable approver, so it cannot explain whether the selected model was legally or organizationally permitted.

units.designRationale: Make execution infrastructure extensible through plugin drivers, keep per-run adapter context visible to the provider, offer an instance-wide operational default with Agent-level exceptions, and prevent stale workspace metadata from overriding current assignment policy.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a neutral ExecutionEnvironmentPort spanning managed cloud, customer-local and hybrid nodes, with tenant isolation, data-egress policy, attestation and explicit selection precedence independent of any Agent vendor.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the capability-declared driver, typed acquire/release lease contract, per-attempt identity and explicit selection receipt. units.function: A 6,889-line PostgreSQL integration suite exercising Paperclip's process/run recovery, hot restart, graceful shutdown, stranded Issue reconciliation, durable retry, interaction continuation, approval resumption, workspace/secret preflight, missing-disposition handoff and recovery escalation paths.
units.dependencyDirection: The suite enters through heartbeatService but reaches across Runs, wakeups, Issues/comments/relations, recovery actions, interactions, holds, Agents, secrets, workspaces, environments/leases, budgets, documents/work products, hot-restart snapshots, local process supervision and telemetry. It also launches real child processes/process groups while mocking adapters, telemetry and selected termination hooks.
units.keyDataModels: HeartbeatRun and contextSnapshot retry metadata; AgentWakeupRequest; Issue assignment/checkout/execution linkage; IssueRecoveryAction and source-scoped evidence; IssueInteraction; Company/Agent responsibility fields; pause holds; execution workspace and environment lease; document/work-product progress; hot-restart process identity and snapshot markers.
units.lifecycle: Protect live work owned by another service instance; classify lost/succeeded/failed/interrupted runs; retry only bounded, cause-matched continuations; persist scheduled retries across restart; adopt or drain eligible processes during hot restart; release locks and leases; require durable external-wait or disposition evidence; avoid nested recovery; create or reuse a canonical source-scoped recovery action; pause or escalate when no live path remains.
units.testAssessment: Exceptionally broad regression evidence accumulated through more than fifty commits and many real failure classes. Strong cases cover cross-instance protection, exact run/interaction binding, restart persistence, retry caps by cause, secret redaction, race deduplication, recovery recursion prevention, pause-hold exemption and durable-wait validation. The monolithic fixture is nevertheless expensive and highly coupled: one file spans host-process behavior, database orchestration, domain policy, recovery presentation copy and adapter-specific details; numerous assertions depend on English notice strings and mutable multi-table side effects.
units.designRationale: Paperclip treats recovery as a backstop control loop over persisted execution state rather than trusting process exit alone. It distinguishes a productive terminal run from a genuinely live continuation path, requires durable wait evidence, bounds automated retries, and keeps repeated failures attached to one canonical source incident.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs the same failure knowledge across managed-cloud and self-hosted execution: exact-once or idempotent recovery, Connector loss, restart adoption, approval/interaction continuation, durable waits, evidence redaction and human-visible escalation without losing the responsibility chain.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the scenario catalogue and invariants, not this test file or schema. Split Company OS coverage into Connector execution-lease compatibility tests, durable retry/outbox tests, Approval/Interaction continuation tests, Responsibility/RecoveryCase aggregate tests, and deployment-profile restart tests. General runtime proof must use short-lived secret-free Connector attestation rather than host PID; every retry or escalation must bind accountable human, authority/data/approval contract digests and evidence/result identity.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip can assign orphan blockers and recovery ownership to an Agent, infer recent Agent comments as progress, and perform several sequential Issue/comment/activity/wakeup mutations without an explicit accountable-human decision or atomic durable publication contract. Its default responsibleUserId is present in fixtures but is not consistently the authority or approver governing recovery actions. English issue copy and host process metadata also leak into behavior assertions instead of stable domain codes and verifiable receipts.

units.function: Large mixed unit specification for execution environment/secret layering, low-trust credential gates, Codex-local authentication preflight, run-scoped Skill mentions, referenced-project authorization/synchronization/observability, workspace hints and managed project directory isolation.

units.lifecycle: Environment, Agent, Project and Routine env are resolved with later layers overriding earlier values and secret IDs unioned; PAPERCLIP_API_KEY bindings are dropped while other PAPERCLIP-prefixed names remain; required user bindings fail before resolution and low-trust inline sensitive values are rejected/allowlisted; Git push checks for named credentials at Agent/Project scope; local Codex checks per-Agent API key or shared host subscription auth but sandbox targets skip the host gate; mentioned Skills are deduplicated and appended; authorized referenced Projects are resolved independently, failures warn while remaining work continues, remote targets drop all local staging, and valid configured/managed workspaces become adapter path hints in isolated sibling directories.
units.testAssessment: Thirty-five tests cover precedence, secret manifests, reserved-key stripping, absent layers, low-trust binding propagation, required user secrets, inline sensitive denial, push key presence, Codex local/sandbox/shared auth, Skill ID/version behavior, referenced-project feature gating/authorization/partial failures/remote staging/observability/hints, missing/empty workspace sources, managed clone fallback and path non-nesting. Missing are real Secret/authorization/database/filesystem integration across most helpers; mutation/override authorization; semantic env schemas and future reserved-name collisions; secret TTL/audience/permission verification; Git token repository/write scope; sandbox credential provenance; cross-Company shared Codex auth isolation; data classification/export and mandatory-versus-optional referenced inputs; repo ref checkout/integrity; symlink/path traversal; workspace remote verification; Skill trust/signature/capability authorization; failure policy and immutable selection/evidence receipts.
units.designRationale: Centralize run preparation so configuration is deterministic and inspectable, resolve secrets only at execution time, constrain low-trust runs, fail early on missing credentials, allow optional cross-project context without making one clone failure fatal, and prevent managed Project directories from nesting or colliding.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs enterprise data authorization and export control across layered configuration, human-owned secrets, tools/Skills and multiple project data sources, while supporting cloud/local execution without leaking vendor credentials or silently changing Work semantics.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as separate canonical components, not one Heartbeat helper: ConfigurationPolicy resolves typed non-secret settings; CredentialBrokerPort issues short-lived action/resource-scoped capabilities and secret-free manifests; DataAuthorizationContract classifies each required/optional source and egress; Tool/Skill capability admission verifies publisher/version/signature; WorkspacePort stages content-addressed sources and attestations. Preserve deterministic precedence, pre-resolution missing-binding checks, low-trust allowlists, structured partial-failure observability and non-nested paths. Replace key-name presence with verified provider capabilities, forbid inline secrets at every trust level, reserve an explicit namespace, isolate all user/provider auth per Company, and require the Work policy to choose fail-closed versus optional continuation for missing referenced Projects.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId appears only in missing-secret diagnostics and does not approve environment precedence, shared host authentication, Git write access, Skills or additional Project disclosure. A plaintext GH_TOKEN can satisfy push preflight without proving scope; sandbox credentials are assumed; shared Codex auth may fund or identify multiple Companies; partial project loss still executes; local cwd/repository hints enter Agent context without an immutable data contract. These are configuration conveniences, not a complete responsibility/evidence chain.

units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat mention resolution reads Project links from Issue sources, loads Company-scoped Projects, treats the anchor as already authorized by the parent Work path, asks AuthorizationService for project:read on additional candidates, then returns admitted Project records and human-readable warnings to workspace preparation.

units.lifecycle: Cross-Project sync is on unless explicitly disabled; the anchor is removed from mentions and not re-authorized; unavailable/foreign Projects are dropped before authorization, denials or authorization errors are dropped with warnings while the Run continues; only admitted Projects consume the materialization cap, only available candidates consume the evaluation cap, and evaluation fan-out is bounded under mention floods.
units.testAssessment: Fifteen cases cover feature parsing, driver classification, same-Company admission, anchor dedupe, foreign/unavailable filtering, deny/exception fail-closed behavior, admitted/evaluation caps, denied-first and unavailable-first ordering, flood behavior and cap invariants. Missing are authentication of mention authors, Project/file/data classification, anchor authorization proof, authorization decision version/expiry/revocation, mandatory versus optional source semantics, stable structured failures in this resolver, concurrent Project/permission changes, large real Issue sources, query plans, audit receipts and end-to-end workspace content integrity. Mention order can consume the evaluation window with denied candidates and displace a later authorized source.
units.designRationale: Allow Agents to draw on explicitly mentioned same-Company Projects while enforcing read policy and bounding database/authorization/materialization work under malicious or accidental mention floods.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explicit multi-source DataAuthorizationContracts and egress controls so Agents can use approved company knowledge without a mention silently widening their accessible data surface.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT Company prefiltering, per-source authorization, separate evaluation/admission limits, anchor dedupe, fail-closed decisions and structured omission reporting. Make cross-source access opt-in through a versioned Work data contract that identifies required/optional sources, file/query scope, classification, purpose, retention, destination and accountable approver. Snapshot authorization decisions and source digests at dispatch; required-source denial fails the Work, optional denial produces a typed degraded-mode decision. Prevent mention-order starvation with deterministic policy priority or explicit selection rather than first-N text order.
units.responsibilityConflict: A mention plus Agent project:read is sufficient to widen context; no accountable human approves the disclosure or degraded execution. The anchor bypasses this resolver's authorization, overall work continues after denied/error sources, and warnings are not immutable data-access receipts. Default-on behavior is unsuitable for enterprise data boundaries without a Company policy contract.

units.designRationale: Permit multi-Project context only when the remote transport claims per-tree confinement, keep a rapid rollback switch and preserve authorization/fan-out limits on the new remote path.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS hybrid deployments need safe, provable staging of authorized data from the control plane or customer node into an execution sandbox, with complete export and deletion evidence.

Workspace paths are operational hints, not evidence of what data crossed the boundary.

units.lifecycle: Classify a terminal failure; persist a scheduled_retry Run and paired wakeup; honor provider reset hints or bounded delay; coalesce duplicate schedules; promote only when due and still owning the exact Issue lock; cancel on reassignment, human handoff, terminal/non-progress status, budget or dependency change; cap retries and record exhaustion; quarantine only the currently attached, source-owned failed workspace.

units.designRationale: Retries are durable control-plane work, not in-memory timers. Scheduling and execution are separated so the system can survive restart and revalidate mutable ownership immediately before promotion.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral, restart-safe retry orchestration that never repeats a high-risk action under stale human ownership, approval, data authorization or Connector identity.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the durable schedule/promote split, cause-specific policy, provider retry hint, unique idempotency key and promotion-time fencing. Implement a RetryPolicyPort over a transactional ExecutionAttempt/Outbox boundary; bind retries to Work, Connector capability/version, accountable human, authority/data/approval contract digests and previous evidence/result. Vendor fallback ladders belong inside Connector adapters, not the application scheduler.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip revalidates Issue assignment and execution lock but not the exact responsible human acceptance, authority scope, approval receipt or data contract. units.function: A 1,647-line embedded-PostgreSQL integration suite for suppressing non-actionable timers and invalidating queued Runs when budget, assignment, task status, execution lock, review participant or continuation intent changes before adapter execution.

units.keyDataModels: Agent heartbeat policy and lastHeartbeatAt; WakeupRequest queued/skipped/coalesced/deferred states; HeartbeatRun execution/retry metadata; Issue assignee/status/executionRunId/executionState; daily Run and cost observations; continuation-summary document.

units.designRationale: A queue entry is only an intention. Mutable work and policy state must be revalidated immediately before external execution, and stale holders must release their lock so the next eligible participant can proceed.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must ensure an Agent cannot execute using stale responsibility, approval, data authorization, budget or assignment after waiting in a queue, across both managed and local execution nodes.

Represent wait/review/interaction state as structured codes and receipts, never parse presentation Markdown.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip rechecks Agent assignment and review participant but not the accountable human's active acceptance or the exact approval/data contract. An interactionResolvedAt marker can bypass a prior review park without demonstrating the approver, authorized action/digest or evidence binding. Daily cost/run caps are Agent-local policy and can race because no reservation is established before execution.

units.function: A 1,208-line real-Git plus embedded-PostgreSQL integration suite for rejecting projectless isolated worktrees, containing recorded-versus-actual branch divergence at realize/restore/finalize boundaries, and optionally reconciling provably forward-only changes.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat execution crosses Git process calls, Project/workspace policy, persisted ExecutionWorkspace, Runs/wakeups, multiple related Issues, recovery actions/comments, workspace operations, activity records and adapter context; instance feature flags govern isolated workspaces and auto-forward reconciliation.
units.keyDataModels: Project execution-workspace policy; ProjectWorkspace and ExecutionWorkspace recorded branch/path; Issue workspace binding and execution locks; versioned workspace_incoherence fingerprint; expected/actual refs and HEAD SHAs, cleanliness and ancestry verdict; source-scoped RecoveryAction and WorkspaceOperation.
units.lifecycle: Fail before Run creation when a git-worktree request lacks a Project; validate branch identity on fresh reuse, persisted restore and post-adapter finalization; block only the source Issue, release related execution locks, create one fingerprinted recovery action and notice on unsafe divergence; when enabled, accept only clean forward ancestry, reconcile the durable workspace record, record an operation/activity and resolve a matching recovery action.
units.testAssessment: Real Git fixtures and database assertions provide strong end-to-end evidence across pre-dispatch and post-execution call sites, SHA provenance, divergent-versus-forward ancestry, sibling scoping and recovery linkage. Weaknesses include a 1,208-line fixture, duplicate stable-stringify/fingerprint logic in test, absolute paths inside fingerprints, English copy assertions, no concurrent branch mutation/race, remote/submodule/LFS/symlink cases, rollback after partial reconciliation, authorization of the feature flag, or proof that all sibling lock releases and recovery writes are atomic.
units.designRationale: Never let an Agent continue in a worktree whose durable branch identity no longer matches Git reality; permit automatic repair only when Git proves the actual branch is a clean forward continuation of the recorded branch.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS local execution needs tamper-evident workspace provenance and containment so evidence/results cannot be attributed to the wrong code or data snapshot.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the multi-boundary validation, canonical provenance digest, fail-closed divergence and forward-only proof. units.function: An 866-line unit/integration suite for shared-project-workspace concurrency policy, detecting a live holder, deferring contending Runs through scheduled retries, or allowing concurrent execution with injected coordination prose.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat execution resolves Instance policy, Agent environment driver, ProjectWorkspace and Issue workspace settings; it reads live Runs/lastOutputAt, writes cancelled and scheduled retry Runs/wakeups/Issue locks, and passes coordination text into the adapter context.
units.keyDataModels: ProjectWorkspace identity/CWD; Issue sharedWorkspaceConcurrency auto/serialize/allow and isolated mode; holder Run/Issue; workspace_busy result evidence; scheduled retry attempt/reason; environment driver and instance execution mode.
units.lifecycle: Classify a shared workspace holder by workspace identity and recent Run activity; auto mode permits local concurrency but serializes sandbox/Kubernetes, serialize always waits, allow always proceeds; cancellation schedules a jittered retry and transfers the assignee's execution lock; promotion revalidates reassignment; retry after holder completion; ignore isolated/different/stale holders; continue deferring for an unbounded number of attempts while a holder appears live.
units.testAssessment: Fourteen substantive cases plus delay-window tests cover policy modes, environment resolution, assignee/non-assignee retries, lock preservation, workspace identity, stale holder threshold, reassignment and repeated deferrals. Missing are simultaneous first-acquire races, database uniqueness/fencing, holder cancellation/lease proof, crash/restart, filesystem/git conflict outcomes, bounded total wait/attempts, starvation/fairness, human override authorization and destructive-action risk. The tests explicitly establish that retries continue beyond ten attempts despite the bounded naming.
units.designRationale: Avoid concurrent mutation of a shared workspace when the selected execution environment cannot safely coordinate, while preserving throughput for explicitly allowed/local collaborative workflows.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must prevent two Agents or humans from mutating the same enterprise resource/workspace under conflicting Work, data and approval contracts, across local and managed execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT only the explicit concurrency-policy and retry observability concepts. Require an atomic ResourceLeasePort acquisition with fencing token, holder Work/contract identity, expiry/renewal and cancellation proof before replacement. Default serialize for mutable resources; concurrent mode must require a declared merge/transaction protocol and risk policy, not prompt prose. Bound total wait/attempts and escalate to the accountable human with structured evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: Local auto mode authorizes simultaneous mutation merely by injecting English coordination instructions. A silent holder is ignored without revoking its authority, and a non-assignee retry may execute without an explicit responsibility/approval contract. Repeated deferrals can continue indefinitely, hiding stalled responsibility rather than escalating it.

units.function: A 538-line real-Git and embedded-PostgreSQL integration suite for finalizing managed workspaces after an Agent switches away from the recorded branch.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat realizes an isolated Git workspace, invokes an adapter, observes Agent-side Git and Issue/workspace mutations, runs finalization repair/adoption and persists WorkspaceOperation metadata plus Run/runtime state.
units.keyDataModels: ExecutionWorkspace recorded branch; actual Git branch/commits; Work/Issue status; worktree_prepare and workspace_finalize operations with validation/repair metadata.
units.lifecycle: If an unrecorded branch switch has no new commits, checkout the recorded branch before finalization; if it is a clean forward branch with commits, adopt that branch for the finalization operation without changing the durable workspace record; if the transition was already recorded, accept it directly; in all three cases persist operation evidence and allow the successful Run.
units.testAssessment: Three end-to-end cases use real Git and verify Run outcome, resulting branch/record and structured workspace operations. Missing are dirty/untracked/conflicted/diverged/detached HEAD, concurrent mutation, failed checkout/adoption, rollback after operation write failure, exact commit/tree evidence on the final Result, authorization for an Agent to update the workspace record, remote push/publication and restart between adapter exit and finalization.
units.designRationale: Preserve a coherent managed-workspace baseline while accepting legitimate forward work performed on a new publish branch and recording how finalization resolved the mismatch.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must bind every code/data result to the exact finalized workspace snapshot even when a Connector changes branches or produces a derivative workspace during execution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the post-execution validation and structured operation receipt. The ResultReceipt must name immutable commit/tree/content digests and the workspace lease epoch; branch labels are presentation only. A Connector may propose a transition but cannot update durable workspace identity directly: WorkspacePort validates and applies an authorized transition, with approval when risk policy requires it and an atomic audit outbox.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip treats a successful adapter plus clean forward ancestry as sufficient for automatic finalization, without binding the branch transition to accountable-human authority or an approval/action digest. One test allows the Agent path to update ExecutionWorkspace directly, and another intentionally finalizes a branch not persisted as the workspace's durable branch, which can make later responsibility reconstruction ambiguous unless the exact commit is preserved elsewhere.

units.function: A 2,913-line mixed unit/real-Git suite covering local workspace identity guards, Git-worktree base readiness, credential scrubbing, push preflight, low-trust sandbox isolation, workspace reuse/config freshness, task-session reset/fingerprints, comment wake batching, explicit provider session resume, session-state poisoning defenses, warnings, candidate ordering, compaction and sync-conflict classification.
units.dependencyDirection: Tests many helpers exported from the monolithic Heartbeat service plus Codex codec, filesystem/Git, Agent/workspace/trust shapes. The application layer directly knows local paths, adapter names, Git, provider session formats, Skill keys and internal metadata keys.
units.keyDataModels: Resolved and persisted ExecutionWorkspace; ProjectWorkspace and Git strategy; low-trust boundary/root Issue; versioned workspace/session config fingerprints and safe change categories; TaskSession params/display/lastRun; wake context/comment IDs; provider codec; session compaction policy.
units.lifecycle: Fail local Git-sensitive execution on workspace/project/path/providerRef/branch/metadata mismatch; reject invalid worktree bases and surface materialization cause; redact Git URL credentials; require an explicit PR-workflow Skill and push remote; fail low-trust non-sandbox work before workspace side effects; migrate only matching fallback sessions; fingerprint effective workspace/session configuration, reuse/refresh/replace deterministically and fail explicit restore loudly; reset or defer sessions by wake/config changes; strip control-plane metadata before adapter invocation; validate provider resume state and discard poisoned Hermes identifiers.
units.testAssessment: More than one hundred focused cases encode unusually rich operational lessons: fail-before-side-effect low-trust checks, explicit Skill capability rather than issue-text inference, fallback-cause fidelity, safe config category receipts, instruction content drift without content retention, no raw secret/env values in fingerprints, immutable explicit reuse, provider codec validation and poison fallback. The suite is nevertheless a 2,913-line architectural catch-all with extensive vendor and filesystem assumptions. Missing or weak areas include remote Connector attestation, cross-platform paths/Git, symlink/path traversal, push authorization rather than mere remote presence, config fingerprint canonicalization compatibility, collision/version migration, general session validation for non-Hermes adapters, data-retention/privacy policy, concurrent reuse, and end-to-end enforcement of all pure helpers.
units.designRationale: A Run may reuse mutable workspace and provider session state only when their effective configuration and identity still match. Low-trust work must be sandboxed before any host mutation, and persisted metadata should detect relevant drift without storing secret values or instruction contents.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral execution-context freshness and containment across managed/local Connectors: exact workspace/data snapshot, trust boundary, secret/version changes, model/Skill configuration and opaque provider sessions must not silently cross responsibility contracts.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the invariant catalogue, safe category fingerprints, fail-before-side-effect low-trust gate, explicit capability preflight, immutable explicit reuse and codec-based session validation. Split ownership into WorkspacePort, TrustPolicyPort, SessionPort and Connector compatibility tests. Bind fingerprints to Work/accountable human/authority/data/approval/Skill/Connector versions; use opaque resource IDs instead of host paths; require remote attestation for non-local execution; keep vendor session parsing entirely in adapters and never persist private reasoning.
units.responsibilityConflict: Non-local execution bypasses the local Git guard without a tested remote attestation contract; a configured push remote is treated as capability without proving credential scope or human approval; low-trust policy is rooted in Issue ancestry but not a data-authorization/export contract. Non-Hermes arbitrary session IDs are accepted unchanged, and core Heartbeat logic contains vendor-specific session/compaction policy. Several warnings and decisions are English strings rather than stable codes, while automatic workspace/session migration is not tied to explicit accountable-human acceptance.

units.lifecycle: Treat only untracked running Runs as zombies; filter them from coalescing so a new queued Run can be created instead of refreshing the dead Run timestamp.
units.testAssessment: Thirteen readable unit cases cover running/queued/terminal/null, post-restart and mixed live/zombie cases. units.function: Mocked HTTP route tests for human invitation acceptance when the actor is already a member, when a direct invite grants immediate membership, and when a consumed invite is replayed to repair missing access.
units.dependencyDirection: A session board actor and bearer invite enter access routes; database transaction-like stubs create/update join and invite records, while access services materialize membership and grants and activity logging records approval/replay events.
units.keyDataModels: Invite role/inviter/accepted state, actor user/memberships, human join request/request IP/email/status/approver, membership role/status, principal permission grants and join.approved/join.request_replayed activities.
units.lifecycle: An existing active member receives 409 without invite mutation. A new invitee creates a pending request that is immediately approved under the stored inviter identity, consumes the invite, creates active owner membership and grants, and logs approval. The same user may later replay an already accepted invite, update the pending request, auto-approve it again and recreate operator access without re-consuming the invite.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover non-consumption for current members, immediate grant materialization, inviter attribution, activity events and a self-healing replay path. Persistence and access services are heavily mocked; missing are real transaction/concurrency/one-time constraints, verified email and intended-recipient binding, inviter current authority, revoked/disabled identities, membership-removal reason, invite expiry/revocation during replay, grant rollback, role drift, cross-Company attacks, separation of duties and proof that replay cannot undo an administrator's revocation.
units.designRationale: Treat a direct human invitation as pre-approval and make onboarding resilient when membership materialization was lost or partially completed.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs idempotent human admission that can recover partial writes without allowing an old invitation to override later access revocation or fabricate approval history.
units.companyOsFit: Reject the replay semantics. Use one atomic admission command with an idempotency key and durable acceptance receipt; exact retries may finish the same incomplete transaction only while its intent is active. Once membership was created, any later removal/revocation is a newer authority version and cannot be repaired by the old invite. Reinstatement requires a new qualified-human approval and responsibility event. Validate inviter authority at issuance and record that issuance decision separately from system materialization.
units.responsibilityConflict: A consumed invite can recreate membership and grants after they disappear, potentially reversing an intentional offboarding. The new approval is attributed to the original inviter without proving that person remains authorized or performed the replay decision. An owner role and powerful grants are thus materialized from stale bearer authority, breaking chronological responsibility and revocation precedence.

units.lifecycle: Startup validates or generates signing material, repairs permissions/refuses a symlink, rejects unsafe authenticated-public database configurations, constructs services/app, starts selected maintenance loops and derives runtime/auth endpoints after port detection.
units.testAssessment: Strong security cases verify persisted signing-key directory/file modes, preservation of an existing key, symlink refusal and minimum explicit-secret length; public deployments fail before DB creation. Feedback coverage only proves the service object is passed to createApp, not that authorized pending rows flush correctly. The 725-line file mixes unrelated concerns and relies heavily on mocks, one captured interval callback and microtask timing; it lacks overlapping flush, graceful drain, retry/backoff, multi-instance coordination and no-egress-without-consent assertions.
units.designRationale: Exercise the real composition root without binding tests to live databases, sockets, auth providers or long-running schedulers, while preserving startup regressions accumulated across product areas.
units.companyOsProblem: Both deployment profiles need fail-closed startup security and explicit background-worker lifecycles, especially for irreversible data export and approval signing.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT signing-key no-follow/permission tests, preflight deployment refusal and detected-endpoint ordering. Split startup contracts by subsystem; make DataEgressWorker opt-in, lease/claim durable outbox rows atomically, prevent overlapping local runs, coordinate multiple replicas, use bounded backoff and await or checkpoint in-flight work during shutdown.
units.responsibilityConflict: Wiring a feedback service is not proof of authorized export. The app's immediate flush, 5-second interval and route-triggered flush can overlap because no in-flight guard is visible; rows are marked sent only after upload and the client lacks idempotency, so one consented trace can be transmitted more than once. Signing-key possession also proves server integrity, not human approval authority.

units.function: Real-filesystem integration tests for local object storage round-trip, byte-range streaming, lexical cross-Company access denial and idempotent deletion.
units.dependencyDirection: Company/namespace/file metadata and bytes enter StorageService, which creates a Company-prefixed key and delegates filesystem operations to LocalDiskStorageProvider; callers read streams through the same service guard.
units.keyDataModels: Company ID, namespace, original filename, content type, object key, SHA-256, byte range, content length and HTTP-like 403/404 errors.
units.lifecycle: Put computes metadata and persists bytes; get returns the whole stream or inclusive range; another Company is denied before read; repeated delete succeeds and a later get reports not found.
units.testAssessment: The suite exercises actual disk I/O and useful provider-neutral behavior. It does not test traversal/object-key validation, directory or file symlinks under the storage root, invalid/out-of-bounds ranges, zero-byte/large streaming uploads, digest verification on read, atomic write/rename cleanup, concurrent writes/deletes, permissions, quotas, encryption, retention/legal hold or S3 parity.
units.designRationale: Provide zero-configuration self-hosted object storage behind the same service contract used by a cloud provider.
units.companyOsProblem: Evidence and artifacts must move between managed-cloud and self-hosted profiles without weakening tenant isolation, integrity or lifecycle policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the provider contract, streaming ranges, tenant-prefix guard and idempotent delete semantics. Local storage must use descriptor-based no-follow containment and atomic immutable writes; every read verifies immutable version/digest policy, while S3/local providers share conformance tests for encryption, retention and consistency.
units.responsibilityConflict: A Company-prefixed mutable object and put-time hash are insufficient evidence provenance. The record must bind Work, executor, permission/data contract, collection method, immutable version and verified digest; deletion must respect retention/legal-hold authority.

units.function: Pure executable specification for task-subtree liveness, material stop fingerprints, reviewed-state suppression and the first-run race window.
units.dependencyDirection: Imports only the exported classifier/type from task-watchdogs and supplies in-memory Issue/path/wait fixtures.
units.keyDataModels: Classifier Issue tree, live run/wake paths, blocker and wait IDs, v2 material stop snapshot, reviewed fingerprint/snapshot and first-run timing inputs.
units.lifecycle: Build tree snapshots; classify live/stopped/pending/already-reviewed; compare fingerprints after metadata, leaf, assignee, blocker and wait changes; exclude watchdog-origin subtrees.
units.testAssessment: Fifteen named tests plus five material-change table cases give strong deterministic policy coverage. Gaps include cycles, depth/size bounds, duplicate IDs, invalid dates, tenant-mixed parents, ordering/property tests, human waits and approval/data-contract semantics.
units.designRationale: Keep noise-suppression and race-handling semantics independent of database orchestration.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs pure, replayable liveness and intervention policy tests with stable versioned outputs.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the table-driven material-change and race-window scenarios; add property tests, responsibility and authorization waits, and explicit policy-version migration fixtures.
units.responsibilityConflict: The classifier treats pending approvals as fingerprint material but does not decide which human owns the wait or whether an Agent may act around it.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for watchdog reconciliation, reusable review Issues, wake idempotency/context, reviewed snapshots, stale review recovery and mutation-fingerprint revalidation.
units.dependencyDirection: Invokes taskWatchdogService against real Paperclip schema and captures a fake wake adapter, spanning Issues, Runs, Wake requests, Approvals, Interactions, Documents, Work Products, comments and activity logs.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, Issue tree, IssueWatchdog, HeartbeatRun, AgentWakeupRequest, pending approval/interaction, evidence timestamps, stop snapshots and activity records.
units.lifecycle: Seed watchdogs and tree state; reconcile; inspect created/reopened review Issue, snapshots, comments and wake context; change live/material/review state; reconcile again; verify suppression, re-trigger or stale-scope denial.
units.testAssessment: Eighteen integration cases cover initial trigger, duplicate suppression, stale review, Run/Wakeup live paths, nested exclusion, ancestor reconciliation, reviewed snapshot reuse and JSON round-trip, old/new fingerprint ordering, evidence-only changes, wait payloads, create-race, true idle work and recursion prevention. It does not inject failures between sequential writes, run concurrent reconcilers, verify durable wake uniqueness in the database, test large/deep trees or assert human authority and Connector evidence receipts.
units.designRationale: Protect the cross-table invariants that the pure classifier alone cannot prove.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs intervention compatibility tests spanning event replay, incident projection, authorization, notification and recovery across managed and local profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the scenario catalog but implement against Company OS public ports/events and transactional outbox, including crash matrices and multi-node races.
units.responsibilityConflict: The scheduler proves an Agent wake, not accountable-human acknowledgement or approval; its success criteria omit immutable responsibility and data authorization receipts.

units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL integration suite for Tool policy/profile precedence, application/catalog state, selectors/conditions, context isolation, redaction/audit, idempotency, rate limiting, progressive trust, gateway enforcement and selected Tool Access tenant boundaries.
units.dependencyDirection: Tests exercise the real Policy Service and database schema; final cases cross into ToolGateway and ToolAccessService, providing useful vertical evidence but mixing three audit units. External MCP execution remains fixture-based.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Agent/Run/Issue, Application/Connection/Catalog, Profile/binding/entry, Policy and conditions, grant, audit/call events, Invocation/ActionRequest, rate counter, TrustRule, Secret reference.
units.lifecycle: Each case seeds a production-like PostgreSQL graph, evaluates/records decisions and inspects persisted outcomes. Concurrency races two rate-limit decisions; progressive-trust cases approve repeated actions, constrain promotion, detect catalog changes and revoke the resulting rule; gateway cases prove legacy allowAll cannot bypass policy.
units.testAssessment: ADAPT; this is a strong reference suite with real SQL, fail-closed legacy cases, hostile selectors/regex, concurrency, policy precedence and non-broadening trust promotion. It misses the most important integrity failures: two raw payloads that differ only in redacted/truncated fields, concurrent same-idempotency claims, legitimate repeated side effects without a key, crash/rollback between rate decision, Invocation, ActionRequest and audit, distinct approver/separation-of-duties requirements, approval digest mismatch, policy mutation after decision, Agent termination/grant revocation races, unknown grant scope/risk/catalog fail-closed behavior, multi-replica trust-hit updates, large policy/binding sets and all condition combinations. The test helper directly marks approvals in SQL, so it does not prove approval authorization or evidence.
units.designRationale: Verify policy behavior against real database constraints and prove the gateway cannot bypass the new deny-by-default control plane while exercising progressive autonomy conservatively.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs adversarial integration tests proving that exact action bytes, approvals, idempotency, policy snapshots and audit receipts remain one responsibility chain across crashes, races and Connector retries.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the fixture structure and adversarial policy matrix, then add fault injection, raw-vs-redacted digest collision tests, transaction/outbox recovery, distinct human approvers, stale policy/grant/runtime versions, data-egress conditions and Connector conformance. Keep Policy, Approval and Execution integration suites separately attributable.
units.responsibilityConflict: Tests simulate approval by directly changing status and never establish who approved, under what role, against which responsibility/action/data digest or with what evidence. Consequently green progressive-trust tests do not prove the human responsibility semantics Company OS requires.
