units.function: Large embedded-PostgreSQL integration and route test suite for the Tool Access orchestration boundary.
units.dependencyDirection: Exercises Express routes, database migrations/schema, Tool Access/Policy/Gateway services, secret storage and runtime collaborators; it is downstream verification rather than production ownership.
units.keyDataModels: Applications, connections, OAuth state/tokens, grants, installs, profiles, policies, catalogs, invocations, action requests, runtime slots, activity/audit records and user/Agent authorization contexts.
units.lifecycle: Builds isolated companies/users/Agents/runs and external HTTP fixtures, drives connection/OAuth/profile/policy/approval/runtime workflows, injects selected failures and asserts database state, response visibility and audit redaction.
units.testAssessment: Behavioral breadth and security regression coverage are strong, including genuine two-service refresh concurrency, transaction rollback and database FK race tests. It nevertheless skips key atomicity/failure windows and explicitly accepts unsafe product semantics such as non-Notion move_pages classified read and cross-tenant Google spreadsheet identifiers returned in conflict errors. Many scale/concurrency/cleanup invariants are absent. Direct local execution passed only the 7 non-database tests and skipped 118 database-backed tests because the current environment lacked test database support.
units.designRationale: Use one end-to-end suite to keep a rapidly growing cross-table Tool Access feature coherent across HTTP, services, database and external-provider boundaries.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs executable responsibility, credential, approval and connector compatibility contracts that detect partial failures and unsafe authority transitions, not only happy-path feature regressions.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the embedded-database fixture style, real HTTP OAuth fixtures, tenant/viewer matrices, database-race tests, secret-value absence assertions and failure injection. Split by bounded context and add property/concurrency/crash recovery, uninstall/archive revocation, scope/expiry, outbox, large-tenant and ResponsibilityContract invariants.
units.responsibilityConflict: Several assertions freeze Paperclip-specific authority semantics that Company OS must reject; copying the suite unchanged would make unsafe classification, identifier disclosure and incomplete responsibility state look normative.

units.function: Security tests for canonical Tool arguments, invocation/tool-bound signatures, dedicated signing-key configuration, sensitive-value summaries and prompt-injection rejection on Tool results.
units.dependencyDirection: Tool name/invocation/arguments and a dedicated environment secret feed signing/verification; untrusted arguments/results enter content validation before summary or return to an Agent.
units.keyDataModels: Canonical arguments, signedArguments, invocationId, toolName, signing secret, content direction, redacted summary/findings and validation errors.
units.lifecycle: Arguments are canonicalized and signed for one invocation/tool, tampering fails and verified bytes parse back. Auth/JWT secrets cannot substitute for the dedicated key. Sensitive fields are redacted from summaries and a recognized prompt-injection result is blocked.
units.testAssessment: Strong focused tests establish domain-separated integrity and early content controls. Missing are canonicalization edge cases, signature algorithm/version/key rotation, constant-time verification, expiry/nonce/replay, Work/approval/data binding, multi-node key custody, schema validation, nested/encoded secrets, prompt-injection false positives/bypasses, quarantine/review and signed result/evidence.
units.designRationale: Prevent a Tool action from changing after inspection and keep malicious/sensitive Tool content from silently flowing into Agent context.
units.companyOsProblem: High-risk actions must bind human approval to exact executable bytes and enforce data/tool firewall policy in the Connector runtime.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as the leading ActionEnvelope reference: sign canonical action digest with Work/contract/Agent/Connector, human approval, permissions/data scope, policy version, nonce/expiry and expected evidence/result; verify in the execution node, sign outcome, and route suspicious content to quarantine/human review rather than rely only on heuristics.
units.responsibilityConflict: The signature binds invocation/tool/arguments but not who proposed or approved them, the responsible human, Work contract, data authorization or expiry. A shared service secret attests only Paperclip possession and does not prevent authorized replay.

units.function: Full Tool Gateway acceptance suite spanning HTTP routes, MCP protocol, named/ephemeral tokens, Profiles, remote/local/plugin transports, Secrets, approval, audit queries and runtime supervision.
units.dependencyDirection: Runs across routes, services, database, SDK demo server, local HTTP servers and runtime supervision; it is a system test suite coupled to Paperclip schema and UI-facing projections.
units.keyDataModels: Company membership/permission, Agent/run/issue/project, gateway/session/token/rate counter, application/connection/catalog, Profile/policy, Secret/binding/version/access, Invocation/ActionRequest/Event/Audit and RuntimeSlot.
units.lifecycle: Creates isolated tenants and execution fixtures, drives discovery/call/approval/revocation/audit/runtime flows over service and HTTP boundaries, injects protocol failures and verifies persisted scope, status and redaction.
units.testAssessment: Mature breadth includes cross-instance limit state, company isolation, SSE interoperability, Secret/header precedence, target/credential freshness, session/run invalidation, granular runtime permissions, capacity/backoff/stuck recovery and hosted-local fail-closed behavior. Missing stress/failure semantics include session revoke race, external-effect crash windows, no-length response bounds, cleanup retention, Profile replacement revocation, same-company self-tool authorization, plugin timeout and versioned human/data authority. units.designRationale: Validate the production-shaped MCP execution plane end to end, including operational concerns often missed by feature-only suites.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equivalent compatibility and operational tests across managed-cloud and self-hosted execution while preserving independent domain semantics and a complete responsibility chain.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the real HTTP/SSE fixtures, multi-instance counters, SSRF/header/Secret matrices, deployment-profile tests and runtime recovery cases. Rebuild fixtures around Company OS principals, responsibility/data contracts, Connector capability attestations, effect receipts, transactional outbox and explicit cancellation/idempotency proofs.

units.function: Pure unit tests for trust-preset defaulting, restrictive boundary intersection, fail-closed parsing/scoping, Company isolation and JSON normalization preservation.
units.dependencyDirection: Tests call the resolver directly with shared policy schemas and also verify Issue execution-policy normalization, crossing the boundary between trust resolution and serialization compatibility without database or runtime dependencies.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/Project/Issue policy inputs, low-trust boundary dimensions, standard/low-trust/denied results, review preset version and raw-output disposition.
units.lifecycle: Construct policies, resolve once and assert exact effective boundary or denial; one case normalizes policy JSON and confirms custom extension data survives serialization.
units.testAssessment: ADAPT as a concise base suite, then add a generated pairwise source/dimension matrix, malformed scalar/object inputs, contradictory duplicate preset declarations, Run policy, scalar conflict rules, empty intersections, output promotion, stable digest/provenance and property-based tests proving that adding a restriction can never widen the effective set.
units.designRationale: Prove the safety-critical property that low-trust selection and boundary composition fail closed while allowing extension fields to round-trip.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs monotonic policy-composition tests: every more restrictive source must preserve or narrow authority, never widen it accidentally.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the small table-driven style and add monotonicity/property tests against the Company OS PolicyContext compiler and canonical serializer.
units.responsibilityConflict: Tests validate technical resource boundaries only; they do not bind policies to an accountable human, accepted responsibility, approval evidence or exact Work/action snapshot.

units.function: Unit tests parsing an environment-configured Express trust-proxy policy into unset, trust-all, hop-count, named subnet or CIDR-list forms while rejecting malformed tokens.
units.dependencyDirection: An ambient deployment environment string enters a strict parser and is assigned directly to Express's trust proxy setting, which controls client IP/protocol/host interpretation downstream.
units.keyDataModels: Undefined/false/0, boolean true, positive hop count, loopback/uniquelocal named ranges, IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs and invalid token errors.
units.lifecycle: Startup leaves Express's safe default unchanged for unset-like values, accepts explicit trusted forms with trimming, and throws on leading-zero integers, internal whitespace or unknown/partially invalid tokens.
units.testAssessment: The parser matrix is detailed and fail-closed for malformed input. Missing are negative/zero/overflow hop values, duplicate/overlapping ranges, IPv4-mapped IPv6, link-local/private named sets, actual spoofed X-Forwarded-* integration behavior, variable proxy-chain lengths, deployment-profile defaults and stable startup diagnostic codes.
units.designRationale: Support reverse-proxy deployments without silently accepting malformed trust configuration or enabling proxy trust by default.
units.companyOsProblem: Identity, tenant routing, rate limiting and audit attribution depend on trustworthy network origin across managed cloud, on-prem ingress and hybrid Connector nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit parser and safe unset default, but reject trust-all in production profiles and avoid hop counts where route length can vary. Require profile-owned CIDR/named-network policy, startup validation and integration tests proving spoofed forwarded headers remain untrusted outside the declared ingress path.
units.responsibilityConflict: A misconfigured trust-all or hop-count policy lets an external caller forge origin metadata used by security and audit decisions. Network origin is context only and must never establish accountable-human identity or approval authority.

units.function: Mock-based unit tests asserting that creation of a primary Issue work product and promotion of an existing work product execute their demotion/insertion or demotion/update sequences inside a database transaction.
units.dependencyDirection: Issue/work-product IDs and a primary flag enter workProductService; mocked Drizzle transaction primitives record select/update/insert call counts and return a projected row.
units.keyDataModels: Work product ID, Company/Project/Issue, type/provider, external ID/URL/status/review/health, primary flag, metadata, runtime/workspace/run references and timestamps.
units.lifecycle: Creating a primary first demotes same-Company/Issue/type rows then inserts; promoting an existing row selects it, demotes its current group and updates it, all within the callback supplied to db.transaction.
units.testAssessment: The tests catch accidental removal of the transaction wrapper and expected operation order at a coarse level. Mocks do not prove rollback, isolation or concurrency safety; they omit Company scoping, cross-Company Issue consistency, group-field mutation, database constraints, not-found/error paths, import batching, removal, source trust and actual primary uniqueness.
units.designRationale: Avoid a visible intermediate state with no or multiple selected primary work products during ordinary sequential mutations.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs one authoritative result/evidence projection per Work and artifact type without races or cross-tenant references.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY. Retain the behavioral intent but replace mock call-count tests with embedded-database concurrency, rollback and tenant-invariant tests backed by schema constraints and immutable Artifact/Evidence models.
units.responsibilityConflict: Transaction invocation does not prove the selected artifact is trustworthy, immutable or created under the approved Work/data contract. createdByRunId is nullable and no accountable human, approval digest or evidence digest is asserted.

units.function: Mints and verifies short-lived HS256 Agent run tokens bound to company, control-plane instance, adapter, run and optional responsible user/scope.
units.dependencyDirection: Server auth adapter depends on process secrets/shared scope normalization; middleware consumes neutralized claims, but vendor adapter type remains in token claims.
units.keyDataModels: sub/company_id/adapter_type/run_id/responsible_user_id/key_scope/iat/exp/iss/aud/instance_id/jti claims and per-instance/per-company derived HMAC key.
units.lifecycle: Derive scoped signing key, mint token, verify signature/current-or-legacy key, parse claims, check expiry and conditional issuer/audience/instance, then create Agent actor.
units.testAssessment: 17 JWT tests and seven middleware tests cover signing, expiry, tenant/instance isolation, legacy fallback, run/header mismatch and responsible-user behavior. Gaps: custom JWT implementation, no maximum TTL/future-iat check, no replay/jti store, optional iss/aud/instance acceptance for legacy tokens, shared-secret rotation and a legacy raw-secret forgery window.
units.designRationale: Issue runtime-local credentials without storing raw provider sessions and harden fork/company isolation after a documented incident.
units.companyOsProblem: Connectors need short-lived secret-free runtime proof bound to exact work, capability, tenant and accountable human.
units.companyOsFit: Tenant/instance key separation and run/responsible-user binding are valuable. Company OS should use a standard signed-token library or asymmetric workload identity, mandatory issuer/audience/instance/action digest, bounded clock skew/TTL, key IDs/rotation and replay policy through Identity/Execution ports.
units.responsibilityConflict: A responsible_user_id claim is only identity context, not proof that the human approved the exact action, permissions, data grant or result.

units.function: Express composition root mounting every HTTP route, authentication/host/CSRF middleware, plugin host, UI, schedulers and background exporters.
units.dependencyDirection: A 752-line outer composition root imports virtually every route and plugin service plus static/Vite UI; inward modules do not import it.
units.keyDataModels: App options, deployment exposure, plugin lifecycle handles, host-service disposers and startup promises.
units.lifecycle: Configure parsing/logging/host/auth guards, mount routes, construct plugin/event/tool services, serve UI, start jobs/watchers/exporters and register cleanup.
units.testAssessment: Many route and app integration tests cover individual behavior, hostname gating and authorization. There is no concise composition-contract test proving route-by-route auth/size/origin policy; correctness is distributed across mount order and each router.
units.designRationale: Centralize startup wiring and keep route/service implementations independently testable.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a narrow API service entry with consistent identity, authorization, size, idempotency and audit policies.
units.companyOsFit: Explicit composition is useful, but this root owns too many domains and background lifecycles. Company OS should compose bounded modules through uniform policy middleware and generated route metadata rather than rely on a long hand-ordered mount list.
units.responsibilityConflict: A route mounted outside the expected guard order can bypass organizational responsibility policy. Responsibility checks must be application invariants, not only Express topology.

units.function: Better Auth integration for email/password sessions, instance-scoped cookies, trusted origins and rate limiting.
units.dependencyDirection: Outer identity adapter depends on better-auth/Drizzle and Paperclip auth tables/config; middleware resolves its session shape.
units.keyDataModels: User/session/account/verification rows, session result, cookie prefix, base URL/trusted origins and rate-limit options.
units.lifecycle: Create auth instance against DB schema, issue session cookies, resolve sessions from request headers and map to board actor.
units.testAssessment: 17 focused Better Auth tests plus auth route/session tests cover cookie isolation, secure-cookie choices, trusted origins and rate-limit defaults. Email verification is disabled, sign-up defaults enabled, and enterprise OIDC/SAML/LDAP lifecycle is not represented.
units.designRationale: Provide a simple embedded identity system for local/self-hosted and authenticated modes.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed cloud and local enterprise need replaceable IdentityPort adapters with isolated token audience, tenant binding and independent audit.
units.companyOsFit: Cookie-instance isolation and origin derivation are useful references. Better Auth may be one adapter, never core; production profiles need explicit enrollment, verified identities and enterprise federation/provisioning/deprovisioning contracts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Authentication proves a principal session, not company role, accountable-human assignment or action approval; those remain Company OS domain checks.

units.function: Reads and validates the persisted JSON configuration with a shared Zod schema while warning about likely misspelled keys.
units.dependencyDirection: Server file adapter depends on shared config schema and local home-path resolution; domain code does not call it directly.
units.keyDataModels: Versionless PaperclipConfig JSON plus unknown-key suggestion warnings.
units.lifecycle: Resolve path, read/parse JSON, schema-validate, emit suggestions, return typed config or fail startup.
units.testAssessment: Focused config-file tests cover invalid JSON/schema and unknown-key preservation. They do not establish versioned migrations, atomic writes, rollback, provenance or concurrent writer behavior.
units.designRationale: Fail early on malformed operator configuration without deleting forward-compatible unknown keys.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed-cloud and self-hosted profiles need validated, evolvable, supportable configuration with FDE overlays.
units.companyOsFit: Schema validation and preservation of unknown keys are useful. Company OS additionally needs explicit config schema versions, source precedence/provenance, secret-free support export and transactional migration/rollback.
units.responsibilityConflict: Configuration can change execution and security policy; consequential changes need an actor, digest and audit receipt rather than an anonymous file mutation.

units.function: Combines env, JSON config, defaults, path resolution and bind-mode detection into the runtime server configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: Outer startup adapter depends on shared deployment enums and host filesystem/process commands; config values then fan into every service.
units.keyDataModels: Deployment mode/exposure/bind, auth origin, database/backup, secrets, storage, feedback export, scheduler, deletion and telemetry settings.
units.lifecycle: Load dotenv and file config, apply env precedence/defaults, optionally detect Tailscale, validate bind constraints and return one config object.
units.testAssessment: Configuration behavior is exercised indirectly and through bind/environment tests. Important env parsing is not uniformly strict: unknown enum values silently fall back, most booleans treat any non-'true' value as false, and numeric values use coercion/defaults. This can conceal operator mistakes.
units.designRationale: Offer zero-config local startup and flexible env overrides for containers and managed deployments.
units.companyOsProblem: Dual deployment profiles need the same business code but different adapters and enforceable security posture.
units.companyOsFit: The unified profile object and bind validation are useful. Company OS must parse every security-relevant env value strictly, reject invalid/unknown inputs, expose effective redacted config with provenance, and separate managed policy from mutable local preferences.
units.responsibilityConflict: Silent fallback can weaken intended identity, secret or exposure policy without a visible accountable decision.

units.function: Recognizes Postgres unique violations across Drizzle/driver cause chains and optional constraint names.
units.dependencyDirection: Server service helper depends only on error shapes/SQLSTATE and is called by transactional workflows.
units.keyDataModels: SQLSTATE 23505, constraint/constraint_name and bounded cause chain.
units.lifecycle: Walk up to four causes, detect unique violation and optional exact constraint, return boolean.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests cover wrapped driver variants, names/messages and unrelated failures. The bounded walk is deterministic and does not leak SQL text.
units.designRationale: Translate driver-specific wrapped conflicts into domain-level deduplication behavior.
units.companyOsProblem: Idempotent Connector/work/approval operations need portable conflict recognition at storage adapters.
units.companyOsFit: The cause-chain technique is useful inside a Postgres adapter, but Company OS application code should receive a neutral storage conflict code.
units.responsibilityConflict: None if kept in the storage adapter; a uniqueness conflict must not be interpreted as proof that the same human-approved action succeeded without digest comparison.

units.function: Unversioned filesystem protocol for dev supervisor status and restart request plus a health projection.
units.dependencyDirection: An environment-selected status path is synchronously read; a fixed sibling path is created/overwritten for control; parsed state feeds health API.
units.keyDataModels: PersistedDevServerStatus, DevServerHealthStatus and DevServerRestartRequest.
units.lifecycle: Read/normalize supervisor state, derive restart reason/waiting state and overwrite a restart request for external consumption.
units.testAssessment: Helper tests pass but do not cover the production-critical filesystem and request lifecycle gaps visible in source.
units.designRationale: Use a simple language/runtime-neutral bridge between the server and a local dev process supervisor.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs local development ergonomics without allowing informal file protocols to become production execution authority.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY as dev tooling. A production restart must use a versioned authenticated command/operation with idempotency, actor/approval, exact runtime/config digest, expiry, drain/adoption proof, result and immutable audit evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: The request records only time and a constant reason; there is no accountable human, action target, approved state, work impact or completion evidence.

units.function: Minimal HTTP exception type and status-specific constructors.
units.dependencyDirection: Routes/services throw the server-specific HttpError; error middleware serializes it.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP status, English message and optional untyped details.
units.lifecycle: Construct error in service/route, propagate through Express, serialize message/details.
units.testAssessment: Behavior is covered through route/error-handler tests, but the type does not require a stable code, structured parameters, audience, retryability or safe/public distinction.
units.designRationale: Keep route errors concise and compatible with Express.
units.companyOsProblem: Independent Web, Connector SDK and future bilingual UI require stable machine contracts rather than English text matching.
units.companyOsFit: The status helpers are too weak. Company OS needs mandatory stable code, safe structured parameters, correlation ID, retry class and internal/public cause separation.
units.responsibilityConflict: Free-form details can accidentally expose sensitive evidence or misstate why a responsibility decision was denied.

units.function: Defines default JSON and company-portability upload ceilings, including an environment-overridable compressed ZIP limit.
units.dependencyDirection: Transport constants are imported by app/import routes; no inward domain dependency.
units.keyDataModels: 10 MiB default JSON, 64 MiB portable JSON and a 1 GiB default/64 GiB maximum compressed ZIP byte limit.
units.lifecycle: Parse the environment override at module load, clamp/fallback, configure whole-body parsers and derive decompression guards in import handling.
units.testAssessment: Six focused tests verify constants, override fallback and arithmetic clamping. The code explicitly states the entire upload is buffered in memory and allows up to 64 GiB, but tests do not exercise concurrency, process memory, slow uploads, authenticated tenant quotas or streaming decompression.
units.designRationale: Accept large real-world company packages in one request while bounding decompression arithmetic.
units.companyOsProblem: Enterprise import/export and FDE templates need large portable packages without turning the API into a memory/zip-bomb denial-of-service path.
units.companyOsFit: Separate route-specific limits are sensible, but the in-memory 1–64 GiB design is unacceptable. Company OS should stream to quarantined object storage, enforce compressed/uncompressed/file-count/ratio/tenant quotas, verify digest/signature, scan before activation and resume idempotently.
units.responsibilityConflict: Import mutates organization/data/permission state and needs an accountable initiator, validated manifest digest, preview and explicit apply receipt.

units.function: Full process startup and shutdown: instrumentation, Postgres, migrations, backups, auth, backfills, managed config, adapters, schedulers, WebSockets and listening.
units.dependencyDirection: A 1,536-line process entry imports DB migrations and most server services; it is the terminal composition layer.
units.keyDataModels: StartedServer, migration state, embedded/external DB runtime, deployment/auth state, managed config, backup health and shutdown coordination.
units.lifecycle: Initialize telemetry/secrets, provision DB, inspect/reconcile/apply migrations, validate deployment contracts, backfill/reconcile state, build app and realtime, start schedulers/backups, load adapters, listen, then coordinated shutdown.
units.testAssessment: Startup, shutdown, migration, managed-config, worktree and feedback-export behaviors have focused tests, but the entire production sequence is not exercised as one failure-matrix. Non-interactive startup automatically approves pending migrations unless PAPERCLIP_MIGRATION_PROMPT=never, increasing unattended upgrade risk.
units.designRationale: Make a single command self-healing and easy to operate, including embedded Postgres and compatibility backfills.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted enterprise needs reliable migration, backup, recovery, health, upgrade and rollback semantics.
units.companyOsFit: Refusal to run on stale schema, migration inspection, startup ordering and coordinated cleanup are important references. Company OS should split the orchestrator into testable phases, require an explicit production migration policy, support preflight/backup/rollback receipts and avoid behavior-changing data backfills hidden in process startup.
units.responsibilityConflict: Automatic schema/backfill changes are consequential administrative actions and require operator policy, immutable evidence and rollback ownership.

units.function: Masks current OS usernames and home-directory paths recursively before log export.
units.dependencyDirection: Logging adapter depends on process/env/path data; business records remain untouched.
units.keyDataModels: Candidate usernames/home dirs, replacement token and recursively redacted values.
units.lifecycle: Discover candidate identity strings, replace longest paths then bounded username tokens, recurse plain objects/arrays.
units.testAssessment: Four focused tests cover path, token-boundary, nested and disabled behavior. It cannot discover every PII path or guarantee redaction of non-plain objects/buffers.
units.designRationale: Prevent workstation identity leakage in diagnostic logs while preserving useful paths.
units.companyOsProblem: FDE support bundles and managed-cloud telemetry must not exfiltrate local employee/device identity.
units.companyOsFit: Useful defense-in-depth for support export. Company OS should combine structured sensitivity labels, allowlisted fields and tenant policy; original user input/evidence stays in its governed store rather than being mutated.
units.responsibilityConflict: Redaction must preserve evidence integrity by storing original and redacted derivative separately with a digest/provenance link.

units.function: HTTP actor resolution, cloud trusted headers, CSRF/origin guard, hostname/DNS-rebinding guard, trust-proxy parsing, validation, logging/redaction, compression and error serialization.
units.dependencyDirection: Transport layer depends on DB/shared/services and writes a rich Express actor used by routes; some authorization semantics therefore live in middleware rather than application services.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor sources, memberships/on-behalf-of snapshot, key scope/run ID, cloud stack identity, trusted host/origin/proxy config and structured HTTP error response.
units.lifecycle: Resolve implicit/session/cloud/API-key/JWT actor, validate host and browser mutation origin, execute route, sanitize logs and serialize errors.
units.testAssessment: Dedicated tests cover Agent auth, 17 cloud-tenant cases, board mutation, private host, trust proxy, errors and redaction. Important issues remain: local_trusted is implicit instance admin; Cloud uses one static trusted-header token; private-host and board-origin code reads X-Forwarded-Host directly rather than only through the configured trusted-proxy interpretation; stable error codes are optional.
units.designRationale: Normalize many transport identities once and provide backwards-compatible on-behalf-of human context to all routes.
units.companyOsProblem: Every request needs tenant/principal/capability context, but responsibility/data authorization must remain uniform across HTTP, events and Connector dispatch.
units.companyOsFit: Fail-closed missing responsible user, active membership snapshots and stale elevation cleanup are strong patterns. Company OS should issue a neutral PrincipalContext from IdentityPort, use short-lived audience-bound service identity, derive forwarded host only from trusted proxy state, and enforce responsibility inside application use cases.
units.responsibilityConflict: onBehalfOfUserId is valuable but still only a delegation context. It must not substitute for an exact responsibility contract and high-risk approval digest.

units.function: Server package manifest, build/test entry points and dependency ownership for the Paperclip control-plane process.
units.dependencyDirection: The server directly imports DB/shared/plugin SDK plus every built-in Agent adapter and many infrastructure vendors, making it both composition root and runtime owner.
units.keyDataModels: No domain data; package scripts, published exports and dependency graph.
units.lifecycle: Build/typecheck/test the server and bundle UI/adapter/plugin artifacts into the distributable package.
units.testAssessment: Vitest configuration and a large server suite exist, but the manifest itself has no dependency-policy or architecture test preventing domain-to-vendor coupling. Several runtime packages use compatible ranges rather than exact pins.
units.designRationale: One deployable server simplifies self-hosted installation and makes built-in adapters available without separate services.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a simple deployable profile while preserving replaceable model, Agent, storage, identity and execution ports.
units.companyOsFit: The single-service packaging is operationally useful for an early self-hosted profile, but Company OS must keep vendor adapters out of inward layers and preferably out of the core server package dependency graph.
units.responsibilityConflict: Directly owning execution vendors in the control-plane package encourages transport credentials and sessions to leak across responsibility boundaries.

units.function: Company event WebSocket subscriptions and one-time authenticated SSH terminal bridging for custom sandbox-image setup.
units.dependencyDirection: Realtime transport bypasses Express middleware and implements separate DB/session/key authorization; terminal path depends on custom-image services, ephemeral session store and ssh2.
units.keyDataModels: Company upgrade context, session/API key identity, event subscription, terminal setup/session token, pinned SSH host hash, resize/input/output frames and connection registry.
units.lifecycle: Intercept HTTP upgrade, independently authorize, bind company subscription or validate a short-lived terminal session, bridge frames/SSH, enforce expiry/heartbeat and clean up sockets/sessions.
units.testAssessment: Three live-event tests and eight terminal tests cover cross-company denial, sessions, query/header token behavior, one-time auth, expiry, host verification and cleanup. Live events accept long-lived Agent API keys in URL query parameters, do not accept scoped run JWTs, and do not repeat Agent status/responsible-human checks from HTTP middleware; query credentials may leak through intermediaries despite application log care.
units.designRationale: Support browser-compatible realtime and interactive setup while keeping terminal connection payloads ephemeral.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs realtime projections, while local execution setup may require interactive operator intervention without leaking credentials.
units.companyOsFit: One-time terminal tokens, host-key pinning, expiry and cleanup are good patterns. Company OS should use one shared authorization service for HTTP/WebSocket/events, prohibit long-lived credentials in URLs, use short-lived audience/work-scoped tickets and publish only sanitized projection events with resume cursors.
units.responsibilityConflict: Realtime delivery and terminal transport must not create authority. An interactive human identity and any resulting runtime/config mutation need an exact audited responsibility record.

units.function: Recursively removes credential-shaped fields, command flags, JSON fragments and JWT-shaped values from events/log text.
units.dependencyDirection: Server safety helper imports command redaction from adapter-utils and is used across audit/log/run surfaces.
units.keyDataModels: Secret field-name regex, secret/user-secret/plain bindings, CLI argv rules, JWT pattern and REDACTED marker.
units.lifecycle: Inspect field/type/value, preserve safe secret references, redact secret material and command args, recursively sanitize plain data.
units.testAssessment: Eight core tests plus HTTP/run/comment redaction suites cover nested payloads, flags, bindings, JWTs and audit exceptions. Regex/field-name detection remains inherently incomplete and can both miss novel credentials and over-redact ordinary data.
units.designRationale: Apply one broad defense across heterogeneous Agent/provider payloads without requiring every caller to remember secret fields.
units.companyOsProblem: Control-plane events must exclude credentials/private sessions/reasoning while retaining evidence and original business output in authorized stores.
units.companyOsFit: Reference preservation and structured traversal are strong. Company OS should make sensitivity typed at ingestion and deny unknown payload shapes; heuristic redaction remains a final guard, not the primary security boundary.
units.responsibilityConflict: Redacted audit text cannot replace source evidence. Responsibility records must point to immutable authorized evidence digests and record the redaction transform.

units.function: HTTP workflow for generic approvals, revision/resubmission, comments and mutable links between approvals and issues.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes orchestrate approval, issue-link, comment, Agent and activity services; several responsibility and side-effect rules exist only in this transport layer.
units.keyDataModels: Approval type/status/payload, requester/decider IDs, free-form note, comments and issue-approval links.
units.lifecycle: Agent or board creates an approval, links issues in separate calls, board approves/rejects/requests revision, requester resubmits and participants comment; links remain editable after resolution.
units.testAssessment: Route tests cover actor-derived requester/decider attribution, cross-company protection, payload redaction and idempotent decision responses. They do not require an exact action digest, approval-authority/risk match, immutable target links, evidence/result binding or atomic creation with issue links. Local mode can attribute a decision to the synthetic string 'board'.
units.designRationale: Provide a flexible board inbox that can accommodate several approval types without a schema per type.
units.companyOsProblem: High-risk work must pause on a versioned action contract and resume only after the matching accountable human approves the exact action, permissions, data, evidence expectations and runtime scope.
units.companyOsFit: Actor-derived attribution, hidden cross-tenant existence and idempotent response shape are useful references. Company OS must put approval invariants in application use cases, require a real human principal and make target/action associations immutable after proposal.
units.responsibilityConflict: A mutable issue link and arbitrary payload cannot prove who approved which exact work/action/data contract. Redacting comments before persistence also destroys the original evidence rather than storing a governed original plus derivative.

units.function: Shared route authorization helpers for actor type, instance/company access, cross-tenant existence-oracle protection, actor audit fields and secret-consumer context.
units.dependencyDirection: Express route layer consumes the middleware actor and server authorization shadow-mode setting; services do not depend on these helpers, so some security invariants exist only at HTTP call sites.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor, company membership and viewer role, on-behalf-of responsible user snapshot, actor source/run/key IDs and secret consumer context.
units.lifecycle: Authenticate actor, hide inaccessible resource existence, intersect Agent company scope with an optional responsible-user membership, enforce read/write role, derive audit/secret context, then call a service.
units.testAssessment: The authorization suites cover 19 company-access cases, five secret-context cases and a static route scan preventing known existence-oracle regressions. Gaps: HTTP method is used as the write-risk proxy; static source scanning cannot prove every dynamic path; stable denial codes are inconsistent; shadow mode intentionally permits responsible-user denials; and an Agent whose onBehalfOfUserId is absent skips the human-membership intersection entirely.
units.designRationale: Centralize backwards-compatible company scoping and prevent 403/404 differences from leaking cross-tenant resource existence.
units.companyOsProblem: Every use case must combine tenant, principal, role, responsible human, data grant, work contract and risk-specific approval without leaking object existence.
units.companyOsFit: The indistinguishable not-found pattern, server-derived secret consumer and human/Agent permission intersection are strong references. Company OS must enforce them inside application use cases across every transport, require an accountable human for formal Agent work, remove shadow bypass from production and authorize named actions rather than HTTP verbs.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip treats responsible human context as optional for some JWT/legacy paths and permits a shadow mode. Company OS requires every formal Agent action to resolve an active responsibility contract and exact human owner before execution.

units.function: Paperclip Cloud portfolio reverse proxy with trusted actor headers, server token and a short in-memory per-user cache.
units.dependencyDirection: Paperclip Cloud environment/actor becomes an authenticated request to a vendor control-plane URL; opaque upstream JSON is returned and cached.
units.keyDataModels: CloudStackContext, cloud_tenant actor, tenant bearer token, stack/user headers, opaque portfolio and cache entry.
units.lifecycle: Validate broad context/actor, clean expired cache, build URL, fetch with timeout, map errors, cache and return upstream payload.
units.testAssessment: Focused route tests pass, but destination trust, response contracts, cache bounds and resiliency are important untested source-level gaps.
units.designRationale: Expose a user's Cloud stack portfolio without letting browser credentials or spoofed identity cross the server boundary.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Web may consume managed-cloud organization portfolios or enterprise directories through stable provider adapters.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY because the route/DTO/headers are Paperclip-specific. Implement a typed OrganizationDirectoryPort adapter with startup-validated HTTPS allowlist, egress firewall, secret audience, bounded schema, cache cap, circuit breaker and provenance.
units.responsibilityConflict: The proxy proves actor identity transport but has no explicit authorization decision, responsibility scope or evidence for portfolio access and later stack switching.

units.function: Monolithic company HTTP router covering listing, statistics, timeline, settings and branding, archive/hard delete, feedback traces, artifacts and full company portability preview/export/import with an in-memory async job facade.
units.dependencyDirection: HTTP actors and Paperclip Cloud environment flow directly into access, company, activity, portability, agent, budget, artifact and feedback services plus database queries; route-local helpers own ZIP parsing, job state, deduplication and response projection.
units.keyDataModels: Company and membership, synthetic local-board principal, default responsible user, free-form CEO Agent role, portability bundle/ZIP, import target/collision strategy, process-memory ImportJobRecord and activity entries.
units.lifecycle: Authorize company actor, parse fully buffered JSON/ZIP, preview/export/import; create company then membership/grants/activity/budget sequentially; mutate settings/branding then log; archive/delete; run optional import jobs in process memory and expire terminal records after one hour.
units.testAssessment: The focused authorization suite passed 12/12 and proves its intended access semantics. Source review found no route-level tests here for durable import recovery, stable errors, ZIP/memory exhaustion, human approval, lifecycle transaction rollback, deletion retention/legal hold, data classification or audit completeness.
units.designRationale: Offer one pragmatic board API for organization administration and portable Cloud/self-hosted transfer, plus a narrowly reduced Agent-safe import mode and lightweight async UX without introducing a durable job subsystem.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs independent organization commands, human/Agent responsibility policy, governed export/import, durable migration jobs and evidence-rich audit across managed-cloud and self-hosted deployments.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as bounded application commands and projections behind Organization, Identity, Authorization, Data Export, Durable Job, Event Store, Audit/Evidence and Approval ports. Retain the useful fail-closed ZIP parsing ideas, explicit safe-mode collision restrictions and cross-company tests, but do not copy this router or its Paperclip DTO/service coupling.
units.responsibilityConflict: A free-form same-company ceo Agent can export/import; any active member can archive, hard-delete, export and import. The local-board synthetic principal can become default responsible owner. None of these high-risk actions requires a verified accountable human, purpose/data contract, exact approval binding or evidence/result digest.

securityFindings: multer.memoryStorage buffers ZIP uploads and the configurable limit can reach 1 GiB; decompression permits at least four times the upload limit, creating material memory and decompression denial-of-service exposure.

Async import returns 202 before deferred target authorization/body validation, stores jobs only in memory, loses them on restart and documents a later 404 as soft success after running was observed; completion and responsibility evidence are therefore ambiguous.
Local duplicate suppression is a per-actor Map scan plus hash of JSON serialization, not durable idempotency; Cloud tenant imports do not receive the same guard.

Company creation, membership, grants, activity and budget policy—and import plus activity—are sequential side effects without a visible enclosing transaction or outbox, allowing partial success and misleading failure state.
Terminal error responses repeat a raw English message in error, message and reason rather than exposing a stable structured code/parameters contract.

units.function: Two shared constants for the company-import relative route and assembled HTTP API path.
units.dependencyDirection: A server route-name constant is assembled into a browser-facing /api/companies/import path and imported by transport consumers.
units.keyDataModels: Literal /import relative path and /api/companies/import absolute application path.
units.lifecycle: Compile-time string reuse only; there is no request, schema, versioning, deprecation or compatibility lifecycle.
units.testAssessment: No dedicated test is warranted for the two literal constants, but no contract test verifies server registration/client generation or version compatibility either.
units.designRationale: Avoid duplicated route strings drifting across server and UI.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs one canonical transport specification for independent Web, API clients and deployment profiles without leaking HTTP details into core/application.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY. Keep route naming in an API adapter or generated OpenAPI client and prove it with compatibility tests; core commands/events and Connector SDK must remain independent of HTTP path constants.
units.responsibilityConflict: None in the constant itself, but it expresses no identity, authority, approval, idempotency, data contract or evidence requirements for the high-risk import operation.

units.function: HTTP routes for reading, replacing, resetting and simulating company Skill policies.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes directly compose shared Zod documents, route authz, broad access permissions, policy service and Activity actor mapping.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor, users:manage_permissions, policy DTO, simulated Agent principal, stable transport errors and Activity actor.
units.lifecycle: Validate body; assert company/admin; map actor; mutate/reset or resolve current/simulated principal and evaluate.
units.testAssessment: Source exposes important untested boundaries because route tests were skipped: validation precedes authorization, Agent broad permission can administer policy, every company actor can read full rules and evaluations are not evidenced.
units.designRationale: Reuse existing company permission administration and permit self-service Agent evaluation with little route complexity.
units.companyOsProblem: Executable capability policy is a high-risk governance object requiring authenticated accountable-human ownership, scoped disclosure and approval publication.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as application commands/queries over Identity, Authority, Approval and Audit/Evidence ports. Authenticate/company-bind before parsing expensive policy bodies; separate policy view from self-decision; require human policy-owner authority and separation of duties; bind replace/reset/evaluate to stable request/policy/action digests and codes.
units.responsibilityConflict: An Agent with users:manage_permissions may rewrite/reset its own Skill authority. Local/instance admins bypass company authority, board identity can be synthetic, and no responsible-human approval is required.
evidence: 89ce36d7afcb3b2920c45c47b55f210d635b9976 feat(skills): open-by-default company skill policy and core UX (#9564)
companion route suite fully read; 3/3 tests skipped on this host

Any company actor can retrieve the full policy including protected IDs, roles and internal source locators rather than only its effective decision.
Reset has no expected revision/idempotency key, and evaluate produces no immutable access-decision evidence.

units.function: Company-scoped HTTP API for decision queues, source membership, triage deadlines/snooze and retention archive/keep controls.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes combine shared validators, route actor state, authorization actions and queue/retention services; authority remains transport-mediated.
units.keyDataModels: Named queue, heterogeneous attention-source reference, triage override, responsible-user attribution and retention state.
units.lifecycle: Board or eligible Agent reads/manages queues, adds readable sources, changes triage metadata and archives/revives attention sidecars.
units.testAssessment: Embedded-Postgres route tests cover idempotent queue creation, actor audit, heterogeneous source visibility, hidden/missing equivalence, seeded queues, concurrent partial triage updates and restricted task-bridge/skill-test credentials. Stable error codes and application-level responsibility enforcement remain inconsistent.
units.designRationale: Give Agents and humans one durable inbox/triage surface over many decision-like source types without moving the source records.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs configurable, responsibility-aware work/approval inboxes without duplicating source truth.
units.companyOsFit: The sidecar queue and per-source read check are useful. Company OS should expose one typed Projection API backed by a source registry, stable codes and application authorization; queue mutation must not imply authority to decide the underlying action.
units.responsibilityConflict: The route records on-behalf-of identity but does not require a responsibility contract, and any principal with generic queue-manage authority can reorder organizational attention regardless of accountable role.

units.function: Human-only capture, preview, library, note editing, deletion and full-company JSONL export for decision-training examples.
units.dependencyDirection: HTTP layer exposes the snapshot service directly and relies on board/company/author checks plus activity logging; export serializes every example in memory.
units.keyDataModels: Frozen state snapshot, human notes/history, outcome label, author and JSONL state/label records.
units.lifecycle: A board user previews/captures a decision snapshot, edits only their notes, browses records and can export all company examples or delete their own record.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover human-only writes/reads/exports, author-only mutation, immutable snapshot, audit of reads/exports, no-op notes and strict update shape. They do not test step-up authorization, export data policy/approval, size/streaming, rate limits, purpose consent, redaction breadth or concurrent note updates.
units.designRationale: Turn human decisions into reusable labeled examples while keeping source state frozen and user guidance editable.
units.companyOsProblem: Future Agent Boss training/certification may learn from decisions, but enterprise data cannot silently become a model-training dataset or leave through an unrestricted export.
units.companyOsFit: Do not copy this route. Company OS needs a Data Authorization/Export Firewall use case with explicit purpose, field manifest, preview, accountable exporter, approval, digest, streaming and revocation/retention policy before any training-library feature.
units.responsibilityConflict: Any board user can export snapshots containing issue, comments and run records without a data-owner contract or high-risk approval. Author ownership of notes does not establish consent from people whose data appears in the snapshot.

units.function: Agent-originated proposal and bundle API, board decision/dismissal API, Agent cancellation/readback, statistics and a reviewed attention-archive proposal flow.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes validate shared Decision effects and call Decision/attention/authorization services; the API is tied to Paperclip issue and board/Agent actor concepts.
units.keyDataModels: Decision title/body/options/input prompts, typed issue effects, origin Agent/run, expiry/idempotency, continuation policy and signed archive manifest.
units.lifecycle: An in-run Agent proposes bounded effects, board lists and decides, executor applies them and optionally wakes the origin Agent; archive proposals snapshot an exact reviewed manifest.
units.testAssessment: Strict schemas bound option/effect/input counts and agent/board routes constrain proposal versus decision roles. Gaps: every board member can decide regardless of approval authority/risk class; local implicit board is not a real human; most validation errors use English strings rather than mandatory stable codes; generic high-risk data/tool/model actions are not represented.
units.designRationale: Expose a compact human-in-the-loop protocol that an Agent can invoke during one run and continue after a board answer.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector-neutral Agents need pause/resume approval APIs while humans need role/risk-matched decision surfaces independent of a particular work-item model.
units.companyOsFit: Bounded typed effects, origin-run requirement, archive manifest review and continuation are strong API references. Company OS must define its own action envelope, stable error contract, real-human approval authority and Connector protocol instead of copying Paperclip routes/types.
units.responsibilityConflict: Board membership is treated as sufficient approval authority and the API does not require a responsibility-contract/action/data/evidence digest.

units.function: Company-scoped HTTP CRUD and move routes for routine/skill folders, including creation of a signed-in board user's personal skill folder and activity logging after mutations.
units.dependencyDirection: Express and shared Zod validators feed assertCompanyAccess and folderService; successful mutations then call the activity logger and serialize service results.
units.keyDataModels: Folder ID/company/kind/parent/name/slug/path/depth/color/position/system key, routine or company-skill item reference, board/agent actor metadata and activity details.
units.lifecycle: List parses a required kind; create/update/move/delete validate Company access, mutate through the service, log an activity after success and return JSON; ensure-my additionally requires a signed-in board user.
units.testAssessment: The route file centralizes Company access checks and validates mutation bodies, but its dedicated test covers only the route-order regression. There is no route-level evidence here for access denial, cross-Company IDs, personal-folder ownership, logger failure after mutation, idempotency, concurrency, stable structured errors or rollback consistency.
units.designRationale: Expose a thin authenticated HTTP layer over a folder service and retain actor-attributed operational history without putting hierarchy logic in Express handlers.
units.companyOsProblem: FDE templates, evidence collections and office configuration may need tenant-scoped hierarchies and human-owned private areas without allowing transport code to become the policy owner.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the thin route/service split, Company guard and post-mutation actor context. Company OS must use stable error codes, policy-scoped Principal authorization, idempotent commands and an atomic outbox/event transaction so state cannot commit while its responsibility evidence fails.
units.responsibilityConflict: Mutation and activity logging are separate awaits with no visible atomicity; an activity logger failure can follow a committed mutation. Generic actor metadata also lacks the Work, responsibility contract, approval, data scope and evidence bindings required for consequential changes.

units.function: Combined health/diagnostics router plus a file-mediated dev-server restart control endpoint.
units.dependencyDirection: Public/actor request context drives database probes and projections; filesystem backup/dev status and instance settings feed diagnostics; POST writes a restart request.
units.keyDataModels: Actor/deployment exposure, DB/bootstrap state, server/git/cloud metadata, backup health warnings, active runs/dev-server state and restart request.
units.lifecycle: Authorize detail level, probe dependencies, compute bootstrap/dev/backup projections, redact or expose full response; separately accept and persist a restart request.
units.testAssessment: The reviewed health suite passes but leaves Agent overexposure, control authorization, unbounded dependency work and readiness/degraded behavior unproven; separate pending dev-server tests will be audited independently.

units.testAssessment: The already-audited 509-line embedded-Postgres suite covers important intended behavior, but the implementation exposes serious untested paths. setPrincipalPermission calls ensureMembership with role=member/status=active, and ensureMembership overwrites any differing existing role/status, so granting one permission can silently demote an Owner or reactivate a suspended/archived principal without last-Owner checks. ensureMembership and setUserCompanyAccess independently bypass the locked Owner invariant; setUserCompanyAccess reads its snapshot before the transaction, has a dead last-Owner branch after an earlier blanket Owner/admin rejection, and does no row locking. setMemberPermissions can grant to suspended/archived members. Lists are unpaginated, mutable methods do not emit immutable audit/evidence, and English conflict text is the effective error contract.

units.function: Monolithic authorization decision engine for board/user/Agent actors across Company, Agent, Project and Issue resources, combining memberships, grants/scopes, instance administration, Agent trust presets, runtime token scopes, assignment policies, issue visibility/mentions, inbox delegation, legacy privileges and responsible-user intersection.
units.dependencyDirection: The service imports nine persistence tables, shared action/scope/trust types, trust-resolution logic and logging. AccessService and most protected routes call its structured decision API; the engine itself performs many live SQL reads and recursive hierarchy queries, mixing policy evaluation, resource projection, compatibility and telemetry in one application module.
units.keyDataModels: AuthorizationActor/source/key scope/run/onBehalfOf user, action union, typed resource union, allow/deny reason/code/explanation/grant, CompanyMembership, PrincipalPermissionGrant JSON scope, Agent permissions/reporting/trust preset, Project/Issue execution policy, Run context snapshot, Issue comment mention, inbox policy and responsible-user snapshot.
units.lifecycle: Decisions first authenticate and separate board/Agent branches. Board paths may elevate local board or instance admin, use Company membership defaults and grants. Agent paths enforce Company equality, special fail-closed skill-test/task-bridge token scopes, resolve trust and low-trust boundaries, then apply default visibility/write, assignment, self/manager, mention, explicit-grant and legacy rules. An allowed Agent decision is optionally intersected with a cached responsible-user decision when onBehalfOfUserId is present; enforcement can run in shadow mode.
units.testAssessment: The previously audited 2,443-line embedded-Postgres suite is a strong decision-matrix asset, but implementation inspection confirms unsafe compatibility defaults and architectural fragility. local_implicit board and instance admin allow every action immediately. Active non-viewer board membership alone allows runtime:manage, secrets:read and decision management; standard same-Company Agents are unconditionally allowed runtime:manage, secrets:read/secrets:propose and several visibility actions even when their lifecycle is paused/pending/terminated unless an outer layer blocks the credential. Visible Issue writes are default-open. Unknown grant-scope keys are explicitly treated as unconstrained, empty scopes are broad, and JSON scope schemas are not action-specific. Low-trust returns null for unrecognized actions, so adding an action without updating this switch can fall through to later policy. Mention text creates dynamic access. Responsible-user intersection is absent unless the credential carries onBehalfOfUserId, can be disabled by environment shadow mode, accepts any active non-viewer for broad Issue influence/skill carve-outs and uses a global five-second cache that can retain revoked authority and grows without eviction. Decisions are not durably receipted; many resource/hierarchy reads are repeated and full-Company Agent scans occur in scope checks.
units.designRationale: Layer stricter controls onto a historically open collaborative Agent board without breaking installed workflows: preserve local/simple-mode behavior, add explicit grants and token scopes, place low-trust restrictions before defaults, and gradually cap Agent authority with a responsible-user intersection.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires one deny-by-default, versioned and explainable PolicyDecision boundary for humans and Agents, with exact responsibility, action, resource, data, tool, risk, approval, runtime and evidence context; compatibility defaults cannot be the authority model.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a small pure policy kernel plus typed fact resolvers and immutable DecisionReceipt store. ADAPT the structured action/resource/result envelope, hard Company boundary, low-trust precedence, fail-closed limited token profiles, explicit scope tests and Agent ∩ accountable-human concept. Generate an exhaustive action/resource/policy matrix; validate per-permission scope schemas; add deny/expiry/revocation/policy versions, purpose/data/export/tool conditions, separation of duties, exact Work/action digest/approval/evidence and version-fenced facts. Keep legacy migration in an isolated adapter with explicit sunset, never in the policy kernel.
units.responsibilityConflict: Authority can arise from local-board/instance-admin bypasses, simple membership, same-Company Agent visibility, legacy CEO flags or mutable comment mentions instead of an accepted ResponsibilityContract. The accountable-human ceiling is optional, cache-stale and shadowable; an active non-viewer need not be responsible for the exact Work/action/data. Decisions are not bound to immutable organization/policy snapshots or persisted as evidence, so later audits cannot prove why the action was allowed at execution time.

units.function: Paperclip's complete company package export, import, preview and legacy-migration service, including organization, Agent, skill, project, workspace, routine, issue, evidence-like work product, attachment, asset, secret and presentation artifacts.
units.dependencyDirection: A 6,179-line service is a convergence point for database tables, most domain services, storage, secrets, filesystem and Git subprocesses, arbitrary GitHub fetching, provider-specific adapter normalization, route-layer org-chart rendering and package presentation. Serialization, policy, execution admission and mutation do not form separable inward-facing boundaries.
units.keyDataModels: Schema-v6 portable company package, manifest and selected file map, content-addressed blobs and embedded assets, environment input declarations, collision mode and name overrides, import preview/entity plans, company/Agent/skill/project/workspace/routine/issue child records, and a partial import result.
units.lifecycle: Resolve inline/local/GitHub input; normalize and parse a presentation-oriented package; construct export or preview plans; mutate company and consent; materialize secrets and assets; create or replace skills, Agents, permissions, projects, workspaces, routines and issues; flush child evidence records; perform secret-only best-effort compensation on failure.
units.testAssessment: The focused service suite passed 78/78 tests in one file on 2026-08-18, and the separately audited route contract passed 38/38. The batching integration test was explicitly skipped because its embedded PostgreSQL fixture could not start and was not claimed as passed. Coverage locks many useful behaviors, including hash verification, large YAML rendering, safe-mode rejection and paused monitors, but also explicitly locks dangerous semantics such as export-all when a skill selector matches nothing, copied memberships, additive permissions, non-revalidated overrides and authorship loss. It lacks adversarial selector UUID, include.skills=false, normalized-path collision, custom-YAML prototype, bounded-resource, concurrent preview/apply, failure-saga and full rollback/reconciliation tests.
units.designRationale: Offer a human-readable, portable Cloud/self-hosted company bundle with broad entity coverage, backward compatibility, warnings, content-addressed binary data, collision handling and a safer Agent-oriented import mode.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs durable organization portability, but migration is a governed high-risk action that must preserve accountable humans, responsibility contracts, evidence provenance, consent and data-authority semantics across managed-cloud and self-hosted deployments.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a versioned typed manifest with a canonical complete file inventory and digest, explicit per-version migrations, immutable reviewed plan digest, target revision/lease, capability- and data-classification admission, stable error/warning codes, durable saga/outbox checkpoints, resumable repair and compensations, source-principal provenance, re-consent/rebinding workflows and Connector-owned runtime conversion. ADAPT only content rehashing, cross-company asset ownership checks, prebuffered batch writes, blocking-cycle filtering, warnings for dropped references, imported monitors remaining unarmed, inbox suppression and default automation pausing, backed by compatibility fixtures.
units.responsibilityConflict: The importer can synthesize a board actor, copy memberships and prior consent, reattribute human comments to the importer or system, add rather than replace permissions, activate partially imported executable routines, and return no canonical identities/digest for imported issues, documents or evidence. Route-level activity occurs after mutation and cannot prove the complete action/evidence/result chain.
evidence: 2026-08-18 focused verbose Vitest: server/src/__tests__/company-portability.test.ts, 1 file / 78 tests passed
existing COMPLETE application:server/routes/companies-portability contract: 38/38 focused route tests passed; reused without rereading
existing COMPLETE application:server/__tests__/company-import-batching: embedded PostgreSQL fixture failure caused explicit skip; no passing claim
securityFindings: Explicit Agent/project/issue selectors that all miss or are skipped become an empty selection interpreted as export all; UUID issue IDs are misrouted by a hyphen heuristic, so data-minimizing intent can become a full export.

Skill selection has the same empty-means-all behavior, skill export is not consistently guarded by include.skills, and import processes skills whenever Agents or skills are included, leaking or mutating an unrequested domain.

The hand-written tolerant YAML parser permits duplicate last-wins keys, raw object keys and ordinary-object assignment without reserved-key protection; normalized file-path collisions also resolve by silent last-write-wins.

Remote repository files, local Git operations, storage streams, binary decoding, attachments and the complete export/import graph are substantially memory-resident and lack a coherent file/count/aggregate-byte, timeout, host allowlist and snapshot boundary.

Migration can carry executable workspace commands and provider runtime settings, including an injected Codex flag, through heuristic blacklist-based safe modes rather than versioned default-deny capability admission.

Company, consent, assets, skills, Agents, permissions, instruction bundles, projects, workspaces, routines, issues and stored objects are committed through many independent calls. Only newly created secrets receive best-effort cleanup, so failures leave broad partial state without a durable saga or reconciliation record.

Membership, consent, authority and comment authorship are transferred or rewritten without destination-specific human acceptance and source-principal evidence, conflicting with Company OS accountability and data-governance invariants.

units.function: Company-wide interactive search and filter/facet projection over issues, comments, documents, Paperclip artifacts, Agents and projects.
units.dependencyDirection: A 1,340-line service couples shared UI DTOs and routes to PostgreSQL-specific ranking/CTEs/extensions, most search tables, artifact taxonomy/service, extraction service and in-process cross-type merge/pagination.
units.keyDataModels: Search query/scope/sort, heterogeneous result and snippet/highlight, issue summary, artifact summary, type counts, filter facets, zero-result loosen suggestions and internal ranking fields.
units.lifecycle: Normalize/tokenize; construct phrase/token/fuzzy and comment/document match CTEs; materialize visible company issues; UNION results/counts/facets; enrich snippets; concurrently query artifacts/Agents/projects and counts; merge/sort/page in memory; optionally issue many loosen-count queries.
units.testAssessment: The suite is strong on wildcard escaping, ranking and tenant/hidden-record predicates but database cases were skipped on this host. Source proves uncaught gaps: no Principal/data ACL, English-only fuzzy word splitting, independently capped artifact page retrieval, large query fan-out, unvalidated preview-image URLs, Agent lifecycle visibility and no cost-aware admission.
units.designRationale: Deliver one rich command-palette response with ranking, snippets, heterogeneous counts, facets and recovery suggestions while using PostgreSQL indexes and avoiding row-level N+1 queries.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a governed Chinese-first enterprise search plane over organizations, humans, Agents, responsibilities, tasks, approvals, evidence and authorized data, portable across cloud and local deployment profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind SearchQuery/SearchIndex ports with verified Principal and data-policy predicates, neutral typed projections, cursor/snapshot pagination, stable codes, query-cost budgets, Chinese segmentation/pinyin and pluggable local/cloud index adapters. Keep PostgreSQL as one small/self-hosted adapter. ADAPT parameterized LIKE/array helpers, visible/same-company predicates, materialized match-set concept, batch snippet enrichment, deterministic ties and wildcard/tenant regression fixtures.
units.responsibilityConflict: The service can reveal human assignee IDs, Agent capabilities and evidence-derived snippets based solely on companyId. It neither records who searched nor proves result-level authority, data contract, purpose, approval or query/result digest.
evidence: ae7790861811323de7ffcedffa9f56cd88b98bc0 feat(search): add bulk extract endpoint (#9507)

securityFindings: The service accepts companyId/query without a verified Principal, data contract, purpose or row/field-level access predicate.
Preview image URLs are extracted from arbitrary Markdown with a regex and returned without scheme/asset/provenance validation.

Result limits do not bound database work: comment/document pattern scans, MATERIALIZED match sets, facets, fuzzy operations and zero-result count fan-out can be expensive for large tenants or common queries.

Artifact rows are fetched with a lower independent cap than the global offset window, while hasMore is derived from fetched arrays rather than canonical counts; high-offset artifact/cross-type pages can falsely report completion.
All matching Agents are searched without a lifecycle/status visibility condition, potentially exposing terminated or otherwise restricted worker metadata.

units.function: Bulk literal/URL extraction from visible issue titles/descriptions, comments and linked documents with source references and truncation.

units.keyDataModels: Extract source, issue-grouped match, source reference, excerpt, query filters and paged/truncated response.
units.lifecycle: SQL-prefilter visible company issues, page candidates, batch-load matching comments/documents, rescan full text in JavaScript, deduplicate values, create excerpts and return grouped matches.
units.testAssessment: Source and tests show bounded result/match counts, stable updatedAt/id paging and strong same-company joins. Database behavior was skipped on this host. No tests cover provenance loss from deduplication, content/query resource budgets, CJK, ACL/data contracts, unsafe output rendering or concurrent paging.

Deduplication by lowercased value discards subsequent source references, weakening evidence completeness and responsibility provenance.
Original content excerpts and internal issue/assignee/comment/document IDs are returned without classification-aware redaction or an output policy decision.

units.function: Per-company and per-actor sliding-window request limiter for company search.
units.dependencyDirection: A pure service owns a process-local Map and wall-clock function; routes consume its synchronous result, with no database, shared cache, policy or audit dependency.
units.keyDataModels: Actor tuple of companyId/agent-or-board/actorId, an array of hit timestamps per concatenated key, and a structured allowed/limit/remaining/retryAfterSeconds result.
units.lifecycle: Construct one in-memory limiter, derive an actor key, filter timestamps outside the window, deny at the maximum or append the current hit. Keys are never globally expired and all state disappears on restart.
units.testAssessment: The focused route suite passed 3/3 with isolated PAPERCLIP_HOME and approved local TCP listening. It verifies rejection before search invocation, board `me` resolution and invalid route filters, but does not isolate the service or cover cross-tenant/principal keys, colon collisions, expiry cleanup, invalid limits/windows, wall-clock regression, high cardinality, concurrency, multiple instances or fail-open/fail-closed behavior when a shared limiter is unavailable.
units.designRationale: Provide cheap dependency-free abuse protection with predictable headers and a test-injectable clock.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs tenant- and principal-scoped resource governance for search and other data-sensitive or costly capabilities across managed-cloud and clustered/self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind a RateLimitPort using unambiguous structured keys, shared atomic storage for clustered profiles, bounded local fallback for single-node/demo profiles, validated policies, monotonic-safe time semantics, TTL cleanup, capability/query-cost/data-classification dimensions, stable denial codes and observability without leaking query contents. ADAPT the small structured result, injectable clock and focused same-actor behavior test.
units.responsibilityConflict: The actor tuple is only a caller-provided string key; the limiter does not consume a verified Principal, authority/data contract or policy version and produces no evidence that a governed human or Agent exceeded a defined capability budget.
evidence: 2026-08-18 focused verbose Vitest: server/src/__tests__/company-search-rate-limit-routes.test.ts, 1 file / 3 tests passed
securityFindings: Process-local state lets callers multiply their effective quota across replicas and loses all quota state on restart.
Colon-concatenated unescaped IDs create ambiguous keys, so distinct company/actor tuples can collide and interfere with one another.
Unique actor keys are never evicted unless that actor returns, allowing unbounded Map growth under high-cardinality or attacker-controlled identities.
Invalid maxRequests/windowMs values, wall-clock rollback and concurrent/distributed consumption have no defined fail-closed behavior.

units.function: Persisted first-match company Skill policy engine with source normalization, optimistic replacement, reset, legacy permissions and Activity.

Critical semantics—implicit allow, broad legacy fallback, reset ABA, decision/execution race, authority absence and erased historical rules—are directly visible in source and lack countervailing tests.

ADAPT normalization, deterministic matching, CAS transaction and activity-rollback patterns.
units.responsibilityConflict: No-policy allows all eight mutations, legacy create/suggest grants authorize every action, caller-supplied Activity can lie, and reset erases rules. Decisions omit accountable human, approval and action/data/evidence binding.

companion service suite fully read; 7/7 tests skipped on this host
securityFindings: No materialized policy means allow for create/import/install/edit/update/test/reset/remove, including external code supply-chain and destructive actions.
Legacy skills:create or skills:suggest-changes can authorize the entire mutation surface under default deny, far exceeding least privilege.
Policy selectors omit source digest/signature/publisher, executable capabilities, tools, data/egress and responsibility/approval scope.

units.function: Filesystem-derived health projection for newest gzip SQL backup freshness/size and failure-marker state.

units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY. Retain stable warning-code ideas, but health must verify signed metadata/checksum, nonzero/decompressible content, schema/app compatibility, trusted ownership/modes, replicated destination and periodic restore drills using bounded asynchronous inspection.
