units.function: Durable heterogeneous attention queues, source-level visibility filtering, triage versioning/events and data-backed starter-queue materialization.
units.dependencyDirection: Service directly switches across approvals, decisions, interactions, runs, issues, recovery, join and budget tables and calls authorization/activity services.
units.keyDataModels: Queue/item, sourceKind/sourceId, creator/adder/responsible user, triage version and append-only triage event.
units.lifecycle: Resolve source to an authorization resource, create/list/update queues, add/remove references transactionally, serialize triage writes with advisory locks and seed PR/plan/question queues idempotently.
units.testAssessment: Tests exercise primary mutations, source visibility, idempotent seeding and concurrent triage merging. Missing coverage includes high-cardinality performance, deleted-source reconciliation for non-board readers, all attention kinds and source-switch/schema drift. Listing performs per-queue then per-item authorization queries, creating an N+1 scaling path.
units.designRationale: Keep attention organization orthogonal to underlying domain objects while preserving source-specific authorization.
units.companyOsProblem: One Agent Boss desk must project tasks, approvals, failures and data/security alerts without one giant coupled service.
units.companyOsFit: Adopt the sidecar-reference, visibility-before-disclosure, versioned triage and append-event ideas. Replace the central sourceKind switch with registered projection providers and batched authorization; source IDs stay opaque and source lifecycle emits reconciliation events.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId is optional attribution copied at queue mutation time, not the accountable human frozen on the referenced work contract.

units.function: Versioned attention retention, exact reviewed archive manifests, TTL archive, keep/revive controls and durable Agent notification outbox.
units.dependencyDirection: Service consumes attention projections, source authorization, Paperclip source schemas, activity log and a heartbeat notification callback.
units.keyDataModels: Retention/version/archiveVersion, source activity cutoff, archive actor/reason, signed-review manifest entry and notification outbox claim state.
units.lifecycle: Synchronize source activity, increment version on drift, preserve Keep, atomically re-authorize and archive an exact manifest, auto-archive idle entries, claim stale/pending notifications and retry at least once.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests prove TTL archive/revive, Keep exclusion, one notification batch per Agent and all-or-nothing stale-manifest rejection. Gaps include notification backoff/dead-lettering, concurrent worker locking beyond conditional update, retry ceilings, every source origin mapping, manual archive event atomicity and tenant policy overrides.
units.designRationale: Treat attention as a lifecycle-managed projection and make bulk cleanup reviewable rather than silently deleting source data.
units.companyOsProblem: Responsibility/evidence/attention records need explicit lifecycle, legal retention, human-reviewed bulk actions and reliable follow-up.
units.companyOsFit: This is the best Paperclip reference for exact versioned bulk mutation and outbox delivery. Company OS should generalize it to policy-specific retention/legal hold, immutable evidence retention, retry/dead-letter observability and signed actor/action receipts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Archiving hides a projection rather than deleting evidence, which is appropriate, but generic board/source-read authority is not sufficient for evidence retention or legal-hold changes.

units.function: Canonical-JSON HMAC signing for decision specifications plus secure local generation and persistence of an instance signing secret.
units.dependencyDirection: Server crypto/filesystem adapter is called by the Decision service and depends on Paperclip home-path conventions; no neutral signing port exists.
units.keyDataModels: decision-spec-v1 canonical payload, instance-wide 32-byte-or-longer symmetric secret and version-prefixed SHA-256 HMAC.
units.lifecycle: Resolve explicit secret or atomically publish a generated 0600 key under an owned 0700 directory, sign canonical payload and verify with timing-safe comparison.
units.testAssessment: The implementation defends against partial/concurrent local key creation, ownership and permissive modes. It has no key ID, historical verification set, tenant separation, rotation workflow, asymmetric signer/KMS/HSM adapter or algorithm-agility contract.
units.designRationale: Make tampering detectable in zero-config self-hosting without requiring an external key service.
units.companyOsProblem: Action/approval contracts require deployable-profile-neutral signatures, rotation and durable verification after key changes.
units.companyOsFit: Canonicalization, fail-fast key validation and atomic local creation are strong patterns. Company OS should adapt them behind a SignaturePort with kid/algorithm/tenant/purpose, KMS-capable managed adapter and retained verification keys.
units.responsibilityConflict: A valid instance HMAC proves database content was signed by the instance, not which accountable human consented or whether the signed fields cover the full responsibility contract.

units.function: Captures point-in-time Issue/comment/run/workspace/decision snapshots, resolves a likely code commit, persists labeled examples and scrubs snapshots after source-comment deletion.
units.dependencyDirection: Service reads whole Paperclip DB rows across issues, comments, runs, workspaces and three decision systems, then stores untyped JSON snapshots coupled to those schemas.
units.keyDataModels: Snapshot v1 with full issue/comments/runs, cutoff, decision payload/actor/outcome, approximate commit resolution, notes history and retention marker.
units.lifecycle: Resolve decision cutoff, collect rows last updated before it, infer commit, freeze JSON, deduplicate per source/author, update notes history and redact deleted comment bodies.
units.testAssessment: Strong boundary tests cover cutoff inclusivity, exclusion of later comments/runs/workspaces, comment-deletion scrub, issue cascade, commit-resolution label, uniqueness and snapshot immutability. Missing are schema migration, deterministic canonical digest, field allowlisting, secret/PII redaction, evidence/data provenance, concurrent notes CAS and deletion propagation for run/issue fields beyond comments. Full heartbeat-run rows are copied into the training dataset.
units.designRationale: Prevent hindsight leakage by freezing only information believed available at decision time and preserve code context for later learning.
units.companyOsProblem: Training/evaluation datasets need temporal correctness plus data minimization, consent, lineage and reproducibility.
units.companyOsFit: Temporal cutoff, preview-before-freeze, immutable state/editable label and deletion propagation are excellent design references. Reimplement through governed evidence projections and allowlisted snapshot schemas; never copy entire operational rows or infer authorization from temporal availability.
units.responsibilityConflict: The snapshot omits the governing data contract and copies potentially sensitive operational fields. A recursively discovered commit SHA is not evidence that the selected repository state produced the decision.

units.function: Maps decision/retention continuation events onto Paperclip heartbeat wakeup requests and becomes a no-op when that runtime is disabled.
units.dependencyDirection: Thin adapter couples Decision callbacks to heartbeat vocabulary and payloads.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/issue/decision/outcome continuation and batched archive-version notification.
units.lifecycle: At composition time select enabled wakeup or no-op; on event enqueue a typed automation reason and reference-only payload.
units.testAssessment: Two tests cover disabled no-op and exact decision payload mapping. Retention mapping, idempotency, capability negotiation, missing/deleted Agent, delivery receipt and failure classification are not tested here.
units.designRationale: Avoid accepting continuations when the process cannot own heartbeat execution.
units.companyOsProblem: Paused Connector work must resume through a declared capability without embedding vendor sessions or raw human content.
units.companyOsFit: Reference-only payloads and explicit disabled behavior are useful. Company OS needs a Connector Resume port with idempotency/action digest, capability/version check, timeout/cancellation and delivery/result receipts rather than a heartbeat-specific callback.
units.responsibilityConflict: A wakeup references a decision but does not prove the resumed runtime is bound to the same responsibility/action/data contract.

units.function: Signed human-decision engine with target snapshots, typed issue effects, origin/decider authorization intersection, per-effect execution ledger, idempotency, expiry, continuation delivery and crash recovery.
units.dependencyDirection: Application service directly owns Paperclip issue, run, authorization, activity and retention schemas/services; effect types are Paperclip work-item mutations rather than a portable execution contract.
units.keyDataModels: Decision/bundle, signed options and target snapshots, chosen option/input values, effect execution receipt, origin Agent/run/issue, deciding user, continuation marker and archive manifest.
units.lifecycle: Validate origin run and authority, snapshot targets transactionally, sign effect specification, CAS open to decided, re-authorize origin and decider, claim and execute each effect transactionally, persist result/audit, recover running work and deliver Agent continuation at least once.
units.testAssessment: A substantial focused suite covers idempotent creation/decision, tamper rejection, exact archive manifests, lost access, stale targets, double decision, per-effect failure/partial success, crash recovery, continuation and bounded sweeps. Important gaps: the signature includes only decision ID, options and target snapshots—not title/body/inputs/expiry/origin responsible human/responsibility contract/data grants/approval authority/input values/evidence policy. The accountable human is re-read from the mutable run during execution. Effects are sequential rather than an atomic business transaction, failed effects are terminal rather than policy-driven retryable, and recovery reconstructs a generic board actor from membership.
units.designRationale: Turn Agent proposals into bounded, tamper-evident, human-selected issue mutations that survive crashes without executing one effect twice.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a canonical high-risk decision/effect engine that can prove exact human responsibility and safely resume Connector work across cloud/local execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: This is Paperclip's best reference for decision execution and supersedes its generic Approval design. Company OS should adapt signed immutable manifests, authorization intersection, per-effect receipts, staleness policy, CAS and recovery, while owning neutral action/evidence/data contracts and never importing Paperclip schema/types.
units.responsibilityConflict: The signed payload does not freeze the accountable human, approving authority, permissions/data contract, evidence/result obligations or supplied inputs. A later run-row change can alter the origin human shown in audit, so it cannot serve as Company OS's responsibility proof.

units.function: Monolithic Feedback domain/service implementing Vote upsert, Company/global sharing preferences, target validation, local/shared payload snapshots, Issue/Agent/Skill/Instructions context capture, vendor-specific runtime-file reconstruction, trace queries and remote export state transitions.
units.dependencyDirection: The service directly depends on database tables, Agent Instructions, Run Log Store, filesystem/environment paths and Claude/Codex/OpenCode adapter parsers; routes and startup workers call it for both local feedback and external telemetry delivery.
units.keyDataModels: FeedbackVote and FeedbackExport, consent actor/time/terms, local_only/pending/sent/failed, Issue/comment/document target, Company/Agent/Run/cost/skill/instructions snapshots, adapter files, redaction summary, payload/bundle digests and export attempts.
units.lifecycle: Save validates an Agent-authored target, mutates Company and instance sharing state, upserts Vote/Export and builds a DB payload snapshot inside one transaction; flush selects pending/failed rows, reconstructs a fresh bundle from current DB/log/vendor files, uploads sequentially and then marks each row sent or failed.
units.testAssessment: The 1,155-line embedded-Postgres suite gives unusually strong behavior coverage for consent, non-retroactivity, target validity, sanitization examples and delivery states. Implementation-level gaps remain untested: no atomic row claim or multi-replica exclusion; no backoff/next-attempt/max/dead-letter; unscoped getById/getBundle and unbounded list; filesystem work inside the save transaction; unlimited file count and full-file reads before 10M-character truncation; shared global vendor homes; exact session ownership; mutable-source capture between consent and retry; canonical integrity completeness and authorization to change Company/global consent.
units.designRationale: Maximize diagnostic usefulness by automatically reconstructing rich provider-native execution context while keeping non-shared votes local and preserving durable export status.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a neutral DataEgress/Audit pipeline whose consent applies to an exact immutable byte manifest, not a later vendor-specific filesystem scrape.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as separate Feedback, ConsentPolicy, ExportManifest and DataEgressWorker application modules. Connector drivers may propose bounded artifacts through capability contracts, but Core stores an immutable consent-time manifest/digest, field/data-contract decisions and redaction receipt; worker atomically claims it and sends exactly those bytes with idempotency, retry schedule, dead-letter and delivery evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A board vote can change Company and instance-wide sharing state without service-level role authority. Export-time reconstruction reads mutable Run/log/vendor files after consent, so the approved payload and transmitted payload are not the same object. The bundle digest excludes most non-file fields, failure text is stored unsanitized, and shared local-board identity cannot establish an accountable human.

units.function: Deterministic recursive feedback sanitizer for current-user paths, credential-shaped structures/free text, PEM/JWT/provider keys, connection strings, email/phone PII, truncation metadata and SHA-256 digests.
units.dependencyDirection: Arbitrary feedback strings/JSON-like values enter shared structural redaction plus module-local regex patterns; sanitized values, transformation summary and deterministic hashes feed the feedback export bundle.
units.keyDataModels: Redacted/truncated/omitted field sets, notes/counts, regex kind/replacement, deterministic_feedback_v2 summary, canonicalized value and SHA-256 digest.
units.lifecycle: Text first removes current-user data then applies ordered secret/PII patterns and truncates; records pass through generic secret-field sanitization and recurse; summaries sort field/count metadata; stableStringify sorts object keys before hashing.
units.testAssessment: The design records what was transformed and applies defense-in-depth across structured and free text. In this unit there is no dedicated exhaustive test file; coverage is indirect through large feedback-service tests. Regex detection is necessarily incomplete, recursion/arrays are unbounded and cyclic values fail. Non-plain objects such as Buffer pass through, and the custom canonicalizer has undefined/sparse-array/non-finite-number collision or serialization-parity risks.
units.designRationale: Produce useful reproducible diagnostic traces while automatically removing common secrets, local identity and PII and exposing a machine-readable redaction summary.
units.companyOsProblem: Data egress needs deterministic minimization and a reviewable transformation receipt, but enterprise policy cannot rely on regex scrubbing after assembling an unrestricted bundle.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the transformation-summary and ordered deterministic pipeline. Company OS first constructs a typed allowlisted export manifest under DataAuthorization, rejects unknown/non-JSON shapes, enforces depth/count/byte limits, applies pluggable DLP rules and human preview, then hashes RFC-defined canonical bytes and retains source-to-export digest lineage.
units.responsibilityConflict: Heuristic redaction cannot establish authorization, completeness or non-disclosure. A digest over a custom ambiguous canonicalization is not adequate integrity evidence, and a redaction summary must identify policy/version/actor as well as transformations.

units.function: Direct HTTP uploader for feedback trace bundles using a default Paperclip telemetry endpoint, optional plaintext configuration token and gzip/base64 request envelope.
units.dependencyDirection: Server config and shared FeedbackTraceBundle flow directly into global fetch; a remote JSON response supplies or overrides the returned object key.
units.keyDataModels: Backend base URL/token, date-partitioned Company object key, exportedAt, entire trace bundle, encoding marker, bearer header and remote objectKey/error text.
units.lifecycle: Client creation resolves a default endpoint; upload synchronously serializes/compresses the full bundle, posts it without an abort deadline, throws remote text or status on failure and accepts any nonempty response objectKey.
units.testAssessment: Implementation is small and deterministic but lacks protocol/host allowlisting, private-network/redirect defense, timeout/AbortSignal, size limits/streaming, idempotency key/content digest, retry classification, response validation, stable errors and SecretRef handling. A response-lost success can be retried under a different date-derived object key after midnight.
units.designRationale: Keep feedback export deployment-light and decouple server storage from the telemetry service's object layout.
units.companyOsProblem: The data-exit firewall must be the sole canonical owner of outbound enterprise payloads across managed and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind DataEgressPort. Default is disabled/no destination; policy resolves a registered HTTPS sink and short-lived audience secret, blocks private/redirect escapes, streams a bounded immutable manifest, uses digest-bound idempotency, enforces timeout/retry/dead-letter policy and records consent plus delivery receipt.
units.responsibilityConflict: This client can transmit all bundle fields based only on caller behavior and ambient config; it has no Work/data contract, accountable approver, destination policy or field-level export proof. Remote error text may also enter local failure logs as untrusted content.

units.function: Tenant-scoped Routine/Company Skill folder hierarchy service covering canonical path projection, counts, create/update/move/delete, item filing, protected system roots, personal/project folders, bundled categories and cleanup.
units.dependencyDirection: The application service depends directly on Drizzle/PostgreSQL tables, shared transport-shaped input/output types and HTTP error factories; Folder routes and Skill/Routine workflows consume it. It does not belong in a responsibility-domain core.
units.keyDataModels: Folder with opaque UUID, Company, kind, parentId, name/slug/systemKey/color/position and derived path/depth/itemCount; Routine and CompanySkill carry nullable folderId. Database partial unique indexes protect root and sibling slugs plus Company/kind/systemKey, while the self-reference is only parentId and does not enforce matching Company or kind.
units.lifecycle: Most hierarchy mutations acquire a Company-wide PostgreSQL transaction advisory lock, re-read state under that lock, validate reserved roots/cycles/depth/sibling slug, mutate and rebuild derived views. Item moves are tenant-scoped but do not use the hierarchy lock. Folder deletion rejects children and relies on set-null foreign keys for filed items. Ensure helpers repair squatted reserved slugs and idempotently create system containers/children.
units.testAssessment: Behavior is carefully implemented and the embedded-Postgres suite exercises normal CRUD, paths, depth/cycles, system-folder protection, squatting repair and real lock contention. Risks remain: PostgreSQL advisory locks make the implementation database-specific and Company-wide serialization is coarse; DB constraints do not guarantee parent Company/kind; list/path building and repeated isBundledFolder traversal load whole trees without pagination; service methods trust upstream schema validation; moveItem is outside the lock; no service test proves cross-Company isolation, cross-kind parent corruption resistance, deletion/item-move races, rollback behavior or large-tree bounds. Errors are English messages rather than stable codes.
units.designRationale: Keep folders as mutable presentation organization while reserving deterministic roots for bundled, personal and project Skills; compute paths rather than persisting denormalized descendants; serialize hierarchy repair/mutation to make application validations race-safe.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs optional tenant-scoped hierarchical projections for FDE templates, Connector capabilities and office/workspace navigation, but folders must never become the authority for accountable ownership, permissions, evidence or responsibility.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the invariants and tests: opaque IDs, scoped sibling uniqueness, derived paths, non-destructive deletion, protected system nodes, deterministic/idempotent ensure helpers and explicit cycle/depth checks. Re-express behind Company OS storage/transaction ports, add composite tenant/kind parent integrity or deferred constraint validation, stable error codes, bounded traversal and authorization/audit events. Do not copy Paperclip Routine/Skill coupling, PostgreSQL lock key, shared userId systemKey semantics or HTTP errors into Core.
units.responsibilityConflict: A personal folder is keyed directly by an arbitrary userId and system folders encode project/user identity in presentation metadata; neither establishes a HumanPrincipal, accountable owner or authority. Folder mutation has no intrinsic authorization or evidence emission, so treating this hierarchy as an organization/permission tree would bypass Company OS responsibility contracts.

units.function: Process-local, TTL-bound live status projection for a run's phase/message/tool/assistant snippet with heuristic secret redaction.
units.dependencyDirection: In-memory server adapter depends on Paperclip redaction and shared phase enum; UI readers query it through surrounding Heartbeat APIs.
units.keyDataModels: Company/issue/Agent/run scope, phase, sanitized message/tool/snippet and activity timestamps.
units.lifecycle: Set or touch a scoped Map entry, clone on read, reject scope mismatch and clear/sweep after 90 seconds.
units.testAssessment: Six tests cover scoping, redaction/truncation, expiry, touch monotonicity/fallback and sweep. No multi-process consistency, process restart, capacity/eviction, Unicode size, redaction bypass or authorization-call-site test exists.
units.designRationale: Give responsive live UI feedback without turning noisy transient status into durable database state.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss and office entities need transient working/waiting state while durable evidence remains separate.
units.companyOsFit: The ephemeral-versus-durable split, TTL and scope checks are useful. Company OS should expose an Office/Run Projection port with managed-cloud pub/sub or local memory adapter, bounded capacity and typed safe status codes rather than arbitrary Agent text.
units.responsibilityConflict: Sanitized snippets are not evidence and must not enter the responsibility chain; heuristic redaction is defense-in-depth only.

units.function: Extracts/truncates selected adapter result fields, merges a fallback summary and chooses text to post as an Issue comment.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure server helper accepts untyped vendor result JSON; Heartbeat persistence/comment paths call it.
units.keyDataModels: summary/result/message/error, three cost aliases and timeout/stop metadata.
units.lifecycle: Merge missing summary, project allowlisted top-level fields and select summary/result/message for a comment.
units.testAssessment: Eight tests cover truncation, alias preservation, irrelevant payloads, fallback order and merge precedence. The helper does not redact text, validate numeric cost types, attach currency/provider/model/token dimensions, preserve an evidence digest or bound the full issue-comment length; safe JSON byte constants are defined but not enforced inside this module.
units.designRationale: Keep live/list responses and issue comments useful without returning entire provider payloads.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector outputs need safe structured projection while raw evidence stays governed and immutable.
units.companyOsFit: Reference the projection-before-display idea only. Company OS requires a versioned Result envelope, typed usage/cost, sensitivity labels, evidence digest and separate localized presentation mapper.
units.responsibilityConflict: Free-form adapter summary posted as a durable work comment can be mistaken for verified result evidence and may contain sensitive content unless every caller redacts correctly.

units.function: Infers normalized run stop reason and timeout metadata from adapter type/config, outcome, error code and English error message.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure helper embeds Paperclip adapter names/config keys and is called from Heartbeat finalization.
units.keyDataModels: Outcome, stop reason, effective timeout, configured/source/fired flags.
units.lifecycle: Read timeoutMs/timeoutSec with adapter-specific defaults, infer reason, then merge metadata into result JSON.
units.testAssessment: Seven tests cover local defaults, configured timeout, budget/manual cancellation, graceful interruption, max-turn normalization, inconsistent success and merge. Critical gaps: local coding adapters default to unlimited timeout; budget/paused cancellation is inferred from English message substrings; invalid/negative config silently becomes zero; no Connector-declared reason/version is required.
units.designRationale: Normalize heterogeneous adapters enough for UI/diagnostics without changing every adapter result.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector-neutral execution needs authoritative, stable terminal reasons and bounded timeout policy.
units.companyOsFit: Do not reuse. Company OS Connector SDK must emit typed terminal reason/error code and negotiated timeout/cancellation semantics; deployment/risk policy supplies bounded defaults and invalid values fail closed.
units.responsibilityConflict: Misclassifying a manual cancellation as budget pause changes organizational meaning, and an unlimited default can leave delegated authority running indefinitely.

units.function: Many-to-many association service between issues and generic approvals with same-company validation.
units.dependencyDirection: Thin DB service couples Paperclip issue and approval schemas; routes decide who may add or remove links.
units.keyDataModels: Composite issueId/approvalId link plus duplicated companyId.
units.lifecycle: Validate both records share a company, insert idempotently, list either direction or delete the link at any approval status.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover tenant validation, idempotent link creation and deletion. No immutability/status rule prevents post-decision relinking, and no digest or revision records the association used when a human decided.
units.designRationale: Allow one approval to be surfaced from several related work items without embedding arrays in either row.
units.companyOsProblem: Responsibility projection needs immutable, versioned links from an approval receipt to exact work/action/evidence objects.
units.companyOsFit: Same-tenant foreign-key validation is worth retaining conceptually, but Company OS should create append-only responsibility edges inside the proposal transaction and supersede them only through a new contract revision.
units.responsibilityConflict: Post-resolution mutation can change what the audit trail appears to say was approved.

units.function: Best-effort helper that wakes an assigned non-backlog Agent with issue/task references after assignment-related mutations.
units.dependencyDirection: Issue routes inject the large Heartbeat service; helper knows its source/reason/context vocabulary.
units.keyDataModels: Issue ID/assignee/status, mutation/reason, task key and requester attribution.
units.lifecycle: Skip unassigned/backlog, enqueue assignment wake, swallow/log failure unless explicitly configured to rethrow.
units.testAssessment: No focused test belongs to this unit. Call sites mostly mock it, leaving exact idempotency, responsibility resolution, status races and failure policy unproven.
units.designRationale: Centralize repeated issue-assignment wake payload construction and avoid making ordinary mutations fail on transient scheduler errors.
units.companyOsProblem: Work assignment must reliably dispatch once and preserve initiator/responsible-human/action-contract context.
units.companyOsFit: Do not reuse the fire-and-forget helper. Company OS should persist a transactional dispatch outbox with idempotency/action digest and let a delivery worker call AgentExecutionPort.
units.responsibilityConflict: Wake payload contains attribution but no responsibility contract or exact permission/data grant; swallowed failure can leave assigned work silently undispatched.

units.function: Builds dependency-resolution wake idempotency keys and queries for existing wake requests in selected states.
units.dependencyDirection: Thin DB helper depends directly on the Heartbeat wakeup table; actual dependency transition and enqueue behavior lives in Issue routes/services.
units.keyDataModels: Dependent/blocker IDs, company-scoped idempotency key and wake status.
units.lifecycle: Derive deterministic key, query one existing non-skipped wake for one or several legacy/current keys.
units.testAssessment: No focused unit test exists; route integration covers three dependency/child-terminal scenarios. The schema has no general unique constraint for this idempotency-key family, so check-then-insert can race; 'claimed' is omitted from one related liveness idempotency set and status sets vary across helpers.
units.designRationale: Avoid duplicate Agent wakes when several blocker/parent transitions converge.
units.companyOsProblem: Event-driven work dependencies require atomic deduplication and replay-safe dispatch.
units.companyOsFit: Deterministic causal keys are useful, but Company OS must enforce uniqueness at the dispatch store and compare command digest, not rely on preflight reads with scattered status lists.
units.responsibilityConflict: Deduplicating by issue IDs does not prove the wake uses the same responsible human, work revision or execution authorization.

units.function: Pure create/update resolver that stores only the selected Goal ID and heuristically distinguishes explicit assignments from inherited fallback assignments.
units.dependencyDirection: Issue service supplies current/requested identifiers and already-resolved Project/Company fallbacks; the helper has no database or authorization dependency and returns a nullable string.
units.keyDataModels: MaybeId inputs and one Goal ID without assignment-origin, actor, policy version or effective time.
units.lifecycle: Create applies explicit/Project/Company precedence; update computes current and next fallback, substitutes next fallback for missing or fallback-equal current values and otherwise keeps the current Goal.
units.testAssessment: The implementation is readable and deterministic, but its representation cannot distinguish explicit-equal-to-fallback from inherited state. Passing goalId:null requests fallback rather than a durable explicit-none state, and the helper cannot validate tenant ownership, Goal lifecycle or policy version.
units.designRationale: Achieve automatic Goal inheritance and legacy backfill with a small stateless helper and no schema migration for assignment metadata.
units.companyOsProblem: Responsibility chains require goal assignment intent and provenance to survive policy, Project and organization-template changes.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT with a GoalAssignment aggregate/value object: goalId or explicit-none, origin enum, source Project/template/policy version, assignedBy Principal, assignedAt and replacement reason. Recalculation becomes an explicit command/event rather than an ID-equality heuristic.
units.responsibilityConflict: The algorithm can overwrite a human's explicit intent and cannot answer who assigned the Goal or why it changed. This directly conflicts with Company OS's accountable-human and responsibility-record requirements.

units.function: Persistence service for one active recovery action per company/source issue. It exposes active lookups, source-scoped upsert with attempt accumulation, and guarded terminal resolution, while preserving recovery owner, return owner, cause, fingerprint, evidence, wake/monitor policy and outcome.
units.dependencyDirection: The service imports shared recovery types but is implemented directly against the Paperclip Drizzle database and issue_recovery_actions table. An in-process promise queue serializes upserts per company/source issue; PostgreSQL partial unique indexes are the cross-process correctness backstop.
units.keyDataModels: IssueRecoveryAction with sourceIssueId, optional recoveryIssueId, kind, active/escalated/resolved/cancelled status, ownerType, ownerAgentId/ownerUserId, previous and return Agent owners, free-form cause/fingerprint/evidence/nextAction, wakePolicy, monitorPolicy, attempts, timeout, outcome and resolution note.
units.lifecycle: Read the current active or escalated action; update it and increment attempts when present; otherwise insert; retry up to three times on compare-and-update loss or the two named PostgreSQL uniqueness conflicts. Resolution updates every matching active row selected by company/source plus optional action/kind/cause/fingerprint filters.
units.testAssessment: A focused fake-DB race test proves that an action resolved after the initial read is not reactivated. The 2,110-line embedded-Postgres/API suite exercises source and tenant scoping, repeated upsert, typed fingerprint dedupe, no nested recovery, active projections, wake payloads, hand-back, stale folding, peer-Agent rejection, named-owner resolution, blockers, false positives, provider quota and recovery cause routing. Gaps remain for two-process races, crash/fault injection, retries exhausted, malformed JSON evidence/policies, human owner semantics, delete/retention, outbox atomicity and property-based state transitions.
units.designRationale: Model recovery as a durable first-class action attached to the original work instead of recursively creating recovery work, and make active uniqueness survive process concurrency through database constraints.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs first-class, source-scoped incidents/recovery cases with stable identity, bounded attempts, exact responsible human, executor, permission/data/approval contract digests, evidence references and a durable resolution receipt.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the partial-unique active case, compare-and-update anti-reactivation guard, typed cause/fingerprint, attempt history and explicit return-owner concept. Implement a Company OS RecoveryCase aggregate and store port with optimistic versioning/outbox; use opaque Principal IDs for human and Agent owners, append-only attempts and typed policies rather than Paperclip table rows and free-form JSON.
units.responsibilityConflict: The default owner is an Agent or an abstract board, ownerUserId is not part of the default selection rule, and previous/return ownership is Agent-only. A named Agent may resolve board-owned work. The record does not bind an accountable human, authority scope, data contract, approval digest or immutable evidence manifest; updating the same row also overwrites earlier evidence and policy.

units.function: Static manifest feature and worker-to-host operation capability checker using a central string-to-string requirement map, UI/launcher maps and fail-closed unknown-operation behavior.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on shared manifest/capability/UI types plus server errors/logger; Loader calls install consistency checks and host bridges are expected to call runtime assertions.
units.keyDataModels: PluginCapability strings, operation names, manifest-declared capability set and allowed/missing check result.
units.lifecycle: Checks feature declarations at install, tests declared strings on each operation, rejects unknown operations or missing capabilities and reports human-readable denial messages.
units.testAssessment: Six environment/external-object seam cases passed. They cover selected schema refinements and operation mappings but not exhaustive map/schema/handler parity, excessive grants, unknown-operation API ambiguity, upgrade/removal, scoped grants or denial evidence.
units.designRationale: Make plugin least-privilege intent declarative and centrally auditable while rejecting new host operations until explicitly mapped.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs declared Connector capabilities separated from administrator-approved grants and runtime leases, all narrowed by organization, resource, data purpose/destination, risk, time and Responsibility contract.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the central fail-closed operation registry and feature-consistency tests. Rebuild as CapabilityDeclaration plus ApprovedGrant plus short-lived InvocationAuthority, generate map parity tests from one contract source and emit stable decision codes/evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A manifest string is treated as authority; one environment capability grants the full lifecycle and raw provider-key access. There is no accountable approver, exact package digest, company/resource scope, high-risk action binding, purpose, expiry or evidence chain.

units.function: Plugin database namespace and migration service with regex-based SQL policy, checksum ledger, advisory locking and restricted runtime query/execute facades over the shared database client.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends directly on filesystem SQL, Drizzle raw SQL, central plugin/migration tables and the plugin manifest's database declaration; worker host services call the runtime methods.
units.keyDataModels: Derived schema namespace, coreReadTables allowlist, migration key/checksum/version/status/error and parameterized runtime SQL/result rows.
units.lifecycle: Creates a schema, records its namespace, locks by plugin, validates and applies sorted SQL files transactionally, rejects checksum mutation, then validates and executes worker SQL through the server database role.
units.testAssessment: Nine pure SQL/environment cases passed and eight embedded-database cases skipped. Positive transaction/checksum tests are valuable, but the suite lacks an adversarial SQL corpus, database-role/RLS proof, tenant predicate enforcement, resource limits, symlink and migration-order attacks.
units.designRationale: Give plugins useful relational storage and controlled core joins without granting unrestricted public-schema writes, while keeping migrations idempotent and serialized.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Connector data storage isolated by installation and company, with database-enforced least privilege, governed data-source contracts, bounded query execution and reversible/exportable lifecycle.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE deterministic namespace derivation, checksums, advisory locking and install-transaction rollback. Replace regex-only policy with parsed restricted queries or a typed data API plus separate least-privilege roles/RLS, mandatory company scope, budgets/cancellation and explicit migration/retention contracts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Unqualified relations and side-effectful SELECT functions can escape lexical checks; whitelisted public tables expose all companies without predicate enforcement; mutable manifests can broaden access; all SQL uses the shared server role and produces no per-query Responsibility/DataAuthorization evidence.

units.function: Small controller mapping lifecycle stop/unload and worker crash events to per-plugin HostServices disposer callbacks.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends only on lifecycle event subscription and a mutable pluginId-to-disposer Map; application wiring owns registration and replacement.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin worker crash/restart event, lifecycle stopped/unloaded payload and synchronous disposer registry.
units.lifecycle: Registers listeners, disposes on stop/crash, removes on unload, can dispose all and can detach listeners.
units.testAssessment: No focused tests were found. Throwing/async disposers, restart replacement, duplicate registration, teardown order and lifecycle path coverage are unverified.
units.designRationale: Avoid leaked event/session subscriptions across worker crashes and unloads without coupling HostServices to the lifecycle manager.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a durable runtime supervisor whose cancellation and cleanup convergence can be awaited, retried and observed across crashes and deployments.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE event-to-resource cleanup ownership, but implement async all-settled disposal with timeout, idempotency, generation fencing, restart replacement, failure evidence and focused lifecycle tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: Best-effort synchronous callbacks can silently leave resources active after a state change, and no evidence shows which actions, credentials, subscriptions or data leases were actually revoked.
evidence: no focused test found by repository search

units.function: A 3398-line worker-to-host implementation exposing configuration, filesystem, state, SQL, entities, events, HTTP, Secrets, telemetry, organization/task data, approvals, Agents, Goals, access administration, authorization policy and Agent sessions.
units.dependencyDirection: Directly composes most server domain services, database tables, storage, networking, telemetry, worker/event infrastructure and plugin SDK types; capability enforcement lives outside this object in a separate dispatcher.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Agent/Project/Issue/Goal/Approval, human/agent actor IDs, plugin/company state, SQL, Secret refs, invite/grant/policy, attachment bytes, Agent session/live events and operational telemetry.
units.lifecycle: Builds one instance-wide plugin facade, accepts company/resource/actor parameters from worker calls, performs reads and high-impact mutations, records plugin activity, forwards events, buffers logs and disposes subscriptions best-effort.
units.testAssessment: The five focused access/authorization cases all skipped locally. Other separate tests cover spans and scoped routing, but this unit lacks a complete operation-by-operation capability/tenant/actor/data matrix and adversarial SSRF, resource-limit, impersonation, session-isolation and failure-recovery proof.
units.designRationale: Give plugin authors a rich typed SDK while reusing core services, preserving company equality checks and adding targeted safety helpers such as DNS pinning, redaction and provider-span clamping.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs narrow ports whose authority is host-minted per invocation from authenticated principal, approved Connector grant, Responsibility contract and DataAuthorization, with every mutation/effect producing durable evidence.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT the monolithic facade and caller-supplied authority model. Selectively reference provider-span clamping, DNS pinning, non-oracle tenant responses and active-membership checks as defense-in-depth; split Company OS interfaces by capability and require a non-forgeable InvocationAuthority object that services cannot bypass.
units.responsibilityConflict: A plugin can name an eligible human and have approvals/comments/interactions attributed to them without proof of intent; plugins are instance-wide with no company grant; high-risk access/policy/Agent actions lack exact human approval; entity/SQL/state/session paths have cross-tenant or wildcard hazards and data egress is not purpose-bound.

units.function: Install-source path guard that canonicalizes local directories and restricts cloud-managed installs to real paths strictly beneath the bundled plugin catalog.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on filesystem realpath/stat, path-relative containment, the Loader's bundled-root constant and cloud-instance environment detection; the plugin route must invoke it in the correct sequence.
units.keyDataModels: Managed-instance boolean and a success/failure canonical-path result with human-readable reason.
units.lifecycle: Rejects null/missing/non-directory paths, resolves symlinks and traversal, canonicalizes the catalog root and decides segment-based containment before Loader invocation.
units.testAssessment: All fifteen pure guard cases passed. They cover core canonicalization and containment well but omit TOCTOU/content mutation, nested symlinks/entrypoints, immutable digests, platform mount/case behavior and route sequencing.
units.designRationale: Treat plugin installation as an RCE boundary on managed infrastructure and fail closed based on an unforgeable deployment-harness environment marker.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs deployment-profile install policy plus a content-addressed trust decision that remains valid through verification, migration and execution on managed or customer-owned nodes.

units.function: Compatibility/backfill helper that creates missing Agent Company memberships and derives missing human permission grants from legacy membership roles; the same default-grant helper is also called during authentication, first-admin claim, Company import and test setup.

Per-human helper calls repeat the additive grant insertion at login/claim/import without deleting or reconciling obsolete grants.
units.testAssessment: The previously audited Access integration tests prove two-run idempotency, preservation of an existing scoped grant and exclusion of pending/terminated Agents. They do not prove bounded startup behavior, concurrent startup, partial failure/restart across the two phases, role-demotion removal, policy-version migration, unsupported/unknown roles, Agent membership status synchronization after lifecycle changes or audit provenance. The implementation performs an unpaginated instance-wide Agent scan, an unpaginated active-human scan and one insert per human, producing an N+1 startup path. Additive on-conflict behavior cannot revoke grants removed from a later role policy, so stale privilege can survive indefinitely.

Company OS should implement a versioned migration job with checkpoints, pagination, policy version/source metadata, dry-run/diff, explicit grant reconciliation (add and revoke), immutable migration evidence and lifecycle-derived Agent membership projection. Runtime login and normal authorization must not depend on a compatibility module mutating policy state.
units.responsibilityConflict: Every non-terminal Agent becomes an active Company member without a responsibility contract or accountable-human binding. Human grants are inferred from a mutable display role and inserted with null grantor; obsolete grants are never revoked when role policy narrows. This creates authority without a contemporaneous accountable decision and makes the effective permission set diverge from stated organizational responsibility.

Idempotency is select-then-insert without a shown conflict replay path. Invocation and ActionRequest inserts are not transactional, nor are decision/rate consumption/invocation/audit; partial states and consumed quota are possible. units.testAssessment: The previously audited 82-line suite proves tamper detection, Invocation/tool binding, dedicated-key requirement, basic redaction and one prompt-injection block. Implementation review finds untested semantic and robustness gaps: sensitiveMode=redact only transforms plain objects; strings and arrays are returned unchanged even when the summary detects/redacts a Secret. promptInjectionMode=redact records findings but does not redact or quarantine the content. Signed blobs and nested payloads are decoded/parsed before verification with no byte/depth limit. Canonicalization has no explicit handling for undefined, bigint, cyclic/non-JSON values, Unicode normalization or numeric edge cases. HMAC envelope lacks key ID/rotation, issued/expiry time, nonce/replay scope, Company/Work/Agent/Connector/action/policy/data binding and result signature. Shared symmetric instance key gives no execution-node identity. Heuristic regex scanning is bypassable and false-positive prone.

Use a standard canonical JSON/CBOR profile with strict input limits; bind Company/Work/ResponsibilityContract/Agent/Connector/tool+schema version/action digest/permissions/data contract/approval/policy version/nonce/iat/exp; support key IDs and rotation or node public-key signatures; verify before expensive decode where possible; sign Result/Evidence.
